### Verse 72

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 7:72:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/7:72:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/7:72:1)


**ביום עשתי עשר יום.** כבר בארתי בספר מאזנים למה השתנה זה המספר וטעם **עשתי.** כמו עשתנותיו מה שיולידו מחשבותיו כאילו העשר הוליד והוא סוד גדול. ויאמר רבי יונה הספרדי כי פירושו על שתי עשר והטעם החשבון שהוא קודם ממנו והנה טעה שתי טעיות גדולות. האחד כי חשבון שנים עשר הוא על אחד עשר הפך דבורו והעד הנאמן מבן עשרים שנה ומעלה. והטעות השנית כי אילו היה על שתי היה ראוי שיאמר עשני עשר ולא עשתי עשר כי עשתי לשון נקבה רק עשתי מלה אחת:


ON THE ELEVENTH DAY. I have already explained in my work *moznayim* why this number³⁷ (eleven). differs [from the other numbers].³⁸ (2) *asar*; 13, *sheloshah* (3) *asar* (10); etc. However, the word for eleven in our verse is *ashte asar* and not *ahad* (1) *asar* (10). The word *ashte* in (*ashte asar*, eleven) is similar to the word *eshtonotav* (his thoughts) (Ps. 146:4). It (*ashte*) refers to that which a person’s thoughts give birth to. The number ten, as it were begets [eleven, etc.]. This is a great secret.³⁹, p. 163). Rabbi Jonah the Sephardi⁴⁰ says that *ashte asar* is short for *al shete asar*. Its meaning is, the number that precedes twelve.⁴¹ means eleven. Now Rabbi Jonah made two great mistakes. One, contrary to his words, the number twelve is beyond (*al*) the number eleven.⁴² means above, not before. Hence if *ashte asar* is short for *al shetem asar*, then its meaning is, not before 12 but beyond 12. *From twenty years old and upward* (va-ma’alah) (Num. 1:3) is proof of the aforementioned.⁴³ and *al* come from the same root. We thus see that *al* means upward or beyond, not before. His second mistake is that if the word *ashte* is short for *al shete*, then the text should have read *ashne asar*,⁴⁴. not *ashte asar*. For *ashte* is in the feminine.⁴⁵ is short for *shetem asar*. *Shetem asar* is feminine. Now *yom* is masculine. Why would Scripture employ a feminine? *Ashte* is therefore one word.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/7:89:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/7:89:1)


וטעם **ובבא משה.** יתכן שתחלת הדבור שהוא ויקרא אל משה היה כאשר נשלמה החנוכה וכל המדקדקים אמרו כי מדבר אליו מבנין התפעל והתי"ו מובלע ולפי דעתי שהוא שם הפועל כמו הנה לא ידעתי דבר והמ"ם תחת מן למשפט הלשון:


[AND WHEN MOSES WENT IN.] It is likely that the beginning of God’s word to Moses [in the tabernacle], which is what *And the Lord called unto Moses* (Lev. 1:1) refers to, was uttered when the dedication of the tabernacle was completed. All the grammarians say that the word *middabber* (speaking) in *speaking unto him* is a *hitpa’el*⁴⁶ with the *tav* swallowed.⁴⁷. In other words, *middabber* is short for *mitdabber*. However, in my opinion *middadbber* is an infinitive. It is similar to the word *dabber* (speak)⁴⁸ in *behold, I cannot speak* (Jer. 1:5). The *mem* prefixed to *middabber* is in place of the word *min*, as is the rule in the Hebrew language.⁴⁹ placed in front of a word has the meaning of from. I.E. renders *va-yishma et ha-kol middabber elav* (then he heard the voice speaking unto him) as, then he heard the voice of the One who spoke to him.

footnotes:
⁴⁶ So too Rashi.
⁴⁷ By the dallet
⁴⁸ Which is an infinitive.
⁴⁹ A mem


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 7:89:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/7:89:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/7:89:2)


וטעם **וישמע.** שהוא לבדו היה שומע הקול ולא ישמענו מי שהוא באהל מועד מחוץ לפרוכת גם זה נכון כי השם הוסיף בהרגשת אזניו כאשר הוסיף באור עיני נער אלישע וכן ויגל ה' את עיני בלעם:


The meaning of *va-yishma* (then he heard) is that only Moses heard the voice. Anyone in the tent of meeting outside of the curtain did not hear the voice. The following is also correct: God made Moses’ ear supersensitive⁵⁰ as he added to the sight of Elisha’s young man (II Kings 6:17). Similarly *Then the Lord opened the eyes of Balaam* (Num. 22:31).⁵¹

footnotes:
⁵⁰ So that Moses heard what others did not
⁵¹ Which, according to I.E., means God made his eyes more sensitive than the eyes of other people.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 8:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/8:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/8:2:2)


**אל מול פני המנורה.** פירוש והאיר אל עבר פניה והנה מלת האיר יוצאה כמו תאיר נרי ואין כן יאירו והארץ האירה ונסמכה זאת הפרשה להורות כי הדבור יהיה גם בלילה כי שם יהיה הנר דלוק ולא יכבה:


IN FRONT OF THE CANDLESTICK. This explains *to give light* (he’ir) *over against it* (Ex. 25:37).² is, shall give light in front of the candlestick. Now the word *he’ir* (give light)³ is transitive. It is similar to the word *ta’ir* (dost light) in *For Thou dost light my light* (Ps. 18:29). However, this is not the case with the word *ya’iru* (shall give light)⁴ (shall give light) is intransitive and means shall shine, not shall shine upon. I.E. renders our clause, *shall shine in front of the candlestick*. and the word *he’irah* (did shine) in *and the earth did shine* (Ezek. 43:2). This section⁵ follows⁶ in order to teach that God’s word also came at night, for the light was to burn in the tabernacle and was not to be extinguished.

**תקח לחטאת.** בציווי כי הם יקחו והטעם יתנו כמו ויקחו לי תרומה או יקחו עמם כמו ויקחו להם איש שה לבית אבות:

The meaning of *Then let them take* (ve-lakechu) is, then let them give.³² means shalt thou offer. Compare, *ve-yikechu li terumah* (that they take for Me an offering).³³) to Me an offering. ###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 8:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/8:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/8:16:1)


**כי נתונים נתונים.** הם ובניהם ישראל נתנום לי ואני לקחתי אותם לי והטעם קבלתים ולא נתנום בעבור פדיון פטרת כל רחם. ופטרת ופטר שתי לשונות כמו צדקה וצדק או על משקל אחר:


FOR THEY ARE WHOLLY GIVEN UNTO ME. They, and their children, are given unto Me.⁴⁰ (for they are wholly given unto Me). I.E. believes that the first *netunim* refers to the Levites and the second to the children of the Levites. The Israelites gave them to Me⁴¹ *and I took them unto Me*;⁴². that is, I accepted them. Why are they given [unto Me]?⁴³. 38. The printed texts apparently read, they are not given (unto me). This is an obvious error. In order to redeem all that openeth the womb. The word *pitrat* (openeth) and *peter* (openeth)⁴⁴ (that openeth the womb). The Book of Exodus refers to the first-born as *peter…rechem* (openeth the womb) (Ex. 13:2). are two different words.⁴⁵ Compare, *tzedek* (righteousness) and *tzedakah* (righteousness).⁴⁶ refers to any act of righteousness. *Tzedakah* in rabbinic literature refers to a gift of charity. Or they might be the same word in two paradigms.⁴⁷ and *pitrat*.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 9:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/9:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/9:19:1)

AND WHEN THE CLOUD TARRIED. The meaning of *u- ve-ha’arikh* (and when it tarried) is to be rendered, and if it tarried.¹⁰ Scripture first speaks in general terms.¹¹ It then goes on to say that sometimes the Israelites would journey for a few days or encamp according to the commandment of the Lord.

### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 9:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/9:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/9:21:1)


**או יומם ולילה.** הנה פעמים יסעו בלילה ויש אומרים כי פירושו יומם ולילה כמשמעו והוא הנכון בעיני והעד או יומם:


OR IF IT CONTINUED BY DAY AND BY NIGHT. They thus occasionally journeyed at night.¹² (by day and by night) is to be rendered, by day *or* by night. Our verse reads as follows: or if it (the cloud) continued by day or by night, when the cloud was taken up they journeyed. In other words, sometimes the cloud stayed over the tabernacle during the day and was taken up at the beginning of the night. Thus Israel at times took up their journey at night. Others say that *yomam va-laylah* (by day and by night) is to be interpreted literally.¹³ of *yomam va-laylah* is to be translated literally. Thus *yomam va-laylah* means by day *and* by night. Therefore what the verse is telling us is that the cloud continued on the tabernacle a day and a night and was taken up in the morning, and then Israel journeyed. The verse thus teaches that Israel journeyed in the morning, not at night. This interpretation appears correct to me. The term *yomayim* (two days) (v. 22)¹⁴. 38. See also Filwarg. The printed texts have *yomam*. is proof that this interpretation is correct.¹⁵ follows *yomam va-laylah*. *Yomayim* refers to two days and two nights. Hence *yomam va-laylah* must refer to a day and a night.

¹³ In other words, the vav
¹⁴ So Vat. Ebr
¹⁵ The term yomayim

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 10:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:6:1)

### Verse 29

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 10:29:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:29:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:29:1)


מצאנו שצפורה היא בת רעואל כי כן כתוב ויתן את צפרה בתו ועוד להשקות צאן אביהן אל רעואל אביהן והנה חובב הוא בן רעואל והנה הוא אחי צפורה ולפי שקול הדעת הוא יתרו בעבור חנותנו במדבר ואמר על דבר יתרו כאשר בא אל המדבר אשר הוא חנה שם ואם יטעון טוען כי הכתוב אמר על יתרו חותן משה יש להשיב כי דרך המקרא לקרוא אבי הנערה ואחיה חותן והעד לחובב בן רעואל המדיני חותן משה וכבר נתברר שחובב אחי צפורה וקראו חותן משה ואם אמר אין חותן משה דבק עם חובב רק עם רעואל התשובה מבני חובב חותן משה ורבים אמרו שחובב הוא יתרו והוא אבי צפורה ורעואל היה זקנה ואמר הכתוב אל רעואל אביהן כאשר אמר יעקב אלהי אבי אברהם ואמר הכתוב בתו כאשר אמר על בלשצר שהוא בן נבוכדנצר והוא בן בנו וחכמינו אמרו שבעה שמות היו לו ליתרו ושבעים פנים לתורה:


[29. AND MOSES SAID UNTO HOBAB, THE SON OF REUEL.] We find Scripture telling us that Zipporah was the daughter of Reuel, for it is written, *and he* [Reuel] *gave Moses Zipporah his daughter* (Ex. 2:21). Furthermore, Scripture states, *to water their father’s flock*³² (Ex. 2:16), *and to Reuel their*³³ *father* (Ex. 2:18). Now Hobab was the son of Reuel.³⁴ Thus Hobab³⁵ was the brother of Zipporah.³⁶ According to a rational analysis of Scripture, Hobab is to be identified with Jethro, because the Torah states, *as thou* [Hobab] *knowest how we are to encamp in the wilderness* (v. 31) and it states with regard to Jethro when he came to the wilderness, *into the wilderness where he was encamped* (Ex. 18:5). Should one disagree³⁷ and argue that Scripture refers to Jethro as *choten mosheh* (Moses’ father-in-law) (Ex. 18:1), then one can respond that it is the way of Scripture to refer to the father and the brother of a young woman by the term *choten* (father-in-law).³⁸ means a father or brother-in-law. *Unto Hobab, the son of Reuel…choten mosheh* (Moses’ father-in-law)³⁹ is proof of the aforementioned. For it has already been made clear to you that Hobab was the brother of Zipporah, and Scripture calls him *choten mosheh* (Moses’ father-in-law). Should one argue that *choten mosheh* (Moses’ father-in-law) is not connected to Hobab but to Reuel, then the response is, Scripture explicitly states *Hobab choten mosheh* (the father-in-law of Moses) (Jud. 4:11). Many say that Hobab and Jethro are one and the same. They maintain that Jethro/Hobab was the father of Zipporah and that Reuel was the grandfather of Zipporah. They argue that Scripture says, *to Reuel their father* (Ex. 2:18)⁴⁰ in the same manner that Jacob said, *O God of my father Abraham* (Gen. 32:10).⁴¹ Scripture similarly refers to Zipporah as Reuel’s daughter in the same manner that it refers to Belshazzar as Nebuchadnezzar’s son,⁴² when in fact he was Nebuchadnezzar’s grandson. Our sages say that Jethro had seven names.⁴³ 1. There are seventy faces to the Torah.⁴⁴, a late aggadic Midrash on the alphabet composed sometime between 700-900 C.E. Some manuscripts read, there are seven faces to the Torah. According to the rabbis, Jethro, Hobab, and Reuel are one and the same person (see Rashi on Ex. 18:1 where he quotes all seven names). Hence I.E.’s comment.

³⁷ With the identification of Hobab with Jethro.

³⁹ Our verse.
⁴⁰ The father of Zipporah and her sister.
⁴¹ Isaac, not Abraham, was Jacob’s father. Thus father is used for grandfather. Similarly, in Ex. 2:18 father refers to grandfather.

### Verse 33

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 10:33:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:33:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:33:1)


לפי דעתי שהמסע הראשון לבדו לא היה כשאר המסעות והפסוק שאמר ונסעו הקהתים אחר נסוע שני הדגלים בכל המסעים חוץ מזה כי הארון היה נוסע לפניהם וזה היה שלשת ימים בלבד וזה טעם דרך שלשת ימים וכמוהו וילכו שלשת ימים במדבר איתם אין פירושו שהלכו ביום אחד מהלך שלשה ימים ויש אומרים שהלכו מהלך שלשה ימים ביום אחד ויש אומרים שהלכו מהלך שלשה ימים כנגד המסעים שנסעו בצאתם ממצרים והארון היה רחוק מהם דרך שלשה ימים וזה טעם וישכן הענן במדבר פארן ויפרשו ויסעו בראשונה כי על פי משה נסעו כי הענן נסע מיד וזה לא יתכן כי משה לא יסור מהארון והעד ויהי בנסוע הארון ויאמר משה ובנחה יאמר והנכון בעיני אשר אמרתי. וטעם וישכן הענן במדבר פארן שם כלל לתבערה שהוא קברות התאוה ולחצרות ורתמה ומסעים רבים והעד שלא הזכיר הכתוב בפרשת אלה מסעי במדבר פארן ועוד אפרשנו:


[33. AND THEY SET FORWARD FROM THE MOUNT OF THE LORD THREE DAYS’ JOURNEY.] In my opinion the first journey was unlike the rest of the journeys. The verse which states, *and the Kohathites…set forward* (v. 21) after the two standards journeyed refers to all the other journeys except this one, for⁵⁴ the ark journeyed before the camp of the Israelites.⁵⁵ However, this was the case for only three days. This is the meaning of *three days* (v. 33). Similarly, *And they went three days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham* (Num. 33:8) does not mean that they traveled a three days journey in one day.⁵⁶ Others say⁵⁷ that they traveled a three-day journey in one day.⁵⁸ Others say that they traveled a journey of three days corresponding to the journeys when they left Egypt,⁵⁹ and the ark was a three-day distance from them.⁶⁰. This is the meaning of *and the cloud abode in the wilderness of Paran* (v. 12).⁶¹ They explain that *And they took their first journey* (v. 13), means that they journeyed by the command of Moses, for the cloud traveled immediately.⁶² However, this is not so, for Moses did not distance himself from the ark, as proved by *And it came to pass, when the ark set forward* (v. 35) *And when it rested* (v. 36). What I said above appears correct to me.⁶³ *Paran*, in *and the cloud abode in the wilderness of Paran* (v. 12), is a general name for Taberah,⁶⁴ which is the same as Kibroth-hattaavah (v. 34), Hazeroth (Num. 33:17), Rithmah (Num. 33:18), and many other journeys.⁶⁵ The fact that Scripture does not mention the wilderness of Paran in the Torah portion *Elleh Mase* (these are the stages)⁶⁶ is proof of this. I will explain this later.⁶⁷

[THEM THAT HATE THEE.] The word *mesanekha* (them that hate Thee) is a *pi’el*.⁶⁹. *Pi’el* is referred to as the heavy conjugation. There is apparently an error in our texts and manuscripts. The *nun*⁷⁰. does not receive a *dagesh*⁷¹ receives a *dagesh*. Hence I.E.’s comment. in order to simplify the enunciation of the word.

### Verse 36

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 10:36:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:36:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:36:1)


**ובנחה.** בנוח הארון ונכתב בה"א כמו ה"א אהלה כי אותיות אהו"י מתחלפים:


AND WHEN IT RESTED. When the ark rested. *U-venucho* (when it rested) is spelled with a *heh*⁷⁴. The pronominal suffix *o* is usually spelled with a *vav*. Hence I.E.’s comment. in the same way that the word *oholo* (his tent) (Gen. 13:3) is,⁷⁵ ends in a *heh* and not, as expected, in a *vav*. for the letters *alef, heh, vav, yod* interchange.⁷⁶ was substituted for a *vav* in *oholo* and *u-venucho*.

footnotes:
⁷⁴ Rather than a vav
⁷⁵ Oholo
⁷⁶ In other words, a heh


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 10:36:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:36:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/10:36:2)


**שובה ה'.** אמר רבי יהודה המדקדק הראשון כי כל שב שטעמו מגזרת תשובה הוא פועל עומד ולא יוצא בבנין הקל רק אם היה טעמו בשלוה והשקט כמו בשובה ונחת תושעון כן שובה ה' רבבות אלפי ישראל שיניח' ולא ירגזו' מאויב. ודע כי רבבה מגזרת רב והטעם כמו רבבה כצמח השדה נתתיך ויתכן שנקרא עשרת אלפים כן בעבור היותו מספר רב על כן נסמכה מלת רבבות לאלפי ומשה התפלל שיניח וישקיט השם כל ישראל ואם הם רבים:


RETURN, O LORD. Rabbi Judah, the first grammarian, says that every time the word *shav* in the *kal* conjugation is related in meaning to *teshuvah* (return), it is intransitive, not transitive.⁷⁷ has the meaning of return, it is intransitive. However, when it means peace and quiet, as in *in sitting still* (be-shuvah) *and rest shall ye be saved* (Is. 30:15), and similarly in *Return* (shuvah), *O Lord, unto the ten thousands of the families of Israel*,⁷⁸ it means that God will give them rest and they will not be disturbed by any enemy.⁷⁹), O Lord, unto the ten thousands of the families of Israel. Note, the word *revavah* (ten thousand) comes from the same root as the word *rav* (many). *Revavah* in our verse is similar to the word *revavah* (increase) in *I cause thee to increase* (Ezek. 16:7). It is possible that ten thousand is called a *revavah* because it is a great number. The word *revavah*⁸⁰. is therefore connected to the word *alfe* (thousands).⁸¹). Moses prayed that God would grant rest and quiet to all of Israel, though they be many.

⁷⁷ In other words, whenever the word shav
⁷⁸ Then it is transitive.
⁷⁹ According to I.E. our clause should be rendered, give rest (shuvah
⁸⁰ In its plural form revevot
⁸¹ Thus I.E. renders our clause, Give rest, O Lord, unto the many thousands of Israel (revevot alfe yisra’el

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 11:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:1:4)

AND DEVOURED. *Va-tokhal* (and devoured) is penultimately accented. Compare, *va-yomer* (and he said) (Gen. 14:19).⁶ However, when it ends a clause,⁷) or at the end of a verse (*sof pasuk*). then it is ultimately accented. The latter is contrary to the laws of Hebrew grammar,⁸ but we find it to be so.

According to I.E. there are three souls in the body, *neshamah, ru’ach*, and *nefesh*. The *neshamah* (rational soul) is manifested in the brain; the *ru’ach* (spirit) is located in the heart; and the *nefesh* (the lusting soul), the part of the psyche that desires food and sex, is in the liver.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 11:8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:8:5)


**לשד.** י"א כי הלמ"ד נוסף כלמ"ד שלאנן ושלו והיה ראוי להיות השמן מלרע בעבור שהוא תאר השם והנכון בעיני שהלמ"ד לשד שורש כמו נהפך לשדי והוא הפך בחרבוני קיץ והיא הלחה הנכבדת העולה למעלה מכל שמן ויהיה השמן מלעיל כמשמעו:


A CAKE. Some say that the *lamed* of *leshad* (cake) is superfluous.⁴³ (breast). According to this interpretation, *leshad ha-shamen* means breast of the oil. See *Sifre* on Num. 11:8. “Just as the suckling imbibes, so to speak, every possible flavor with the mother-milk, so the Israelites found all flavors in the manna” (translated by Rosenbaum Silbermann, Num. p. 54). So too Rashi, “Our Rabbis explained it as meaning breasts.” It is similar to the *lamed* of *shalanan* (at ease)⁴⁴. in *at ease and quiet* (Job 21:23). The word *ha-shamen* (with oil) should have been ultimately accented⁴⁵ is ultimately accented. When the word *shemen* or *shamen* is a noun, it is penultimately accented; when an adjective, it is ultimately accented. because⁴⁶ the word *shamen* (oil) is an adjective.⁴⁷. However, I believe that the *lamed* of *leshad* is a root letter. The word *leshad* is similar to the word *leshadi* (my sap) in *My sap was turned* (Ps. 32:4). *My* (leshadi) *sap* stands in contrast to *the droughts* (charvone) in *the droughts of summer* (*Ibid*.)*. Leshad* refers to the finest part of the oil that floats on top of all oil. In this case, the word *ha-shamen* is penultimately vocalized in accordance with the meaning of the word.⁴⁸

footnotes:
⁴³ The basic word is shad
⁴⁴ The basic word being sha’anan
⁴⁵ However, ha-shamen
⁴⁶ According to this interpretation.
⁴⁷ Describing leshad
⁴⁸ For the word is a noun.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 11:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:21:1)


**שש מאות אלף רגלי.** ואין צורך להזכיר הפחותים. ורבים פירשו זאת הפרשה לטעמים רבים יש אומרים כי משה אמר מה שיאמרו לו ישראל בעת שישאלו מה הוא הבשר והתשובה שיאמר להם אין לכם צורך לשאול **היד ה' תקצר.** ולא אדע למה הצרה הזאת רק הדבר כמשמעו כי משה לא ידע כי השם יחדש אות או מופת כי אם להצדיק נביאו כאשר אפרש:


SIX HUNDRED THOUSAND MEN ON FOOT. There is no need to mention the lesser ones.⁹¹ Many interpret this section in various ways.⁹² Some say that Moses paraphrased what the children of Israel would say to him. When they would ask, what sort of meat,⁹³ Moses would answer them, you have no need to ask,⁹⁴ for *is the Lord’s hand waxed short*?⁹⁵ has been detached from the verse and opens a new comment on verse 23. However, this is an error. See Meijler.I do not know why we must suffer in this manner.⁹⁶ The text must be interpreted according to its plain meaning. Moses did not know that God would create a sign or a miracle.⁹⁷ He thought, as I will explain, that he would do so only to justify his prophet.⁹⁸

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 11:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:22:1)


**ומצא להם.** כדברי המתרגם ארמית ומה נכבד דרש קדמונינו במלת ישחט על הבהמה ויאסף על הדג:


WILL THEY SUFFICE THEM. *U-matza la-hem* (will they suffice them) is to be interpreted as in the Aramaic translation.⁹⁹ as, will they suffice them. The literal meaning of *u-matza la-hem* is: and he will find them. Hence I.E.’s comment. How precious is the interpretation of our ancients to the effect that the word *yishachet* (be slain) applies to cattle, and *ya’asef* (be gathered) refers to fish.¹⁰⁰) but fish do not. See *Hullin* 27b.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 11:25:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:25:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:25:3)


**ולא יספו.** פעם שנית וכן קול גדול ולא יסף ולא יסף עוד לדעתה ואין מדקדוק הלשון להיותו מגזרת פן תספו בכל חטאתם אמרו חכמים ז"ל שלקח משה מכל שבט ששה והנה שנים ושבעים ובעבור שאמר לו השם שבעים איש הניח השנים וזה נכון:


BUT THY DID SO NO MORE.¹⁰⁵. A second time.¹⁰⁶ is, they did not add. Hence I.E. points out that this term is an idiom meaning they did not repeat it. The same applies to the phrase *ve-lo yasaf* (and it went on no more) in *with a great voice, and it went on no more*¹⁰⁷ (Deut. 5:19) and *ve-lo yasaf* (now more) in *and he knew her again no more*¹⁰⁸ (Gen. 38:26). According to the rules of Hebrew grammar, the word *yasaf* is not related to the word *tissafu* (swept away)¹⁰⁹ comes from the root *yod, samekh, peh*, while the root of *tissafu* comes from the root *samekh, peh, heh*. If our word came from the latter root, it would have read *safu* not *yasefu*. in *lest ye be swept away in all their sins* (Num. 16:26).¹¹⁰ Our sages of blessed memory say that Moses took six men from each tribe. Their number thus came to seventy-two. However, Moses dropped the two¹¹¹ because God told him to gather seventy men.¹¹². 17a. This is correct.

### Verse 28

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 11:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/11:28:1)


**מבחוריו.** יש אומרים שפירושו מבחרותו והטעם שלא אמר כדברי זקן ויש מדביקים מבחוריו עם משרת משה והטעם ששרת אותו מיום שהיה בחור וזה איננו נכון כי זה המעשה היה בשנה השנית והנכון בעיני שהוא מבחוריו הוא מהמובחרים לשרת משה כי אחרים יש עמו ודע כי מלת בחור בלשון רבים פעם תשתנה ופעם לא תשתנה וכן מלת סריס אולי הם שני משקלים:


FROM HIS YOUTH UP. Some say that the meaning of *mi-bechurav* (from his youth up) is, from his youth. It means that he did not speak as an elder speaks.¹¹⁷ Others connect *mi-bechurav* (from his youth up) to *mesharet mosheh* (the minister of Moses);¹¹⁸, meaning the minister of Moses from his (Joshua’s) youth on. this means the one who served Moses from the time of his youth.¹¹⁹ However, this is incorrect, for this event occurred in the second year.¹²⁰ In my opinion, the word *mi-bechurav* means from the chosen. It means that he was one of those chosen to serve Moses, for there were others with him.¹²¹ Note that the word *bachur* (youth, or chosen) sometimes changes in the plural and sometimes does not.¹²² (Ps. 78:31) and at other times with a *sheva* as in our verse (*bechurav*, rather than *bachurav*). The same applies to the word *saris* (officer).¹²³ is both *sarisim* (Esth. 2:21) and *serisim* (Gen. 40:7). It is also possible that they belong to two different paradigms.¹²⁴ comes from the singular *bachur* (vocalized *pattach, shurik*), *bechurav* from the singular *bachur* (vocalized *kamatz, shurik*). Similarly *sarism*, and *serisim*. According to rules of Hebrew grammar, in the former form the *kamatz* changes to a *sheva* in the plural. Compare, *davar, devarim*. However, in the latter case the *pattach* is maintained in the plural form.

## Chapter 12


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 12:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:1:1)


**ותדבר מרים.** היא דברה גם אהרן הסכים או החריש על כן נענש:


AND MIRIAM…SPOKE. Miriam spoke. Aaron agreed or was silent.¹ is to be interpreted: And Miriam spoke against Moses, and Aaron remained silent (or agreed). I.E. interprets thus because our verse reads, *va-tedabber miriam ve-aharon*.

footnotes:
¹ In other words, And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 12:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:1:2)


וטעם **ותדבר.** עם בי"ת דרך גנאי כמו וידבר העם באלהים גם ימצא לשבח גם בדרך נבואה. יש אומרים כי משה מלך על כוש ולקח כושית והמתרגם אמר שפירתא וטעמו לשון כבוד כאשר יקראו הישמעאלים לזפת הלבן גם אנחנו נקרא העור סגי נהור. והנה לא יתכן שנקרא שם שהוא לשבח להפכו לגנאי ויש אומרים כי כוש בן ימיני הוא שאול וכן הלא כבני כושיים וכבר פירשתיו והישר בעיני שזו הכושית היא צפורה כי היא מדינית ומדינים הם ישמעאלים והם דרים באהלים וכן כתוב ירגזון יריעות ארץ מדין ובעבור חום השמש אין להם לבן כלל וצפורה היתה שחורה ודומה לכושית:


Now *va-tedabber* is in the feminine. Thus our verse is to be rendered, And Miriam spoke, and Aaron. If both spoke, then our text should have read, *va-yedabberu miriam ve-aharon*. Hence he was also punished.*Va-tedabber* (spoke) is followed by a *bet*² (And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses). and has a negative connotation. It is similar to *va-yedabber ha-am be-Elohim* (And the people spoke against God) (Num. 21:5). The verb *dabber* (spoke) followed by a *bet* is also found with a positive connotation.³ (adabberah): *Peace be within thee* (bakh) (Ps. 122:8). It also appears in prophetic statements.⁴ (II Sam. 23:2). Some say that Moses was king of Cush⁵ and took a Cushite woman.⁶ on *Shemot* 168; 247. Onkelos renders Cushite, beautiful.⁷ (the Cushite woman) as the beautiful women (*ittetah shappirtah*). According to Onkelos, Cushite is an honorific term. The Arabs similarly call pitch white. We too refer to a blind person by the term *sege nahor* (rich of light).⁸ 58a. But it is illogical⁹ to turn a positive name into a negative one.¹⁰ Some say that *Cush the Benjaminite* (Ps. 7:1) refers to Saul.¹¹. See Rashi and I.E. on Ps. 7:1. They say the same with regard to *Are ye not as the children of the Ethiopians* (Khushiyyim) *unto Me* (Amos 9:7).¹² I have already explained this.¹³I believe that the Cushite woman is to be identified with Zipporah, for Zipporah was a Midianite.¹⁴ The Midianites are Ishmaelites¹⁵ and they live in tents.¹⁶ Scripture similarly writes: *The curtains*¹⁷ *of the land of Midian do tremble* (Hab. 3:7). Because of the sun¹⁸ they do not have any whiteness at all. Zipporah was black and was like a Cushite.

footnotes:

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 12:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:1:3)


וטעם **כי אשה כשית לקח.** זה הדבור שדברה מרים ומה נכבד דברי קדמונינו שאמרו על הזקנים אשריהם ואוי לנשיהם והנה חשדו משה כי לא נמנע לשכב עם צפורה רק בעבור שאיננה יפה:


[FOR HE HAD MARRIED A CUSHITE WOMAN.] These are the words that Miriam spoke. How precious are the words of the ancients who said with regard to the elders, “Happy are they, but woe to their wives.”¹⁹ 17b; *Sifre, Devarim* 99; and *Yalkut Shimoni, Devarim* 738. They suspected that Moses refrained from sleeping with Zipporah only because she was not beautiful.²⁰ is to be understood as: because he refrained from sleeping with her because she was a Cushite.

footnotes:

²⁰ And not because he was a prophet. According to I.E., because of the Cushite woman whom he had married



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 12:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:2:1)


**ויאמרו הרק אך במשה.** הביאה ראיה כי לא עשה זה לקדושת השם כי הם היו נביאים ואין המשכב אסור להם:


AND THEY SAID: HATH THE LORD INDEED SPOKEN ONLY WITH MOSES? Miriam offered proof that Moses did not act in this manner because of the sanctity of God, for they too were prophets and they were not prohibited from engaging in sexual intercourse.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 12:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:2:2)


**הרק אך.** והאחד יספיק רק הוא דרך צחות כמו המבלי אין קברים:


ONLY WITH. Scripture reads, *ha-rak akh*.²¹ means only; so does *akh*. Thus our clause, which reads *ha-rak akh be-mosheh dibber Adonai*, literally reads: Hath the Lord spoken only only with Moses. Hence I.E.’s comment. One term²² or *akh*. Our text should have read, *ha-rak be-mosheh*, or *ha-akh be-mosheh*. would have sufficed. However, Scripture is employing elegant language.²³ Compare, *ha-mi-mi-beli en kevarim* (because there were no graves) (Ex. 14:11).²⁴ and *en* mean the same thing. See I.E. on Ex. 14:11 (Vol. 2, p. 277).

²¹ Rak
²² Rak
²³ It is considered poetic to repeat certain words in certain contexts.
²⁴ Beli

AND THE LORD HEARD IT. Even though they spoke in secret.²⁵

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 12:3:1

WAS VERY MEEK. The word *anav*²⁶. (meek) is similar to the word *shalev*²⁷. (at peace) (Job 16:12).²⁸. In both words a *vav* has been substituted for a *heh*. Its meaning is that Moses did not seek honor over his brother.²⁹

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 12:4:1

SUDDENLY. The *mem* of *pitom* (suddenly) is superfluous. It is like the mem of *shilshom* (three days ago).³⁰ of which is superfluous. *Pitom* is related to *peti* (a thoughtless one) (Prov. 9:4). It refers to something that one did not think of.³¹ is a person who does not anticipate the consequences of his acts. Similarly, the word *pitom* (suddenly) means unanticipated.

IN A VISION The meaning of *im yiheyeh nevi’akhem Adonai*³⁶ (if there be a prophet among you, I the Lord) is, if there be a prophet, one who is a prophet of God among you.³⁷ should be read as if written *nevi’akhem nevi Adonai*. (even the prophecy of Oded the prophet (II Chron. 15:8); and *ha-ohelah sarah immo* (his mother Sarah’s tent) (Gen. 24:67);³⁹ (the tent, tent of Sarah his mother). See I.E. on Gen. 24:67 (Vol. 1, p. 243). and *kisakha Elohim olam*⁴⁰ (Thy Throne, Throne of God for ever). See I.E. on Gen. 24:67 (Vol. 1, p. 243). (Thy throne given of God is for ever) (Ps. 45:7).

**בכל ביתי נאמן הוא.** טעמו כבן בית שיכנס בלא רשות ואם יצטרך ידבר צרכיו ואתם כאשר אתודע לכם בחלום תדעו ואם לא אין לכם רשות לשאול:


HE IS TRUSTED IN ALL MY HOUSE. It means that Moses is, at it were, a member of My house. He enters without permission. If necessary he states his needs. However, in your case when I make myself known to you in a dream, then you are informed. If not, then you have no permission to ask.

**נואלנו.** מבנין נפעל ואין לו ריע כי אם נואלו שרי צאן ויש אומרים שהוא הפוך מאולת קשורה וטעמו ידוע:

Some say that the root of *no’alnu*⁵⁶ comes from the root *yod, alef, lamed*. was formed by inverting the root *ivvelet*⁵⁷ (*yod*), *lamed*. (foolishness). Compare, *Foolishness is bound up* (Prov. 22:15) (in the heart of a child). The meaning of *no’alnu* is known.⁵⁸

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 12:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/12:12:1)


**אל נא תהי כמת.** אל עתה תהיה אחותינו כנפל המת כאשר יצא מבטן אמו נאכל חצי בשרו וכן בשר המצורע ואין צורך לתיקון סופרים:


LET HER NOT, I PRAY, BE AS ONE DEAD. Let our sister not now be as a stillborn child, half of whose flesh is consumed when it comes out of its mother’s womb. The same is true of the flesh of a leper.⁵⁹ There is no need for a scribal emendation.⁶⁰ should be read as if written our mother’s womb, and “half of his flesh” as if it read half our flesh, for Scripture employed the third rather than the first person plural because it wanted to avoid using non-flattering language regarding Moses and Aaron. See *Sifre debe Rav, Be-Ha’alotekha* 105. Also see Rashi on our verse. I.E. apparently believes that the Midrash was of the opinion that the scribes changed the original text of the Torah from the first person to the third person. He disagrees and maintains that there is no need to change the reading when interpreting our verse.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 12:16:1

**ויחנו במדבר פארן.** על דעת רבים שהענן היה שם בעבור שמצאו וישכן הענן במדבר פארן ויפרשו הענן סר מעל האהל כמשמעו ולפי דעתי אין זה הפירוש נכון:


AND PITCHED IN THE WILDERNESS OF PARAN. Many believe that the cloud was there.⁶³ They interpret thus because they found Scripture stating *and the cloud abode in the wilderness of Paran* (Num. 10:12).⁶⁴ They interpret *And when the cloud was removed from over the Tent* (v. 10) literally.⁶⁵ However, I believe that this is not the correct meaning.⁶⁶

**עלו זה בנגב.** עלו זה הדרך בנגב וידוע כי מצרים הוא נגב ארץ ישראל כאשר פירשתי בספר דניאל והראיה כי רוחב מצרים פחות משלשים מעלות ורוחב ירושלים שלשים ושלש ומדבר פארן בנגב ארץ מצרים והנה פירוש בנגב אינו נגב המחנה רק פירושו בנגב של ארץ כנען והעד בחברון שהוא ליהודה והכתוב אמר יהודה יעמוד על גבולו מנגב:


GET YOU UP HERE INTO THE SOUTH. Get you up this way in the south.¹⁶ is to be rendered: get you up this way i n the south (of the land of Canaan). The literal meaning of *alu zeh ba-negev* is: get you up this into the south. Hence I.E.’s comment. It is known that Egypt is south of the land of Israel, as I have explained in the Book of Daniel.¹⁷ The following is proof of this. Egypt is less than thirty degrees north of the equator.¹⁸, a term referring to the distance of a plane to the equator. Jerusalem is thirty-three degrees north of the equator.¹⁹ The desert of Paran²⁰ is south of the land of Canaan.²¹ Observe that the meaning of *in the South*²². is not south of the camp²³ but in the south of the land of Canaan. Proof of the aforementioned is that Scripture tells us concerning Hebron, which belonged to the tribe of Judah, *Judah shall abide in his border on the south* (Josh. 18:5).²⁴

¹⁸ Hebrew, rochav
¹⁹ See above.
²⁰ Where Israel was encamped when Moses sent out the spies.
²¹ The text reads, south of the land of Egypt. Paran was the place where Israel was when it sent out the spies. Geographically speaking, Paran is not south of Egypt. It is north of Egypt and lies between Egypt and Canaan. Hence a number of commentaries suggest emending the text to read, the wilderness of Paran is south of the land of Israel, or the wilderness of Paran is north of the land of Egypt. See Filwarg, Weiser, Krinsky, and Meijler.
²² Hebrew, ba-negev
²³ For taking a road south of the camp would lead them back into Egypt, as Paran is north of Egypt.
²⁴ We thus see that the south (the Negev) is a district in the Land of Israel.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 14:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/14:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/14:13:1)


**ושמעו מצרים כי העלית.** טעמו ואשר העלית ואחר שאמר ושמעו ואמרו אל יושב הארץ הזאת היא ארץ כנען פירש מה שמעו על כן פעם אחרת שמעו כי אתה ה' כבודך בקרב העם הזה:


WHEN THE EGYPTIANS SHALL HEAR–FOR THOU BROUGHTEST UP THIS PEOPLE. The meaning of *ki he’elita* (for thou broughtest up) is: that you brought up.¹² is to be interpreted as if written *asher he’elita*. In other words, the *ki* (for) in our verse is to be rendered *asher* (that). After Scripture states, *When the Egyptians shall hear* (ve-shame’u)…they *will say to the inhabitants of this land*, the reference being to the land of Canaan, it goes on to explain¹³ what the Egyptians heard. Scripture therefore repeats the word *shame’u* (have heard) and states they *have heard* (shame’u) *that Thou Lord* [Thy glory] *art in the midst of this people* (v. 14).¹⁴ in verse 14 picks up the thought which was interrupted by *they will say to the inhabitants of the land*.

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 15:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/15:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/15:2:1)


**כי תבואו אל ארץ מושבתיכם.** נסמכה זאת הפרשה בעבור שנחלשו ויתאבלו לנחם הבנים להודיעם כי יבאו אל הארץ והנכון בעבור שנשאו קול כל העדה (וחטאו) ונסלח להם בעבור תפלת משה אמר וכי תשגו והעד ונסלח להם והוצרך להזכיר משפט מנחות כל עולה וזבח ובסוף והנפש אשר תעשה ביד רמה רמז למעשיהם והזכיר דבר המקושש כי עשה ביד רמה ומרוב חמלת השם על ישראל שם הציצית לזכר שלא יעשה האדם ביד רמה או שלא ישכח:


WHEN YE ARE COME INTO THE LAND OF YOUR HABITATIONS. This chapter follows [the one dealing with the spies] in order to console the children by informing them that they would enter the land, for the Israelites grew weak and mourned.¹ However, the real reason that this chapter follows the one dealing with the spies, is because all the congregation shouted and sinned.² God forgave their sin because of the prayer of Moses.³ Scripture says, *And when ye shall err* (15:22).⁴ *And they shall be forgiven* (15:25) is proof of this.⁵ Scripture found it necessary to mention the law of the meal offering and of all burnt offerings and sacrifices.⁶ At the end,⁷ it states, *But the soul that doeth aught with a high hand* (v. 30). The latter alludes to Israel’s deeds.⁸ Scripture mentions the gatherer of wood (verses 32-34)⁹ because he acted with a high hand. God designated the fringes as a sign¹⁰ because of His great pity on Israel, so that a person will not act with a high hand or¹¹ forget.¹² issues. Thus in regard to the law concerning fringes, I.E. notes it is possible that Biblical rules require that the corners of garments be left unwoven so that their threads hang down to form fringes. He further notes that the law of fringes applies to pants. However, he then goes on to say that this interpretation is of no consequence, for the rabbis say that the fringes are specially prepared threads which are placed on the corner of any garment having four corners. Therefore pants are not included in the law of fringes.

[Verse 4.] A MEAL-OFFERING OF…FINE FLOUR. A tenth of an ephah for each one of the flock, (that is) he-lambs or kids. Scripture similarly states at the end (of the verse), *for each lamb* (v. 5). Scripture does not mention the free-will offering²⁰. along with the bullock.²¹ It mentions the peace offering²². [with the bullock] because it did not mention it above.²³ They all have one law.²⁴ (vow) mentioned in verses 3 and 8 and the *nedavah* (free-will offering) mentioned in verse 3 all have one law. ### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 15:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/15:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/15:16:1)


וטעם **תורה אחת.** לבד מהעולות כי העולות הם בחיוב חקה ועוד אמר השם כאשר תביאו מנחה על העולה מהסלת כן תתנו גם מעריסותיכם ואין צורך להזכיר מה שקבלו קדמונינו ז"ל כי הם שתים חלה ותרומה ושיעורן לפי שכל דבריהם אמת וזולתם הבל הנה שעור נוסף בין שעשו בשגגה מה שצוו שלא לעשות ובין שלא עשו בשגגה מה שצוו לעשות:


[ONE LAW.] Its meaning is, one law aside from the burnt offerings, for the burnt offerings are obligated by statute.³³ (statute) refers to. Verse 15 states, *there shall be one statute* (chukkah) *both for you, and for the stranger that sojourneth with you*. Verse 16 states, *One law* (Torah) *and one ordinance shall be both for you, and for the stranger. Prima facie*, Scripture is redundant. Hence I.E. comments that verse 15 deals with that which is obligatory, namely, the burnt offering (for it concludes the law mentioned in verse 14, which deals with sacrifices), and verse 16 deals with all the other commandments, for it speaks of Torah (Filwarg). God also says,³⁴ as you bring a meal offering of fine flour along with the burnt offering, thus shall you do with your dough.³⁵ follows the law of the meal offering. There is no need to mention what our ancients, of blessed memory, received by tradition, namely, that one is obligated to set aside two offerings, a portion of the dough³⁶. and a portion of the grain,³⁷. In other words, one has to set aside a portion from the dough, even though he has already set aside a portion from the grain out of which this very dough was made (Filwarg). and their amount.³⁸ Their words are true. Everything else is nonsense.

### Verse 39

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 15:39:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/15:39:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/15:39:1)


**והיה לכם לציצת.** והנה ישוב הפתיל להיותו בקצה כמו הציצית. והפירוש השני כאשר העתיקו חז"ל ובעבור שיש עדים נאמנים על הפירוש השני בטל הראשון והם העתיקו כי זאת המצוה עם בגד שיש לו ארבע כנפים והציצית הם הגדילים ועוד אפרשנו. והנה מצוה על כל מי שיש לו בגד בארבע כנפים שיתכסה בו ביום תמיד ולא יסירנו מעליו למען יזכרו והמתפללים בטלית בשעת התפלה יעשו זה בעבור שיקראו בקריאת שמע והיה לכם לציצית ועשו להם ציצית רק לפי דעתי יותר הוא חייב להתעטף בציצית בשאר השעות משעת התפלה למען יזכור ולא ישגה ולא יעשה עבירה בכל שעה כי בשעת התפלה לא יעשה עבירה:


AND IT SHALL BE UNTO YOU FOR A FRINGE. The thread at the end was like the fringe.⁶⁸ The other interpretation is the one which the rabbis of blessed memory transmitted.⁶⁹ Now the first interpretation is nullified in view of the fact that there are true witnesses⁷⁰ to the second explanation. The rabbis transmitted to us the law that this commandment applies to a garment that has four corners and that the tzitzit are fringes.⁷¹ I will explain this law later.⁷² Now this commandment states that everyone who has a four-cornered garment shall always cover himself with it during the day. He shall not remove it so that he remembers⁷³. 38. *Mikro’ot Gedolot* reads, so that they remember. the commandments. Those who pray with a *tallit* during the time of prayers do so because they read in the *shema*,⁷⁴ is part of the morning and evening prayers. It consists of Deut. 6:4-9; Deut. 11:13-21; Num. 15:37-41. *And it shall be unto you for a fringe* (v. 39) and *that they make them throughout their generations fringes* (v. 38). However, I believe that one is more obligated to enwrap oneself in fringes when he is not at prayer than during the time of prayer, so that he remembers the commandments and does not err and trespass during the other hours of the day, for in the hour of prayer he will not sin.⁷⁵, p. 79.

## Chapter 16


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 16:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:1:1)


**ויקח קרח.** זה הדבר היה במדבר סיני כאשר נתחלפו הבכורים ונבדלו הלוים כי חשבו ישראל שמשה אדונינו עשה מדעתו לתת גדולה לאחיו גם לבני קהת שהם קרובים אליו ולכל בני לוי שהם ממשפחתו והלוים קשרו עליו בעבור היותם נתונים לאהרן ולבניו וקשר דתן ואבירם בעבור שהסיר הבכורה מראובן אביהם ונתנה ליוסף אולי חשדוהו בעבור יהושע משרתו גם קרח בכור היה כי כן כתוב. ודגל ראובן חונה בנגב וקרח בנגב המשכן כי הוא מבני קהת ואלה נשיאי העדה היו בכורים והם היו מקריבים את העולות על כן לקחו מחתות והראיה על זה הפירוש מופת המטה שראו כל ישראל כי השם בחר שבט לוי תחת הבכורים על כן כתוב ותכל תלונתם כי התלונה על זה היתה. גם אמר משה כי לא מלבי בעבור שחשדוהו כי מלבו עשה ועוד לא ה' שלחני בשליחות הזה כי כבר האמינו בו כל ישראל ועוד ראיה גמורה כי כל העדה כלם קדושים וזה רמז לבכורים שהם קדושים כי כן כתוב קדש לי כל בכור והם היו הכהנים הנגשים אל ה' והם עיקר כל העדה:


NOW KORAH, THE SON OF IZHAR…TOOK. This event occurred in the wilderness of Sinai when the first-born were set aside¹ and the Levites were placed in their stead.² Israel thought that our master Moses acted out of his own will in giving his brother an elevated position. They suspected that he acted similarly towards the sons of Kohath, who were his relatives, and to all the sons of Levi who were of his family. The Levites rebelled against Moses because they were subservient to Aaron and his sons. Dathan and Abiram rebelled because Moses³ removed the birthright from Reuben their forefather, and gave it to Joseph. It is also possible that they suspected that Moses favored the tribe of Joseph because Joshua was his assistant.⁴ Korah too was a first-born, as Scripture clearly states.⁵ The banner of Reuben camped in the south.⁶ So did Korah, for he was a Kohathite.⁷ The princes of the congregation were first-born. They offered the burnt offering. They therefore took the fire pans. The miracle of the staff,⁸ which demonstrated to all of Israel that God chose the Levites in place of the first-born, is proof that this explanation is correct.⁹ Hence Scripture reads, *that there may be made an end of their murmurings against Me* (Num. 17:25), for the murmuring was an account of this.¹⁰ Moses also said, *that I have not done them of mine own mind* (v. 28). He said the aforementioned because Israel had come to believe that he had acted on his own. Furthermore, Moses said, *then the Lord hath not sent me* (v. 29) in this thing,¹¹ take the place of the first-born and the Levites be subservient to the *kohanim*. because Israel had come to believe in him.¹². It does not appear in the verse. Here is another rigorous proof: *seeing all the congregation are holy* (v. 3). The aforementioned alludes to the first-born who are holy, for Scripture states, *Sanctify unto Me all the first-born* (Ex. 13:2). The first-born were the priests *that come near to the Lord* (Ex. 19:22). They were the most important ones of the congregation.

³ Actually Jacob did so on his death bed. However, Moses enforced Jacob’s decree. Hence Dathan and Abiram blamed Moses.
⁴ Joshua was descended from Ephraim the son of Joseph.
⁵ Ex. 6:21.

### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 16:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:11:1)


**לכן.** על כן קשרתם אתה וכל עדתך שאתם נועדים על השם והטעם כמו ורוזנים נוסדו יחד על ה' ועל משיחו שעשו וועד להריב עם השם וכן בהצותם על ה' וי"א כי ה"א הנועדים נוסף:


THEREFORE. Therefore you and your whole congregation that art gathered together, rebel against the Lord.³³ means against the Lord, and is to be interpreted as rebel against the Lord. The literal meaning of *al Adonai* is on the Lord. Thus the literal meaning of our verse is: Therefore you and your whole congregation that are gathered together on the Lord (*al ha-Adonai*). Hence, I.E.’s comment. Its meaning is similar to *And the rulers take counsel together, Against the Lord*,³⁴ (literally on the Lord). However, its meaning is against the Lord. *and against His anointed*³⁵ (literally, and on His anointed). However, its meaning is, *and against His anointed*. (Ps. 2:2). They gathered in order to fight with God. *When they strove against the Lord*³⁶. (Num. 26:9) is similar.³⁷ has the meaning of against. Some say that the *heh* prefixed to *no’adim* (gathered together) is superfluous.³⁸ (that art gathered together) is to be read *no’adim* (gathered together). If the *heh* is not superfluous, then our verse is to be interpreted, *Therefore thou and all thy company that are gathered together* (ha-no’adim) *against the Lord*. If the *heh* is superfluous, then our verse reads: Therefore thou and all thy company are gathered (*no’adim*) together against the Lord.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 16:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:14:2)


**העיני האנשים ההם.** טעמו תרצה לנקר עיני האנשים ההם רמז ליוצאים ממצרים כאילו אמר תרצה לנקר העינים שלא תראינה כי זה שעשית לנו נראה הוא לעינים ודרך משל לומר סגורות הן עיני פלוני על כן לא יראה על כן לא נעלה ויש אומרים התרצה להחשיך העינים שלא תראינה כלומר אחיזת עינים אתה עושה לנו לא נעלה ויש אומרים אילו היית מנקר עינינו לא נעלה ואמר האנשים ההם על דרך בני אדם חסרי דעת שלא ירצו לדבר על נפשם בגנאי והנכון בעיני שמלת האנשים ההם רמז לזקנים שהיו עם משה כי כן כתוב וילכו אחריו זקני ישראל:


WILT THOU PUT OUT THE EYES OF THESE MEN? Its meaning is: you want to put out the eyes of these men. This alludes to those who left Egypt. It is as if Korah said, you want to put out their eyes so that they do not see. But what you did is visible to the eyes. Therefore we will not come up. It is metaphoric to say so and so’s eyes are closed and he therefore cannot see.⁴⁵ is not to be taken literally. Others say its meaning⁴⁶? is: Do you want to darken the eyes so that they do not see? In other words, you are fooling us. We will not come up.⁴⁷, this interpretation seems to be identical to the one above. Hence Filwarg suggests that this interpretation is that *We will not go up* means we will not go up to the Land of Israel. In other words, Korah said you are fooling us, for you have no intention of bringing us to the Land of Israel. Others say its meaning⁴⁸? is: even if you put out our eyes we will not go up. Korah said *of these men* because he spoke in the manner of the unintelligent, who do not want to say anything negative about themselves.⁴⁹ refers to Korah himself. According to this interpretation the meaning of *wilt thou put out the eyes of these men* is, will you put out my eyes? However, I believe that *of these men* alludes to the elders who were with Moses, for Scripture clearly states, *and the elders of Israel followed him* (v. 25).

**למשכן קרח.** הנכון בעיני שהיה לקרח אהל לאדם שלו ולרכושו רחוק ממחנה הלוים והיה עם אהלו אהלי דתן ואבירם כי לא יחנו סביב המשכן כי אם הלוים לבדם ומזה הכתוב נלמוד כי בעל הדגל היה חונה קרוב ממחנה הלוים:


THE DWELLING OF KORAH. I believe that Korah had a tent for his household and his wealth. This tent was far from the camp of the Levites. The tents of Dathan and Abiram were close to Korah’s tent, for only Levites camped around the tabernacle.⁶¹ We learn from this verse that the bearer of the banner⁶² camped close to the camp of the Levites.⁶³

footnotes:

The Israelites camped around the four sides of the tabernacle (Num. 2:2). The family of Kohath camped on the south side (Num. 3:29). So did the tribe of Reuben (Num. 2:10). Now Korah’s tent was close to the tent of Dathan and Abiram, who came from the tribe of Reuben, because the tribe of Reuben bore the banner of the tribes that camped on the south and were thus close to the Levites.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 16:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:28:1)


**לעשות את כל המעשים.** להחליף הבכורים בלוים ודע כי דבר גדול היה ומכעיס לאשר איננו מאמין להסיר הבכורים מכהונתם ולהשיב המעלה למשפחת משה לבדו וכל זה הי' בעבור מעשה העגל כי ויעלו עולות ויגשו שלמים הבכורים העלום כי הם היו לבדם הכהנים ובני לוי הרגו עובדי העגל ויש בכאן שאלה ותשובתם בפרשת וילך משה:


TO DO ALL THESE WORKS. To have the Levites take the place of the first-born. Note, it is a major and grievous act to the one who does not believe that God ordered the first-born to be removed from their position as *kohanim* and to have this status conferred only upon the family of Moses. All of this was done⁶⁶ because of the incident of the golden calf, because *and offered burnt-offerings, and brought peace-offerings* (Ex. 32:6) speaks of the first-born who offered these sacrifices, for they alone were the *kohanim*. Also, the sons of Levi⁶⁷ killed those who served the calf.⁶⁸. There is a question here.⁶⁹ Its answer is found in the Torah portion which opens with the words *va-yelekh mosheh* (Deut. 31:1).⁷⁰.

⁶⁷ Alone.

⁶⁹ It isn’t clear what the question is. I believe it to be the issue of God changing His mind. According to medieval Jewish philosophy, God and His mind are one. Thus God’s mind is immutable. This being the case, how could He change His mind regarding the fitness of the first-born to serve as priests?
⁷⁰ I.E. there explains that God does not change. It is people who do. See I.E. on Deut. 31:16. Here I.E. is probably hinting that it wasn’t God who changed His mind but rather the first-born who changed by becoming unfit to serve as kohanim

**בריאה.** י"א שהיא תורה על המצא מה שלא היה וכבר פירשתי שאין המלה רק מגזרת וברא אתהן וכבר נבקעו מדינות רבות וירדו הדרים בהן שאולה והנה פירושה כטעם גזרה:


BUT IF THE LORD MAKE A NEW THING. Some say that the word *beri’ah* (a new thing) refers to the bringing forth of something that was never in existence.I have already explained that the word *beri’ah* is related to the word *u-vara* (hack) in *and hack them* (Ezek. 23:47).⁷¹ Many cities⁷². have been split open, and those who dwelt in them have gone down to the pit.⁷³ The meaning of *bara* is to cut.⁷⁴ (But if the Lord make a new thing) should be interpreted, but if God shall certainly split. An alternative interpretation of I.E. is: The meaning of *bara* is to decree. According to this interpretation I.E. renders *ve-im beri’ah yivra Adonai* (but if the Lord make a new thing) as, but if God shall decree.

**ופצתה האדמה את פיה.** כמו ופתחה וכן יפצה פיהו וכבר רמזתי בעבור היות נשמת האדם העליונה תיכונה תדבר על הגבוהים ממנה כדרך ארמונה שהוא הגוף וכן על השפלים ממנה והטעם להבין השומעים:

### Verse 35

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 16:35:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:35:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/16:35:1)


ה"א **החמשים** מושכת עצמה ואחרת עמה. י"א כי קרח מהנבלעים היה והראיה ותבלע אותם ואת קרח וי"א כי נשרף היה והעד ואת קרח במות העדה באכול האש וחז"ל אמרו כי נשרף ונבלע ולפי דעתי שלא נבקע רק מקום דתן ואבירם כי לא נזכר וקרח היה עומד עם מחתתו עם אהרן ועם נשיאי העדה מקריבי הקטרה ופירוש הפסוק ואת קרח איננה דבק עם ותבלע אותם רק עם במות העדה ואם יטעון טוען ויאמר למה לא הזכיר קרח עם השרופים התשובה כי אחר שהזכיר הכתוב שנשרפה עדתו שבאה לעזרה אין צורך להזכיר קרח כי מקל וחומר יודע הדבר וכמוהו מרכבות פרעה וחילו ולא הזכיר בשירה פרעה שטבע ובאמת טבע כי כן כתוב ונער פרעה וחילו והעד הנאמן כי קרח היה מהשרופים ולא יהיה כקרח וכעדתו:


[AND FIFTY MEN.] The *heh* of *ha-chamishim* (the fifty) is to be read as if written twice.⁸⁷ (and…fifty men). Our text, which reads *ha-chamishim u-matayim*, should be read as if written, *ha-chamishim ve-ha-matayim* (and…the two hundred and fifty men). The latter is the correct grammatical construction. Hence I.E.’s comment. Some say that Korah was among the ones who were swallowed. They offer as proof, *And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up together with Korah* (Num. 26:10). Others say that Korah was burned. They offer, *with Korah, when that company died; what time the fire devoured* (*Ibid*.) as proof. Our sages say that Korah was burned and swallowed.⁸⁸I believe that only the place of Dathan and Abiram split open,⁸⁹ for no other place is mentioned.⁹⁰ Korah was standing with his fire-pan with Aaron and the leaders of the congregation who were offering incense.⁹¹ *With Korah* (Num. 26:10) is not connected to *and swallowed them up* (*Ibid*.) but rather to *when that company died* (*Ibid*.). This is the way the aforementioned verse is to be interpreted. If someone should argue and say, “Why isn’t Korah mentioned among those who were burned?” the answer is: once Scripture mentions that Korah’s company, which came to his aid, was burned, it is not necessary to mention Korah. For we know this by arguing from a minor to a major premise.⁹² *Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath He cast into the sea* (Ex. 15:4) is similar.⁹³ Moses does not mention in the song⁹⁴ is stated. that Pharaoh drowned. The truth is that Pharaoh drowned, for Scripture explicitly states, *But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea* (Ps. 136:15). The verse *that he fare not as Korah, and as his company* (Num. 17:5) is proof that Korah was among those who were burned.⁹⁵

footnotes:
⁸⁷ It is also to be placed in front of the word u-matayim
⁸⁸ San. 110:a.
⁸⁹ Thus it was only Dathan and Abiram and their families who were swallowed by the ground.
⁹⁰ Scripture does not mention that any other place split open.
⁹¹ And were consumed by fire.
⁹² If Korah’s followers were burned, then Korah certainly was.
⁹³ In that by employing a similar argument, we learn from this verse that Pharaoh died.
⁹⁴ The song of Moses wherein Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath He cast into the sea
⁹⁵ For the term company refers to the 250 men who were consumed by fire.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 17:11:1

**את המחתה.** הידועה:


TAKE THY FIRE-PAN. The reference is to a specific fire-pan.¹⁸ (fire-pan) has the definite article *ha* prefixed to it. The literal meaning of *kach et ha-machtah* is, take the fire-pan. According to I.E. *the fire-pan* in our verse means the specific fire-pan used to offer incense (Krinsky).

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 17:11:2

**ושים קטרת.** ולא אמר הקטרת והמשכיל יבין:


AND LAY INCENSE THEREON. Scripture does not say, and lay “the” incense on.¹⁹ (incense), it refers to another incense. The intelligent will understand.²⁰

footnotes:
¹⁹ “The” incense would refer to the incense usually burned in the tabernacle. Since the definite article is not prefaced to ketroret
²⁰ The difference between the two types of incense. Some of the commentators on I.E. believe that he was of the opinion that the incense used by Moses to stop the plague had the power to clean the air of pollutants that caused the plague (Krinsky, Filwarg).


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 17:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/17:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/17:11:3)


**והולך.** לשון צווי כמו הושב את אביך ושרשו כמו הוליכי וטעמו הובילי כמו ילך עמך:


AND CARRY. The word *holekh* (and carry) is an imperative.²¹ looks like a *kal* participle. In this case the word would mean goes or walks. However, the context negates such a rendering. Hence I.E.’s comment. It is similar to the word *hoshev* (make to dwell)²² imperative. in *make thy father…to dwell* (Gen. 47:6). *Holekh* comes from the same root as *helikhi* (take away) (Ex. 2:9).²³. It means bring,²⁴ means: and bring (and carry) the fire-pan quickly to the congregation. the idea being it²⁵ should go with you.

footnotes:
²¹ In the hifil. Holekh
²² A hifil
²³ Its root is yod, lamed, kaf
²⁴ Ve-holekh meherah el ha-edah
²⁵ The incense-bearing fire-pan.

RODS. Some say that the rod of Levi is not God’s rod, for God’s rod was already known.³⁰ Why then write Aaron’s name on it.³¹ Others say that the rod³² was like the other rods. There was no difference between them.³³ This interpretation appears correct to me.

### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 17:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/17:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/17:20:1)


**והשכותי.** מפעלי הכפל כמו והתמותי (טמאתך) מגזרת וחמת המלך שככה וטעם **והשכותי.** כדרך בני אדם למצוא מנוחה ומטה לוי בתוך השנים עשר והנה יוסף במטה אחד:


I WILL MAKE TO CEASE. The word *ve-hashikkoti* (I will make to cease) comes from a double root.³⁷. It is similar to the word *ve-hatimmoti*³⁸. Both words are *hifils*. (and I will consume) in *and I will consume thy filthiness from out of thee* (Ezek. 22:15). It is related to the word *shakhakhah* (assuaged) in *then was the king’s wrath assuaged* (Esth. 7:10).*Ve-hashikkoti* (I will make to cease) means I [God] will find rest.³⁹ Scripture employs human language.⁴⁰ The rod of Levi was among the twelve. Behold, the tribe of Joseph was represented by one rod.⁴¹

FOR THE HOUSE OF LEVI. The word *matteh* (rod of) is to be read as if written twice. Our verse⁴² is to be read as if written: the rod of Aaron, the rod of the house of Levi.

**ויגמול.** מגזרת ויגדל הילד ויגמל ורבים אמרו בעבור שקדים כי המטה היה ממין האילן ואינה ראיה ודרך דרש כי שקדים כמו כי שוקד אני:


AND BORE RIPE ALMONDS. The word *va-yigmol* (and bore ripe) is related to the word *va-yigammal* (and was weaned) in *And the child grew, and was weaned* (Gen. 21:8). Many say that the rod⁴³ came from an almond tree because the rod bore almonds. However, this is not proof. The word *shekedim* (almonds) has midrashically been related to the word *shoked* (watch) in I *watch over My word to perform it* (Jer. 1:12).⁴⁴

### Verse 27

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 17:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/17:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/17:27:1)


**ויאמרו בני ישראל.** די לנו שגוענו ואבדנו והנה עוד כל הקרב אל המשכן ה' ימות כמות השרופים ומי יתן ותמנו לגוע אז אמר השם לאהרן שהוא הנגיד על שבט לוי להזהירו שלא יכשילו הלוים את ישראל. וטעם לאהרן על יד משה או כאשר הוא כי גם אהרן נביא היה גם זאת הפרשה לאות כי במדבר סיני היתה כאשר הוקם המשכן ונבחרו הלוים ונפסלו הבכורים:


AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SPOKE UNTO MOSES, SAYING. It is enough for us that we perished and were undone.⁴⁵ Now, in addition, everyone that comes near the tabernacle will die like those who were burnt. O that we should cease dying.⁴⁶ God then spoke to Aaron, who was the leader of the tribe of Levi, and cautioned him that the Levites not cause the Israelites to stumble.⁴⁷ The meaning of *unto Aaron* (Num. 18:1) is that God communicated with Aaron through Moses. On the other hand, the clause may be taken at face value,⁴⁸ because Aaron too was a prophet. Also, this section⁴⁹ is proof that the rebellion took place in the desert of Sinai when the tabernacle was erected and the Levites were chosen, and the first-born were disqualified.⁵⁰

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 18:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/18:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/18:2:1)


**שבט אביך.** הוא לוי וחז"ל פירשוהו כמשמעו ולפי דעתי מה שפירשתיו כאילו אמר מטה לוי שהוא שבט אביך:


THE TRIBE OF THY FATHER. The reference is to Levi.³ is to be understood as the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your patriarch Levi. Our sages say that *the tribe of thy father* is to be taken at face value.⁴ However, I believe that it is to be explained in keeping with my earlier interpretation. Our verse is to be read as if written, the tribe of Levi which is the tribe of your father.⁵ is to be read as if written, *matteh levi she-hu shevet avikha*.

So too the word *yillaveh* (be joined) in *Now this time will my husband be joined* (Gen. 29:34). Look, the Levites are joined by their names.⁶. Their name indicates that they have joined Aaron. **זאת חקת.** גם זאת הפרשה במדבר סיני נאמרה כאשר צוה השם וישלחו מן המחנה ובפסח היו טמאי מתים. ונסמכה זאת הפרשה בעבור שהיא לכהן:


THIS IS THE STATUTE. This chapter was also¹ stated at Sinai. It was given when God commanded *that they put out of the camp…whosoever is unclean by the dead* (Num. 5:2). There were also people who were unclean by coming into contact with a dead body when Passover² arrived (Num. 9:6). This chapter is placed here³ because it relates to the *kohen*.⁴ played a major role in the ritual of the red heifer.

² Celebrated by Israel in the second year after the Exodus.
³ Following the laws dealing with the tithes.

A RED HEIFER, FAULTLESS. The heifer is not to be small.⁵ (cow), not of an *eglah* (heifer). The Gaon⁶ says that *the water of sprinkling* (v. 13)⁷ is similar to honey, which is injurious to the one who has red bile⁸ but stimulates the one who has phlegm.⁹ However, there is no need for this interpretation.

**ושרף את הפרה.** השורף והעד לעיניו:


AND THE HEIFER SHALL BE BURNT IN HIS SIGHT. *Ve-saraf et ha-parah* (and the heifer shall be burnt)¹⁴ is: and he shall burn the cow. is to be rendered, and someone shall burn the heifer. The term *le’enav* (in his sight)¹⁵ proves the latter interpretation.

footnotes:
¹⁴ The literal meaning of ve-saraf et ha-parah
¹⁵ Eleazar’s sight.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:6:1)


**עץ ארז.** כמו למצורע ושם רמזתי סוד:


CEDAR-WOOD. As in the case of a leper.¹⁶ I have hinted there at some secret.¹⁷

footnotes:
¹⁶ Cedar wood was used in cleansing a leper (Lev. 14:4).
¹⁷ I.E. points out that there is a connection between leprosy and death. Hence cedar is employed in cleansing someone who has been contaminated by contract with a leper or a dead body.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:7:1)


**וכבס בגדיו.** הכהן השורף:


THEN THE PRIEST SHALL WASH HIS CLOTHES. The *kohen* who burns it.¹⁸, the reference is to the cow. However, in view of the fact that the latter is stated in the next verse, some say that the reference is to the cedar. See Filwarg and Krinsky.

footnotes:
¹⁸ Prima facie


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:7:2)


**וטמא הכהן.** וכבר ישב טמא ויש אומרי' שיהיה טמא עד הערב שלא יאכל מן הקדשים:


AND THE PRIEST SHALL BE UNCLEAN. The meaning of *ve-tame ha-kohen* (and the priest shall be unclean) is, and the *kohen* has already been unclean,¹⁹ has been made unclean by performing the ritual. According to this interpretation the *vav* prefixed to *ve-tame* means “and.” Hence the meaning of *ve-tame ha-kohen* is: and the *kohen* was unclean. or, as some say, the *kohen* shall be unclean.²⁰ is a future form meaning: and he shall be unclean. The *vav* is a conversive *vav*. *Until the even* refers to the eating of sacred food.

footnotes:
¹⁹ The kohen
²⁰ In this case ve-tame



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:9:1)


**איש טהור.** איננו הכהן השורף:


A MAN THAT IS CLEAN. The reference is not to the *kohen* who burns the cow.²¹ does this (Krinsky). According to the *Sifre* on this verse, any clean person, even if not a *kohen*, may gather the ashes of the red cow. However, I.E. seems to believe that this task was assigned to a *kohen*.

footnotes:
²¹ Another kohen


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:9:2)


**למי נדה.** פירושו רחוק כמו מנדיכם:


A WATER OF SPRINKLING. The meaning of *niddah* (sprinkling) is distance.²² (water of sprinkling) means the water of the distant, i.e., the water to be used to purify the distant. Compare, *me-naddekhem*²³ comes from the same root as *niddah*. When one hates another person, he keeps his distance from him. (that hate you) (Is. 66:5).

footnotes:
²² The person who is unclean is distanced from the sanctuary. Thus me-niddah
²³ Me-naddekhem



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:10:1)


**וטמא עד הערב.** ואחר שאמר שיכבס את בגדיו אין צורך להזכיר שירחץ במים:


AND BE UNCLEAN UNTIL THE EVEN. Once Scripture states that the gatherer of the ashes shall wash his clothes there is no need to mention that he shall wash in water.²⁴

footnotes:
²⁴ For Scripture earlier linked the two. See verse 7.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:10:2)


**ולגר הגר בתוכם.** בעבור היות ארץ ישראל קדושה כי הכבוד שם:


AND UNTO THE STRANGER THAT SOJOURNETH AMONG THEM. For the Land of Israel is holy because God’s glory is there.²⁵

footnotes:
²⁵ Hence even a stranger (a non-Jew) must abide by this rule.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:11:1)


**לכל נפש אדם.** יהודי או עובד כוכבים:


EVEN ANY MAN’S DEAD BODY. Be it the body of a Jew or a non-Jew.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:11:2)


**אדם.** ולא בהמה:


MAN’S…BODY. Not the body of an animal.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:11:3)


**וטמא.** יהיה טמא והוא פועל עתיד כי הוי"ו השיבו ועל דעתי שהוא פועל עבר:


SHALL BE UNCLEAN. The meaning of *ve-tame* is, shall be unclean. It is a future form, for the *vav* changes the verb²⁶, a third person perfect. from a perfect to an imperfect. However, I believe that *ve-tame* is in the past tense.²⁷ being conjunctive. Thus the meaning of *ve-tame* is: and he was unclean. The import of our verse thus is: and after being unclean for seven days he shall purify himself. See I.E. on verse 7 and the notes thereto.

footnotes:
²⁶ Tame
²⁷ Its vav



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:12:1)


**יתחטא בו.** יסור חטאו בו או כמו תחטאני באזוב ואטהר וידוע כי בסוד החשבון השלישי כמו השביעי:


THE SAME SHALL PURIFY HIMSELF THEREWITH. The meaning of *hu yitchate vo* (the same shall purify himself therewith) is, he shall remove his sin therewith.²⁸ means sin. Hence I.E.’s interpretation. On the other hand, the word *yitchate* (shall purify himself) is similar to the word *techatteni* (purge me) in *Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean* (Ps. 51:9).²⁹ means purify. Those who are acquainted with the secret of numbers know that the number three is like the number seven.³⁰

footnotes:
²⁸ That is, by undergoing this ritual he will remove the potentiality of entering the sanctuary in a state of impurity and thus sinning. The word chet
²⁹ In other words, yitchatta
³⁰ The number seven has mystical significance in that seven days make up a lunar quarter. The number three is close to half of the number 7. See I.E. on Gen. 34:25 and the notes thereto (Vol. 1, p. 330).



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:13:1)


**כי מי נדה.** יש מפרשים כמו אך במי נדה יתחטא:


BECAUSE THE WATER OF SPRINKLING. Some say that that *me niddah* (the water of sprinkling) has the same meaning as *me niddah* (water of sprinkling) in *it shall be purified with the water of sprinkling* (Num. 31:23).³¹

footnotes:
³¹ In other words, both refer to water mixed with the ashes of the red heifer. Num. 31:23 deals with the purification of utensils captured from non-Jews. I.E. prefaces these remarks with “some say” because, according to the rabbis, Num. 31:23 refers to water in which a menstruant immerses herself.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:13:2)


**לא זורק עליו.** על המים:


WAS NOT DASHED. The word *zorak* (dashed) refers to the water.³² is singular and *me* (water of) is plural.

footnotes:
³² Even though zorak


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:13:3)


**עוד.** תמיד כמו עוד כל ימי הארץ:


IS YET. The word *od* (is yet) means continuously.³³ Compare, *od* (while) in *While the earth remaineth* (Gen. 8:22).

footnotes:
³³ He is continuously unclean until sprinkled.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:14:1)


**באהל.** והבית כאהל רק הזכיר הכתוב האהל בעבור היות ישראל באהלים וכן אשר ישחט שור או כשב ועז במחנה:


IN A TENT. A house has the same law as a tent. Scripture mentions a tent because Israel then lived in tents. *That killeth an ox, or lamb, or goat, in the camp* (Lev. 17:3) is similar.³⁴

footnotes:
³⁴ The law laid down in Lev. 17:3 applies equally to a town. Scripture speaks of a camp because Israel then lived in tents in a camp.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:14:2)


**וכל אשר באהל.** מבגד:


AND EVERY THING THAT IS IN THE TENT. Garments.³⁵

footnotes:
³⁵ For the next verse deals with vessels.



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:15:1)


**צמיד פתיל.** שנים פתילים:


COVERING CLOSE-BOUND. Two coverings.³⁶ (close bound). According to I.E. each one of these terms refers to a covering. The *tzamid* goes over the opening, while the petil goes round about the above covering and the rim of the utensil (Krinsky). Others claim that I.E. believes that the cover is made of two parts. See Krinsky, Filwarg, and Weiser.

footnotes:
³⁶ Scripture reads, tzamid, petil



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:16:1)


**או בקבר.** של אדם:


OR A GRAVE. Of a human being.



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:17:1)


ו. **לקחו לטמא.** הנה פירוש איך יתחטא:


AND FOR THE UNCLEAN THEY SHALL TAKE. See, Scripture explains how one who comes into contact with the dead shall purge himself.³⁷. However, it did not describe the procedure. Now it does.

footnotes:
³⁷ Earlier, in verse 12, Scripture had said, the same shall purify himself therewith



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:18:1)


**איש טהור.** והקרוב להיותו כהן:


A CLEAN PERSON. The reference is most probably to a *kohen*.³⁸ are acquainted with the laws of purification.

footnotes:
³⁸ For kohanim



### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:20:1)


**ואיש אשר יטמא.** וכבר הזכיר כל הנוגע במת בנפש ונכרתה ועתה הזהיר על העצם ועל הקבר:


BUT THE MAN THAT SHALL BE UNCLEAN. Scripture has already mentioned, *Whosoever toucheth the dead…that soul shall be cut off from Israel* (v. 13). It now warns the one who touches a bone or a grave [not to defile the sanctuary].



### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:21:1)


**יטמא עד הערב.** ולא יטהר עד אשר ירחץ:


SHALL BE UNCLEAN UNTIL EVEN. And shall not become clean until he washes.



### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:22:1)


**וכל אשר יגע בו הטמא יטמא.** שהוא טמא מת או עצם או קבר:


AND WHATSOEVER THE UNCLEAN PERSON TOUCHETH SHALL BE UNCLEAN. The reference is to one who has become unclean by touching a dead body, a bone, or a grave.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 19:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/19:22:2)

SHALL BE UNCLEAN UNTIL EVEN. And washes.³⁹
