## Chapter 20


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:1:1)


**בחדש הראשון.** בשנת הארבעים והנה אין בתורה כלל שום מעשה או נבואה רק בשנה הראשונה ובשנת הארבעים:


IN THE FIRST MONTH. In the fortieth year.¹ Look, the Torah does not contain any act or prophecy except in the first and the fortieth year.²

footnotes:
¹ Following the Exodus.
² Scripture describes what happened in the first and the last year of Israel’s sojourn in the wilderness. What happened in the other years is ignored. Actually the Book of Numbers opens with a command to Moses in the second month of the second year. Filwarg explains that I.E. was not being precise. Some editions read, “except for the first year, the fortieth year.” The latter is to be interpreted as if written, and the fortieth year.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:1:2)


וטעם **ויבאו בני ישראל כל העדה.** בעבור שמתו דור המדבר ועתה באו הבאים אל ארץ כנען:


[AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL, EVEN THE WHOLE CONGREGATION, CAME.] Scripture states this because the generation that left Egypt died in the wilderness and they who were entering Canaan came to the desert of Zin.³ appears to be unnecessary. I.E. says that it refers to those about to enter Canaan. They are now the complete congregation, for none of them need die in the wilderness. Rashi comments similarly.

footnotes:
³ The phrase even the whole congregation


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:1:3)


**וישב העם בקדש.** בעבור שישבו שם ימים רבים כי כן כתיב:


AND THE PEOPLE ABODE IN KADESH. For they dwelt there for many days.⁴, because they dwelt there for many days. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture.⁵.

footnotes:
⁴ Scripture states, and the people abode in Kadesh
⁵ See Deut. 1:46, So ye abode in Kadesh many days



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:2:1)


**ולא היה מים לעדה.** ספר הכתוב שנים מאורעים האחד מות מרים והשני מות אהרן ומשה ולא יכנסו לארץ והחל לספר הסבה:


AND THERE WAS NO WATER FOR THE CONGREGATION. Scripture tells of two incidents.⁶ One, the death of Miriam. Two, the death of Aaron and Moses and their failure to enter the land.⁷ It begins by telling the cause of the latter.

footnotes:
⁶ That happened in Kadesh.
⁷ I.E. considers this one incident, for the latter was dependent upon the former.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:3:1)


**וירב.** מבנין הפעיל:


AND THE PEOPLE STROVE. *Va-yarev* (strove) is a *hifil*.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:3:2)


**בגוע אחינו.** שם הפעל כמו כשכב אדני המלך:


WHEN OUR BRETHREN PERISHED. *Bi-geva* (when…perished) is an infinitive. It is similar to *ki-shekav* (when…shall sleep) in *when my lord the king shall sleep with his fathers* (I Kings 1:21).


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:3:3)


**אחינו.** הם דור המדבר שמתו והם עבדי השם:


OUR BRETHREN. The generation that died in the desert. They were servants of the Lord.⁸. Why add, *before the Lord*? According to I.E., *before the Lord* indicates that they worshipped the Lord.

footnotes:
⁸ Scripture states, our brethren perished



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:4:1)


**ולמה הבאתם.** ידבר למשה ולאהרן כי כן כתוב ויקהלו על משה ועל אהרן:


AND WHY HAVE YE BROUGHT. This was addressed to Moses and Aaron, for Scripture goes on to say, *and they assembled themselves together against Moses and against Aaron* (v. 2).


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:4:2)


וטעם **וירב העם עם משה.** שהמריבה היתה עם משה חזקה:


Scripture reads, *And the people strove with Moses*, (v. 3) because their quarrel with Moses was more intense.⁹

footnotes:
⁹ Than their quarrel with Aaron.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:5:1)


**העליתנו.** מלה זרה:


HAVE YE MADE US TO COME UP. *He’elitunu* (have ye made us to come up) is irregular.¹⁰

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:6:1)


**ויבא משה ואהרן מפני הקהל.** כדמות בורחים:


AND MOSES AND AARON WENT¹¹ FROM THE PRESENCE OF THE ASSEMBLY. Like those who flee.¹² (mi-pene) *of the assembly*. I.E. believes that the latter indicates that they fled.

¹¹ Hebrew, va-yavo’u. This literally means, and they came.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:6:2)

### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:8:1)


**קח את המטה.** יש בכאן פירושים רבים יש בדברי יחיד בעבור שאמר לישראל שמעו נא המורים והם בני אברהם יצחק ויעקב ואילו היה כן למה אמר להם עוד ממרים הייתם ואחרים אמרו כי מלת ודברתם כמו והכיתם וכמוהו ותדבר את כל זרע המלוכה ואין זה נכון כי המלה מגזרת דבר או מן ידבר עמים תחתנו והנה פי' ותדבר כמו ותאבד וכן בספר השני והנה פירוש ודברתם אל הסלע ואבדתם ועוד אם כן הפירוש למה נענש משה גם הם השיבו בעבור שהכה פעמים אם כן למה נענש אהרן ויאמר רבי משה הדרשן ז"ל הספרדי יש אותות נעשות בדבור ויש בפועל ודבור כמו מלת אלישע והשם צוה שיקח המטה להכות בסלע כמשפט הצור והוסיף מלת ודברתם להוציא המים במכה ובדבור ובעבור שהכעיסו ישראל אמר להם המן הסלע הזה נוציא לכם מים והיתה דעתו כי אין יכולת בנו להוציא מים מהסלע כי אם בכח השם והנה לא פירש דבורו היטב וחשבו אנשים בלבם כי דבורו שלא יוכל השם להוציא מים מן הסלע וזה טעם אשר לא קדשתם אותי והביא ראיה מדברי המשורר שאמר כי המרו את רוחו ויבטא בשפתיו והנה החטא היה בבטואו לא במכה גם זה איננו נכון כי משה אמר זה ולמה נענש אהרן ועוד כי אין במעשה זכר דבור והראיה שהביא איננה ראי' כי אין פי' כי המרו את רוחו כי אם אל השם וכן כתוב והמה מרו ועצבו את רוח קדשו וזה פירוש ויקציפו על מי מריבה והטעם שהקציפו השם וכן כתוב המה מי מריבה אשר רבו בני ישראל על ה' וירע למשה בעבורם כי המרו את רוח השם ויגזור על משה שלא יכנס לארץ. ואחרים אמרו כי הדבור אל הסלע שאיננו שומע איננה כי אם במכה ואם כן למה נענש משה. ואחרים אמרו בעבור שלא אמרו שירה כמו עלי באר ענו לה וזה טעם אשר לא קדשתם והאחרים אמרו כי השם צוה שידברו והם לא דברו רק הכה משה על כן נענשו שניהם ונאמר להם מעלתם מריתם לא האמנתם לא קדשתם. ואנשי שקול הדעת אמרו שלא יתכן שיהיה שליח השם ימיר דבור השם ואם הוא המיר איך נאמין בתורתו גם אלה לא דברו נכונה כי אילו היה מחליף במצוה מיד היה נענש כי הנה נענש על דבר שאינו מצוה לעולם ולא תורה לישראל ולא נעשה בזדון רק בשגגה בעבור שהכעיסוהו ישראל וכן אמר גם בי התאנף ה' בגללכם ואחרים אמרו כי ישראל אמרו שיוציא מסלע אחר וראיתם המן הסלע הזה ומשה פחד להחליף דבור השם ובעבור שלא האמין להוציא מים מן הסלע שאמרו על כן נענש וזה טעם לא האמנתם בי גם זה הפירוש איננו נכון כי הכתוב אמר מריתם את פי והנה לא מרו. והפירוש הנכון בעיני אגלנו ברמיזות דע כי כאשר ידע החלק את הכל ידבק בכל ויחדש בכל אותות ומופתים ואמת כי השם אמר למשה ולאהרן ודברתם ולא דברו בעבור מריבת העם עם משה והנה החלק חלק והכה הסלע ולא יצאו מים עד שהכהו פעם שנית והנה לא קדשו השם ומרו ומעלו בשגגה גם יוכל המפרש לפרש ויבטא בשפתיו על משה כי על כן נענש כי לא היה ראוי שידבר דבר עד שימלא שליחות השם גם יהיה דרש קדמונינו ז"ל כי החטא היה בעבור שאמר שמעו נא המורים ורמזו זה הסוד:


TAKE THE ROD. Many interpretations are offered for this incident.¹³ There is an individual opinion that Moses sinned because he said to Israel, who are the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: *Hear now, ye rebels* (v. 10). However, if this were the case why did he again say,¹⁴ *ye have been rebellious against the Lord* (Deut. 9:7). Others say that the word *ve-dibbartem* (and speak ye) has the meaning, and ye shall strike. It is similar to the word *va-tedabber* (and destroyed) in *and destroyed all the seed royal* (II Chron. 22:10). However, this is incorrect, for *va-tedabber* is related to the word *dever* (destruction) or to the word *yadber* (he subdueth) in *He subdueth peoples under us* (Ps. 47:4). *Va-tedabber*¹⁵ thus means, and destroyed. Indeed, it so reads in the other book.¹⁶ (va-te’abbed) *all the seed royal* (II Kings 11:1). The meaning of *ve-dibbartem el ha-sela* (and speak ye unto the rock) thus is,¹⁷ and ye shall destroy the rock.¹⁸ Furthermore, if this is the meaning of the word,¹⁹ means, and you shall strike. why was Moses punished? The above commentaries answer, because he hit the rock twice. However, if this is the case why was Aaron punished?²⁰ Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen the Spaniard, of blessed memory, says that some signs²¹ are performed by word of mouth, others by action and speech, as in the case of the salt²² (the incident of). which Elisha cast into the water.²³ (Elisha) *went forth unto the spring of the waters, and cast salt therein, and said, Thus saith the Lord: I have healed these waters; there shall be not be from thence any more death or miscarrying*, (II Kings 2:21). God commanded Moses to take the staff and strike the rock as he did in the case of the rock [at Horeb].²⁴ He added the word *ve-dibbartem* (and speak ye)²⁵ so that the water would flow via the speech and the blow. Because Israel angered him, Moses said, are we to bring you forth water from the rock? What Moses meant²⁶? was, we do not have the power to bring water out of the rock. We can only do so by the power of God. Now Moses did not make himself clear. People thought what he said was that God cannot bring water out of the rock. This is the meaning of *because ye sanctified Me not in the midst of the children of Israel* (Deut. 32:51). Rabbi Moses offered proof from the words of the poet who said, *For they embittered his spirit, And he spoke rashly with his lip* (Ps. 106:33). The sin was thus in his expressing, not by striking [the rock]. However, this too is incorrect, for Moses said, *are we to bring you forth water out of this rock* (v. 10). Why was Aaron punished?²⁷ Furthermore, no speech is mentioned in the Torah’s description of the act of striking the rock.²⁸ The proof offered²⁹ by Rabbi Moses is no proof because the meaning of *For they embittered his spirit* is that they embittered God’s spirit. Scripture similarly writes, *But they rebelled, and grieved His holy spirit* (Is. 63:10). This is the meaning of *They angered Him also at the waters of Meribah* (Ps. 106:32). It means they angered God.³⁰ Scripture similarly states, *These are the waters of Meribah, where the children of Israel strove with the Lord* (Num. 20:13).³¹, refers to God. Scripture says, *And it went ill with Moses because of them* (Ps. 106:32) because they embittered God’s spirit, and He decreed that Moses not enter the land.³² Others say that the meaning of speak to the rock can only mean strike the rock, for a rock cannot hear.³³ Now if this is so, why was Moses punished?³⁴ Some say that Moses and Aaron were punished because they did not sing a song of praise³⁵ as in *Spring up, O well-sing ye unto it* (Num. 21:17). They say that this is the meaning of *because ye sanctified Me not* (Deut. 32:51).³⁶ Others say that God commanded Moses and Aaron to speak to the rock, but they did not speak to it. On the contrary, Moses struck the rock.³⁷ Therefore they were both punished and they were told, *ye trespassed* (Deut. 32:51); *ye rebelled* (v. 24); *ye believed not in Me* (v. 12), and *ye sanctified Me not* (Deut. 32:52). Those who are guided by reason³⁸ say that it is impossible that a messenger of God would alter God’s word.³⁹ If Moses transformed God’s word, how can we believe his Torah?⁴⁰ However, the aforementioned⁴¹ also spoke incorrectly, for if Moses had altered a commandment he would have been punished immediately.⁴² Look, Moses was punished with regard to something which was not an eternal commandment and not a law given to Israel. Nor did he knowingly violate God’s command. He only did so inadvertently because Israel angered him. Moses clearly said, *Also the Lord was angry with me for your sakes* (Deut. 1:*37)*.⁴³ Others say that Israel told Moses⁴⁴ to bring water out of a different rock.⁴⁵ They offer *this rock* as proof (v. 10).⁴⁶? implies that we cannot bring water out of this rock, but we can out of another, that is, the rock about which God commanded us. However, Moses was afraid to alter God’s word.⁴⁷ Moses was punished because he did not believe that he would be able to bring forth water from the rock that Israel chose. He was therefore punished.⁴⁸ This is the meaning of *ye believed not in Me* (v. 12). This interpretation is also incorrect, for Scripture states, *ye rebelled against My word* (v. 24). However, they did not rebel.⁴⁹I will reveal in hints the explanation which appears correct to me. Know, when the part⁵⁰ knows the All,⁵¹ he cleaves to the All and creates signs and wonders with the help of the All.⁵² Now it is true that God told Moses and Aaron, *speak ye unto the rock*. They did not speak to the rock because the people were quarreling with Moses. The “part” thus remained a “part.”⁵³ He struck the rock, and water did not come out of it⁵⁴ until he struck it a second time.⁵⁵ Moses and Aaron thus did not sanctify God’s name. They inadvertently rebelled and trespassed. It is also possible to explain that *And he spoke rashly with his lips* (Ps. 106:33) refers to Moses.⁵⁶ It was unseemly for Moses to say anything⁵⁷, etc. (v. 10). before fulfilling God’s command. Moses was therefore punished. The midrashic interpretation of our ancients, of blessed memory, who said that Moses sinned because he said, *Hear now, ye rebels* (v. 10) is also in keeping with this interpretation. The rabbis hint at this secret.

**אל הסלע.** שהודעתיך או הנמצא סמוך למחנה:


UNTO THE ROCK. Which I pointed out to you or which is found close to the camp.⁵⁸ rock and not of *a* rock.

⁵⁸ Hence Scripture speaks of the


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:8:3)


**ונתן מימיו.** בעבור מימיו טעו רבים ואמרו כי זה הסלע הוא הצור ואלה עורי לב כי הצור הוא בחורב וזה הסלע היה בקצה ארץ אדום כי בקדש היה גם יתכן לפרש מימיו המים שאתן בו:


THAT IT GIVE FORTH ITS WATER. Many erred and said that the rock is to be identified with the stone [at Horeb]⁵⁹ because Scripture reads, *its* water.⁶⁰ water indicates that the stone had already produced water. See Bahya and *Da’at zekenim mi-ba’ale ha-tosafot*. However, they cannot think straight. The stone was in Horeb and this rock was at the border of the land of Edom, for it was in Kadesh.⁶¹ It is also possible to interpret *its water* as meaning, the water which I will place in it.

### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:12:1)


**יען לא האמנתם בי.** היא הסוד שרמזתי שלא נקדש השם על ידם:


BECAUSE YE BELIEVED NOT IN ME. This alludes to the secret at which I hinted, i.e., that God’s name was not sanctified through them.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:13:1)


**ויקדש בם.** במשה ואהרן כטעם בקרובי אקדש:


AND HE WAS SANCTIFIED IN THEM. Through Moses and Aaron.⁶⁴ (in them) does not refer to the water. Our verse has the same meaning as *Through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified* (Lev. 10:3).⁶⁵

### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:14:1)


**מקדש.** שם מקום עיר ואיננו קדש ברנע כי אותו הוא מדבר וכן הכתוב אומר יחיל ה' מדבר קדש:


FROM KADESH. Kadesh is the name of a place where a city is located. It is not to be identified with Kadesh-barnea,⁶⁶ for the latter was a wilderness.⁶⁷ Thus Scripture reads, *The Lord shaketh the wilderness of Kadesh* (Ps. 29:8).⁶⁸

### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:16:1)


**וישלח מלאך.** כמשמעו וכן הכתוב אומר ומלאך פניו הושיעם ורבים פירשוהו על משה כי מצאו ויאמר חגי מלאך ה' ואין זאת דעתי:


AND SENT AN ANGEL.⁷¹. The word *malakh* can be rendered as messenger or angel. Hence I.E.’s comment. This is to be taken literally. Scripture similarly states, *And the angel of His presence saved them* (Is. 63:9). Many said that the reference is to Moses⁷² for they found *Then spoke Haggai the Lord’s messenger* (malakh)⁷³. (Haggai 1:13). However, this is not my opinion.

⁷¹ Hebrew, malakh
⁷² See Rashi.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:17:2)


**דרך המלך נלך.** אם הדרך שהמלך הולך בה או פירושו הדרך שיצוה המלך שהוא מלך אדום נלך:


WE WILL GO ALONG THE KING’S HIGHWAY. The major highway upon which the king travels. Or its meaning is, the road that the king, namely, the king of Edom, will command us to travel in.⁷⁴

footnotes:
⁷⁴ According to this interpretation the meaning of our verse is: we will go on any road which you the king will choose for us to travel on.



### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:19:1)


**במסלה נעלה.** מה יזיקכם שנעלה במסלה ואם הוצרכו למים תמכרום לנו וזה טעם מכרם כמו דמיהם:


WE WILL GO UP BY THE HIGHWAY. What harm will it cause you if we up by the highway? If we need water you will sell it to us. This is the meaning of *mikhram* (v. 19). It means the price thereof.



### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 20:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/20:22:1)


וטעם **בני ישראל כל העד'.** בעבור שיצא אדום להלחם בם הגיד הכתוב שלא נפקד איש מבני ישראל בבואם מעיר אדום אל הר ההר:


[THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.] Its meaning is, *the entire congregation*. Because Edom went to fight against them, Scripture relates that no one was missing from the children of Israel when they came from the city of Edom to Mount Hor.⁷⁵

**וישמע הכנעני מלך ערד.** אמרו הקדמונים שהוא סיחון ונקרא הכנעני כי כל אמורי כנעני ורבים אמרו כי זאת הפרשה יהושע כתבה והראיה מלך ערד אחד ומצאו שבני יהודה קראו שם המקום חרמה ולא אמרו כלום כי אותו המקום יקרא בתחלה צפת וזה מלך ערד והאמת שני מקומות ורבים במקרא כמו הם ומלך ערד על פשוטו הוא מעבר לירדן מזרחה ונסמכה זאת הפרשה למות אהרן כי הכתוב ספר מה שאירע בהר ההר קודם נסעם משם והעד וישמע הכנעני מלך ערד ואחריו ויסעו מהר ההר ואם תבקש מה שמע הנה מפורש:


AND THE CANAANITE, THE KING OF ARAD. The ancients¹ said he² 3a: “Sihon, Arad, and Canaan are one and the same.” is Sihon. He is called a Canaanite, for all Amorites are Canaanites.³ Many say that Joshua wrote this section.⁴ *The king of Arad, one* (Josh. 12:14) is proof of this.⁵ They also found that Scripture states that the children of Judah called the name of the place Hormah.⁶ However, they are wrong, for that place⁷ was originally called Zephath⁸. while the place spoken of in our verse was ruled by the king of Arad.⁹ In reality they are two places.¹⁰ There are many such instances in Scripture.¹¹ According to the plain meaning of the text the king of Arad ruled over the eastern bank of the Jordan.¹² This portion¹³ was connected to the death of Aaron, because Scripture relates what happened on Mount Hor¹⁴ before they [Israel] journeyed from there. *And the Canaanite, the king of Arad… heard…and they journeyed from mount Hor* (v. 4) is proof of this.¹⁵ If you want to find what the king of Arad heard, observe, it is clearly stated.¹⁶ (v. 1).

**על נס** שיהיה גבוה ויראו אותו הכל ורבים השתבשו ואמרו כי זאת הצורה לקבל כח עליונים וחליל' חלילה כי הדבר נעשה בצווי השם ואין לנו לחפש למה צורת נחש ואם לא כן יראנו היש עץ שימתיק המים המרים אפי' הדבש לא ימתיקם ומה טעם לשום דבלת תאנים על השחין ואין בתולדת הדבלה להסיר השחין והאמת כי נשגבה ממנו דעת עליון:


AND SET IT UPON A POLE. So that it be on a high place and everyone will be able to see it. Many err. They say that this was an image that had the capability of receiving powers from on high.²⁴ Far be it, far be it [for one to believe such a thing], for this thing was made by God’s command.²⁵ We should not investigate why Moses was commanded to make the form of a snake.²⁶ Should someone disagree,²⁷ let him show us if there is a tree that makes bitter waters sweet.²⁸ Even honey will not sweeten them.²⁹ What reason was there to put a cake of figs upon a boil?³⁰ It is not in the nature of figs to remove boils. The truth is that the mind of the Almighty is beyond us.

It is found⁴³ only in place of a *yod*. Compare, *valed* (child) (II Sam. 6:23).⁴⁴. The explanation of the Aramaic translation is known.⁴⁵ (Suphah) as *yama de-suf* (the sea of reeds).

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:18:1)


**כרוה נדיבי העם.** כפול כמשפט:


WHICH THE NOBLES OF THE PEOPLE DELVED. Scripture repeats itself,⁶⁰ repeats *which the princes digged*. as is its style.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 21:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:18:2)


**במחוקק.** ע"י מחוקקים כמו לבי לחוקקי ישראל וזו הבאר היתה במדבר רחוק מהיישוב ומזה המדבר נסעו אל מתנה ומשם אל נחליאל ודע כי אשד הנחלים והמדבר הנקרא באר ומתנה ונחליאל כולם מקומות ויש להם שם כלל והוא עלמון דבלתימה כי כן כתוב בפרשת אלה מסעי או אלה שמות מקומות עברו עליהם במסע אחר והרי העברים לפני נבו הוא הבמות והגיא אשר בשדה מואב והעד שאמר הכתוב כי מהגיא נסעו אל ערבות מואב בעבר לירדן ירחו וכתיב כי מהר העברים נסעו אל ערבות מואב על ירדן ירחו ועוד ונשב בגיא מול בית פעור עת שהתחננתי ובמקום אחר עלה אל הר העברים הר נבו גם ויקבוד אותו בגיא ושם כתוב ויעל משה מערבות מואב אל הר נבו והנה הגיא הוא ראש הפסגה ושם מת משה ואין צורך להוליכו אחר מותו:


WITH THE SCEPTRE. The meaning of *bi-mechokek* (with the sceptre) is, by the governors.⁶¹ means by. The *bet* usually has the meaning of in. Hence I.E.’s comment. Compare, *My heart is toward the governors* (chokeke) *of Israel* (Jud. 5:9). This well was in the wilderness, far from an inhabited place. From this wilderness Israel journeyed to Mattanah. From Mattanah they journeyed to Nahaliel. Note that *eshed ha-nehalim* (the slope of the valleys) and the wilderness which is called Beer and Mattanah and Nahaliel are all names of places. They are also referred to by a general name, *viz.*, *Almon-diblathiam* (Num. 33:46), which is found in the Torah portion *Ve-Elleh Mase* (*Ibid.*).⁶² (the slope of the valleys), Beer, Mattanah, and Nahaliel are not mentioned there. *Almon-diblathiam* is. Hence I.E.’s comment. On the other hand, it is also possible that these are the names of places that the Israelites passed over in another journey.⁶³ The mountains of Abarim in front of Nebo (Num. 33:47) are to be identified with Bamoth and the valley that is in the field of Moab (v. 20). The following is proof of this. Scripture states that Israel journeyed from the valley⁶⁴ to the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho (Num. 22:1).⁶⁵ It also states that Israel journeyed from the mountains of Abarim to the plains of Moab beyond the Jordon at Jericho (Num. 33:48). It further states, *So we abode in the valley*⁶⁶ *over against Beth-peor* (Deut. 3:29) at the time that I [Moses] pleaded [with God].⁶⁷ Scripture elsewhere states, *Get thee up into this mountain of Abarim, unto mount Nebo* (Deut. 32:49).⁶⁸ Scripture also states, *and he was buried in the valley* (Deut. 34:6). The Torah there states, *And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto mount Nebo* to the top of Pisgah (Deut. 34:1). The valley was thus at the top of Pisgah. Moses died there, and there was no need to move him after his death.⁶⁹

⁶³ Hence they are not recorded in Num. 33:46.

⁶⁵ I.E. connects Num. 22:1 to Num. 21:10.
⁶⁶ Which is in the field of Moab.
⁶⁷ To allow him to enter Canaan. This was shortly before Moses’ death.
⁶⁸ We thus see that Moses went up to Mount Nebo from the valley which is the field of Moab.
⁶⁹ As would be the case if the “valley” where Moses died was not at the top of the mountain. According to I.E. the “valley” was an indentation at the top of the mountain.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 21:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:24:2)


**עד בני עמון.** כי כתוב כי חצי ארץ בני עמון היתה לישראל כי לקחוהו מיד האמורי שלקחו בתחלה מיד בני עמון והכתוב אמר על מואב ועמון שלא יתן השם מארצם לישראל עד מדרך כף רגל והטעם הארץ שהיתה בידם בעת ההיא על כן הוצרך הכתוב לאמר דברי המושלים בעבור חשבון שישבו שם ישראל כי כן כתוב וישב ישראל בכל ערי האמורי בחשבון:


EVEN UNTO THE CHILDREN OF AMMON. Scripture records that half of the land of Ammon belonged to the children of Israel,⁷² for they⁷³ took it from the Amorites who originally took it from the children of Ammon. Now Scripture tells us that God would not give the Israelites even the size of a footstep from any of the land belonging to the Ammonites and Moabites. The reference is to the land which Ammon and Moab possessed at that time.⁷⁴ Scripture therefore had to record the words of the poets.⁷⁵ It did so because Israel lived in Heshbon.⁷⁶ The Torah explicitly states, *And Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorite, in Heshbon*⁷⁷ (v. 25).

### Verse 30

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 21:30:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:30:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:30:1)


**ונירם.** דברי משה והמ"ם סימן מלך אמורי וגדודיו ולו שני פירושים. האחד מגזירת ניר ותהיה מלת ונירם מושכת עצמה ואחרת עמה כמו והנבואה עודד הנביא וכן הוא ונירם אבד ניר חשבון ותהיה מלת ונירם כמו בתוך האהלי הערכך וכן הוא והניר שלהם אבד שהוא ניר חשבון. והפירוש השני שתהיה מלת ונירם מגזרת ירה ויור אשר יריתי והטעם כאשר ירינו אותם אבד חשבון:


WE HAVE SHOT THEM. These are the words of Moses.⁸⁷ The *mem* of *va-niram*⁸⁸ (we shot at them) refers to the king of the Amorites and his troops. It has two interpretations. One, that *va-niram* is related to the word *nir* (kingship). It⁸⁹. is to be read as if written twice.⁹⁰ (we have shot at them—Heshbon is perished), is to be read, *va-niram avad nir cheshbon* (and their king, the king of Heshbon, was destroyed). It is like *even the prophecy, Oded the prophet* (II Chron. 15:8).⁹¹ Our verse means, and their king the king of Heshbon was destroyed. *Va-niram* is similar to the word *ha-oholi* (my tent) in *in the midst of my tent* (Josh. 7:21), and to *ha-erkekha* (thy valuation) (Lev. 27:23).⁹² beneath the *vav* is the sign of the direct object. In other words, *va-niram* is short for *ve-ha-niram*. Thus *va-niram* is similar to *ha-oholi* and *ha-erkekha* in that both words are written with the direct object even though they have suffixes. Words with suffixes usually do not come with the direct object. Hence I.E.’s comment. *Va-niram avad cheshbon* (we have shot at them—Heshbon is perished) means, their king, that is, the king of Heshbon, perished. Second, that *va-niram* is related to *yereh va-yor* (shoot; and he shot) (II Kings 13:17) and *yariti* (cast)⁹³ (Gen. 31:51). It means,⁹⁴ (we have shot at them–Heshbon is perished). when we shot them Heshbon was destroyed.

⁹¹ Which is to be read as if written, even the prophecy, the prophecy of Oded the prophet. See I.E. on Gen. 6:13 (Vol. 1, p. 100) and the notes thereto.
⁹² The pattach
⁹³ Translated literally.
⁹⁴ Va-niram avad heshbon


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 21:30:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:30:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/21:30:2)


**ונשים.** מפעלי הכפל והחיר"ק תחת קמ"ץ קטן כמו ויסב אלהים את העם ויאמר רבי משה הכהן כי הדגשות לחסרון האל"ף כאל"ף מלפנו מבהמות ארץ מגזרת תאשם שומרון וי"א כי חשבון היתה עיר סיחון לעולם וטעם בואו חשבון דברי המושלים למואבים הבאים בשבי אל חשבון כי אש יצאה מחשבון משל למחנות סיחון וכאשר ירינום דברי המושלים על לשון המואבים חשבנו כי תאבד חשבון ונעשה שממה כל הארץ עד נופח או הם דברי משה הדרשן:


AND WE HAVE LAID WASTE. *Va-nashim* comes from a double root.⁹⁵. It comes from the root *shin, mem, mem*. The *chirik* is in place of a short *kamatz*.⁹⁶. In other words, the word should have been vocalized *va-nashem*. Compare, *va-yasev* (led about) in *But God led the people about* (Ex. 13:18).⁹⁷. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that the *dagesh* in the *shin* of *va-nashim* compensates for a missing *alef*.⁹⁸ comes from the root *alef, shin, mem* (guilty). Compare, *Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth* (Job. 35:11) wherein an *alef* is missing in the word *mallefenu* (teacheth us).⁹⁹. The word *va-nashim* is related to the word *tesham*¹⁰⁰. (shall bear her guilt) in *Samaria shall bear her guilt* (Hos. 14:1). Some say that Heshbon was always the city of Sihon.¹⁰¹ In this case, *Come ye to Heshbon* (v. 27) is the line that the poets directed at the Moabites who came as captive to Heshbon. And *for a fire is gone out of Heshbon* is a metaphor for the army of Sihon. When the poets speak on behalf of the Moabites, they say, we thought that Heshbon will be destroyed¹⁰² and the entire land will be laid waste even unto Nophah. Or these¹⁰³ (v. 30). are the words of Moses.

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 22:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:2:1)


**לאמורי.** בקמצות הלמ"ד והטעם לידוע שהוא סיחון ועוג ולא הי' במלכי כנען גדולים כאלה והעד אשר כגובה ארזים גבהו:


TO THE AMORITES. The *lamed* prefixed to the word *emori* (Amorite) is vocalized with a *kamatz*.¹ so vocalized indicates the definite article. Its reference is to the famous Amorites Sihon and Og. There were no kings among the Canaanites as great as they. *Whose height was like the height of the cedars* (Amos 2:9) is proof of this.² [Sihon and Og] *before them, Whose height was like the height of the cedars* (Amos 2:9).

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 22:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:6:1)


**ארה לי.** לשון צווי מפעלי הכפל בחסרון אות הכפל וכן קבה לי והנה קוב על משקל שמור וקבה לי בחסרון הה"א על דרך משקל שכב רכב צלח:


CURSE ME. The word *arah* (curse) is an imperative. It comes from a double root with one of the double letters missing. The same is true of with the word *kavah* (curse) in curse me (v. 18). The word *kov* (curse) is vocalized according to the paradigm of *shemor* (keep).¹⁴. *Kavah*¹⁵ is an elongated form of *kav*. in *kavah li* (curse me) minus the *heh*¹⁶. follows the paradigm of *shechav* (lie), *rekhav* (ride), and *tzelach* (rested on).¹⁷.

THAT WE MAY SMITE THEM. *Nakkeh* (that we may smite them)¹⁸. is an infinitive. The fact that it ends in a *heh* is no argument against the latter,¹⁹ changes to a *tav* in the infinitive in words ending in a *heh*. Thus our word should have read *le-nakkot*. Hence I.E.’s comment. for the word *le-khalle*²⁰. (to finish), in *to finish the transgression* (Dan. 9:24) is similar.²¹ rather than the more usual form *le-khallot*.

**יואר.** הוי"ו הנח הנעלם תחת הדגש שהוא תחת אות הכפל כמו על כמון יושב ולא היה כמוהו מאותו בנין בעבור אות הגרון כמשפט:


IS CURSED. The silent *vav of yu’ar* (is cursed) is in place of a *dagesh*, which is in place of the missing double letter.²² is *alef, resh, resh. Yu’ar* is spelled with only one *resh*. Compare, *yusav*²³ and *yu’ar* are both *pu’als*. (turned about)²⁴ comes from the root *samekh, bet, bet*. **וקסמים בידם.** אמר רבי שמואל הנגיד הספרדי ז"ל שטעמו ודמי הקסמים וראיתי מבידם ולא אמר כלום רק הוא כמשמעו וספר הכתוב ששלח אל קוסם קוסמים כמוהו ועוד שלא יוכל להתעכב לאמר לא אמצא יום נבחר ושעה נבחרת ללכת ולקוב כי הם אנשי אומנותו והעד שפירושו כאשר הוא שאמר הכתוב בימינו היה הקסם:


WITH THE REWARDS OF DIVINATION IN THEIR HAND. Rabbi Samuel Ha-Nagid the Sephardi, of blessed memory, said that the meaning of *u-kesamim* (with the reward of divination)²⁷ is payment for divination. He offers as proof the word *be-yadam* (in their hand).²⁸ refers to the money which they brought with them for the divination. However, he says nothing. *U-kesamim be-yadam* is to be taken literally.²⁹ Scripture tells us that Balak sent diviners like himself to the diviner [Balaam]. Furthermore, Balaam would not be able to tarry, saying, “I can not find a propitious day, and a propitious hour to go and curse,” for the messengers were members of his guild. *In his right hand is the instrument of divination*³⁰ (ha-kesom) (Ez. 21:27) is proof that *u-kesamim be-yadam* is to be taken literally.³¹

### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 22:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:13:1)


**שרי בלק.** ולא הזכיר זקני מדין כי בלק הוא העיקר והוא השולח אליו אמר ר' משה הכהן הספרדי ז"ל כי אף על פי שסימן הפועל ביו"ד לא יתכן להיותו כי אם בנו"ן כמו הלהרגני לא יאמר הלהרגי והנה שכח לתתי להלך עמכם לא אבה יבמי ור' יונה המדקדק אמר כי היו"ד נוסף ואיננו נכון:


THE PRINCES OF BALAK. Scripture does not mention the elders of Midian,³⁶ for Balak was the protagonist and he sent the messengers to Balaam. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen the Spaniard, of blessed memory, says that even though the *yod* is the sign of the object³⁷ (give me). it can only come with a *nun*.³⁸ has to be added to the verb in order to indicate the object. Compare, *ha-lehorgeni* (thinkest thou to kill me) (Ex. 2:14). It does not read *ha-lehorgi*. However, he forgot *le-titti* (to give me) in *to give me leave to go with you* [our verse] and *yabbemi* (perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto me) in *he will not perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto me* (Deut. 25:7).³⁹ alone. Rabbi Jonah the grammarian says that the *yod* of *le-titti*⁴⁰ means the same as *la-tet*. It means to give, not to give me. is superfluous, but what he says is incorrect.⁴¹ does not mean that the object (me) is missing.

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 22:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:19:1)


**בזה.** במקום הזה אמר הגאון ז"ל אם יטעון טוען ויאמר אחר שאמר השם לא תלך עמהם איך אמר קום לך אתם יש להשיב כי השם לא רצה שילך עם האנשים הראשונים עד שיבואו שרים נכבדים מהם ולפי דעתי אין צורך רק טעמו כטעם שלח לך אנשים כי השם אמר לישראל עלה רש והם לא האמינו רק אמרו נשלחה אנשים לפנינו אז שאל משה את השם ואמר לו שלח לך אנשים ואחר שאמר השם לבלעם לא תאור את העם מה צורך היה לו לומר ואדעה מה יוסף ה' דבר רק חשב בלבו מחשבה רעה והשם אמר לו לך עם האנשים רק השמר לך שלא תדבר רק מה שאומר לך והעד על פירושי ויחר אף אלהים כי הולך הוא:


HERE.⁵⁵, literally means in this. Hence I.E.’s comment. In this place. The Gaon, of blessed memory,⁵⁶ says: Should someone argue and say, “How could God tell Balaam rise up, *go with them* (v. 20) after telling him *Thou shalt not go with them* (12)?”⁵⁷ Then we can answer him that God did not want Balaam to go with these messengers but to wait until Balak sent messengers more honorable than they. However, I believe that there is no need for the Gaon’s interpretation. Its meaning is similar to God telling Israel, *Send thou men* (Num. 13:2) and *go up, take possession* (Deut. 1:21). Israel did not believe.⁵⁸ On the contrary, they said, *Let us send men before us* (Deut. 1:22). Moses then asked God.⁵⁹ God told him, *Send thou men* (Num. 13:2).⁶⁰ Now after God told Balaam, *thou shalt not curse the people* (v. 12), what need did Balaam have to say, *that I may know what the Lord will speak unto me more* (v. 19)? Balaam had an evil thought in his heart. God told him go with the men, but take care that you do not say anything save that which I will tell you. *And God’s anger was kindled because he went* (v. 22) is proof that my explanation is correct.⁶¹

### Verse 28

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 22:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:28:1)


**ויפתח ה'.** אחז"ל שי' דברים נבראו בערב שבת בין השמשות ולפי דעתי שהטעם שגזר השם לחדש באותות האלה שהם חוץ לתולדות ויאמר הגאון כי לא דברה האתון ורב שמואל בן חפני תפסו ורב שמואל הספרדי בעל השירים חשב להציל הנתפס ודע כי אנשי שקול הדעת הוצרכו להוציא הדברים ממשמעם כי אמדו שהשם לא יחדש אות בעולם לשנות המנהג שברא רק להצדיק נביאו ולא אמרו אמת כי הנה חנניה מישאל ועזריה נעשה להם אות ולא היו נביאים ויש מהם אומרים כי בלעם נביא היה והאמת כי נבואתו היתה בעבור כבוד ישראל כי קוסם היה וכן קראו הכתוב ויש אומרים כי היה יודע דעת עליונים לקבל כחם למטה בצורות וזה טעם ואשר תאור יואר והנכון בעיני כי היה יודע מזלות ובעת ראותו במזל של שום אדם שהגיע עת רעתו היה מקלל אותו ובבא הרעה אל המקולל יחשבו הרואים והשומעים הנמצאים כי בעבור קללתו באה הרעה והעד שדבר במרמה עם שרי בלק וזה טעם לא אוכל לעבור את פי ה' אלהי כי אין יכולת בנוצר לשנות מעשה היוצר או גזרתו והסוד כי החלק לא ישנה החלק רק גזירות הכל תשנה גזירת החלק ולא אוכל לגלות זה הסוד כי עמוק הוא והישר כי האתון דברה ואם תבין סוד מלאכי אברהם גם יעקב אז תבין האמת:


AND THE LORD OPENED THE MOUTH OF THE ASS. The rabbis, of blessed memory, said that ten things were created on Sabbath eve at twilight.⁷² 5:6. I believe that this means that God specifically decreed the creation of these miraculous phenomena,⁷³ 5:6. for they are beyond the laws of nature.⁷⁴ 5:6. The Gaon⁷⁵ says that the ass did not speak. Rabbi Samuel the son of Hofni attacked the Gaon.⁷⁶ However, Rabbi Samuel the Spanish poet tried to save the one who was attacked.⁷⁷ Note, the rationalists had a need for a non-literal interpretation of our text, for they said that God would not create signs in the world to change the laws which he created.⁷⁸ He would do so only to justify his prophet.⁷⁹ However, they did not speak the truth, for, look, a miracle was done for Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, who were not prophets.⁸⁰ Some of them⁸¹ say that Balaam was a prophet.⁸² However, the truth is that his prophecy⁸³ was because of Israel’s glory, for Balaam was a diviner. Indeed, this is how Scripture refers to him.⁸⁴ (Josh. 13:22). Some say that Balaam knew the mind of the heavenly beings and was able to channel them by images that he made.⁸⁵ This is the meaning of *and he whom thou cursest is cursed* (v. 6). However, it appears to me that Balaam was an astrologer. When Balaam saw in the star of a given person that an evil time had befallen him, he would curse him. When evil befell the one whom he cursed, then those who witnessed and heard the imprecation thought that the evil came because of Balaam’s curse. The fact that Balaam spoke with guile to the lords of Balak is proof of this.⁸⁶ The meaning of *I can not go beyond the word of the Lord my God* (v. 18) is, it is not in the hand of any created being to change a deed or a decree of God. The secret is, the part⁸⁷ can not change a part.⁸⁸ It is only the decree of the All⁸⁹ which can change the decree of the part.⁹⁰ I cannot reveal this secret for it is very deep. The correct interpretation is, the ass spoke. If you understand the secret of the angels of Abraham⁹¹ and of Jacob,⁹² then you will understand the truth.⁹³

### Verse 32

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 22:32:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:32:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/22:32:1)


**כי ירט.** הטעם עוות וכן על ידי רשעים ירטני שהוא מן רטה שאילו היה מן ירט היה ראוי להיות כמו יעטני ואם הם שני שרשים וכמוהו מעיל צדקה יעטני שהוא על משקל אשר יעצני כמו עוטה אור:


BECAUSE THY WAY IS CONTRARY UNTO ME. The meaning of *yarat* (contrary) is perverse.¹⁰³ The word *yirteni* (twists me) in *And twists me by the hands of the wicked*¹⁰⁴ (Job 16:11), which comes from the root *resh, tet, heh*, is similar.¹⁰⁵ comes from the root *resh, tet, heh*. If *yirteni* comes from the root *yod, resh, tet*, then it should be vocalized like *ye’atani*¹⁰⁶ (He hath covered me) (Is. 61:10).¹⁰⁷. *Yarat* and *yirteni* have similar meanings even though they come from two different roots.¹⁰⁸ is *yod, resh, tet* and *yirteni* comes from *resh, tet, heh*. We find the same to be the case with the word *ye’atani* (*Ibid*.), which is vocalized like the word *ye’atzani* (given me counsel) (Ps. 16:7).¹⁰⁹ comes from the root *yod, ayin, tet*. *Ye’atani* is similar in meaning to *oteh* (coverest)¹¹⁰. in (Who coverest Thyself with light) (Ps. 104:2).¹¹¹

וטעם **ואותה החייתי.** כי בן אדם בראותו המלאך ימות והעד ותנצל נפשי ודבר מנוח לעד אף כי הבהמה שאין לה שום שותפות עם רוח המלאך כבן אדם:


AND SAVED HER ALIVE. Scripture is being brief. Its¹¹⁷. meaning is, as I killed her I would have killed you, or I would have killed you and left her alive.¹¹⁸ is short for, I would have killed you and left her alive. The above is explained by the following.¹¹⁹ implies that the ass died. The question arises, “Why?” When a person sees an angel, he dies. *And my life is preserved* (Gen. 32:1),¹²⁰ and the words of Manoah¹²¹ are proof. How much more so the case of a beast that has nothing in common with the spirit of an angel as a human being does.

**שבעה מזבחות.** יש סודות עמוקים לא יבינום כי אם מתי מספר ושביעי בימים ובחדשים ובשנים ושבעה כבשי העולה ושבעה הזאות גם אמר השם לאיוב קחו לכם שבעה פרים ושבעה אילים ובתת שלם לשלם אז תתחדש רוח בינה והמשכיל יבין:


SEVEN ALTARS. There are deep secrets which only a few can fathom. The number seven occurs with regard to days,¹ months,² years;³ the seven lambs offered for a burnt offering;⁴ the seven sprinklings.⁵ God also told Job, *take unto you seven bullocks and seven rams* (Job 42:8). When the complete⁶ is added to the complete,⁷ then a spirit of understanding is newly created.⁸ The intelligent will understand what I speak of.

footnotes:
¹ The seventh day is holy.
² Rosh Ha-Shanah falls on the first day of the seventh month.
³ The seventh year is a sabbatical year. The year of jubilee similarly follows seven sabbatical years.
⁴ Offered on the new moon and the festivals, with the exception of Sukkot. See Num. 28 and 29. On Sukkot, 14 lambs (2 times 7) were offered daily as a burnt offering.
⁵ On Yom Kippur and on the leper. See Lev. 16:14; 14:7. All of these are among these secrets.
⁶ Seven is a complete number.
⁷ To seven. When seven bullocks are added to seven lambs and placed on seven altars. Or when seven animals are sacrificed to God the complete, the celebrant is prophetically inspired.
⁸ In the celebrant; i.e., he is prophetically inspired.

### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 23:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:3:1)


**יקרה.** מגזרת לקראתי:


WILL COME. *Yikkareh* (will come) is derived from *li-kerati* (to meet me).¹² means will meet me. AND WHATSOEVER¹³. HE SHOWETH ME. The word *devar* is connected to *mah*.¹⁴ is connected by hyphen to *yareni* (He showeth me), for the word *devar* is in the construct. If the word were in the absolute it would be vocalized *davar*. Thus our text should be read, *u-devar-mah yareni* (And whatsoever He showeth me), rather than *u-devar mah-yareni*. (And a thing of, what will He show me).

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 23:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:3:3)


**וילך שפי.** דברי המתרגם ארמית ידועים שהוא לבדו והנה שפי לבדו גם הוא בלי אח ואחרים אמרו כי הוא כמו נכאה לכב מגזרת ושפו עצמותיו והנכון בעיני שהוא מגזרת קול על שפיים וימצא ביו"ד גם באל"ף כמלת פתאים והטעם שהלך אל שפי ותחסר מלת אל כמו ויבא ירושלים וכן נסעו העם חצרות ורבים כן והנה הוא מנחש בלכתו כי כן כתוב ולא הלך כפעם בפעם לקראת נחשים והנה גם פה רמזתי לך סוד חתום:


AND HE WENT TO A BARE HEIGHT. The manner in which the Aramaic translator renders *shefi* (bare) is known. He translates *shefi* as alone.¹⁵ Now *shefi* is alone; it is also without a brother.¹⁶ Other say that the word *shefi* means *broken in heart* (Ps. 109:16).¹⁷ They say that the word *shefi* is related to *shuppu* (corrode) in *and his bones corrode* (Job 33:21). However, I believe that the word *shefi* is related to *shefayim* (high hills) in *upon the high hills is heard* (Jer. 3:20). The word is found spelled both with a *yod*¹⁸ and with an *alef*.¹⁹. We find the same thing with the word *peta’im* (simple) (Prov. 1:4).²⁰, and other times with a *yod*. The meaning of *va-elekh shefi* (and he went to a bare height) is, he went to a high hill. The word *el* (to) has been omitted from the phrase.²¹. Our texts reads *va-elekh shefi*, which literally means, and he went to high place. Hence I.E.’s comment. We find the same in *va-yavo yerushalayim* (and he came to Jerusalem)²² (and he came to Jerusalem), for the literal meaning of *va-yavo yerushalayim* is, and he came Jerusalem. (I Kings 3:15) and in *nase’u ha-am hazerot* (the people journeyed unto Hazeroth)²³ (the people journeyed unto Hazeroth), for *nase’u ha-am hazerot* means the people journeyed Hazeroth. (Num. 11:35). There are many such instances.²⁴ has to be added to the text. Observe, Balaam was divining²⁵ when he went,²⁶ for Scripture clearly states, *he went not, as at other times*²⁷ *to meet with enchantments*²⁸ (Num. 24:1). See, I have given you a hint regarding a sealed secret.²⁹

HOW SHALL I CURSE, WHOM GOD HATH NOT CURSED. The word *kabboh* means to curse. Its *heh* is in place of a *vav*.³⁹ rather than *kabbo*. The latter is the usual form. Hence I.E.’s comment. It is like the *heh* in *oholoh*⁴⁰ rather than the more usual *oholo*. (his tent) (Gen. 12:8) and the *heh* in *fera’oh*⁴¹. (let them loose) in *for Aaron had let them loose* (Ex. 32:25). *Kabboh* comes from a double root.⁴². Its full form⁴³ is *kavevo* (they curse him). Compare, *savevo*⁴⁴. Both double root letters are present in *savevu*. (they surrounded him) although it is irregular.⁴⁵ is not found in Scripture (Krinsky). The form used is *sevavuhu* (I Kings 5:17). For other interpretations see Filwarg and Meijler.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 23:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:9:1)


**כי מראש צורים אראנו.** כי על השפי היה והוא גבוה והעד על השפי שהוא כפירושי ולא הלך כפעם בפעם לקראת נחשים וישת אל המדבר פניו ולא אל שפי גם יתכן להיות מראש צורים משל לגזירות היורדות מהעליונים כי ראה בחכמתו שתעמוד זאת האומה לבד' ולא תתערב עם אחרות מתגברת עליה לעזוב תורתה כאשר עשו כל האומות:


FOR FROM THE TOP OF THE ROCKS I SEE HIM. Balaam said this because he was high up on the hill. He went not, as at other times, to meet with enchantments. *But he set his face toward the wilderness* (Num. 24:1)⁴⁷ and not toward the high place⁴⁸ is proof that my interpretation of *shefi*⁴⁹ is correct.⁵⁰ (wilderness), which is a flat area, with *sefi*. Thus *sefi* must refer to an elevated area. It is also likely that *from the top of the rocks* is a parable symbolizing the decrees that come down from heaven. For Balaam in his wisdom⁵¹ saw that this nation would stand alone and not intermingle with other nations that would overpower her and try to force her to give up God’s Torah, as the nations did.

ויפה פירש המתרגם ארמית מלת ישרים וטעם לפי דעתי שהתאוה למות ותהיה אחריתו כאחרית ישראל שהם חלק השם ולא חלק כוכבים כי הוא היה קוסם ויש אומרים שמלת ותהי אחריתי כפולה בטעם והוא היה מתאוה שימות מות ישרים כמו הישרים של ישראל בעבור דעתו כי בחרב ימות והגאון אמר כי מי מנה הוא השם והטעם אתה שתוכל למנות עפר יעקב המת נפשי מות ישרים אם כן מה טעם ומספר את רובע ישראל ולפי דעת רבים שפירושו כמו ארחי ורבעי זרית שהוא כענין רבצי ויפרשו עפר יעקב על עת נסעו:


[LET ME DIE THE DEATH OF THE RIGHTEOUS, AND LET MINE END BE LIKE HIS!] The Aramaic translator beautifully explained the meaning of *yesharim* (the righteous).⁵⁵ as the honest.I believe that Balaam wanted to die. He wanted his end to be like the end of Israel, who are God’s portion and are not ruled by the stars, for he was a magician.⁵⁶ Others say that *mine end* repeats *let me die*. Balaam wanted to die like the righteous of Israel, for he knew that he would die by the sword.⁵⁷ The Gaon⁵⁸ says that *Who hath counted* refers to God. Our verse means: You who are able to count the dust of Jacob, give me the death of the righteous. However, if this is so, then what meaning is there to *Or numbered the stock of Israel*?⁵⁹ after saying, *You who are able to count the dust of Israel*. Many explain that *rova* (the stock of) is similar in meaning to *rivi*, which means my lying down. Compare, *Thou measurest my going about and my lying down* (rivi) (Ps. 139:3). They explain that the *dust of Jacob* refers to the time that Jacob journeys.⁶⁰

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 23:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:13:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 23:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:13:2)


**וקבנו.** מלה זרה ולפי הדקדוק כי הצווי כעתיד ואין ביניהם רק הסימן ירדפהו ירדפנו ירדפוהו אויב ירדפו ובאה זו המלה מורכבת עם נו"ן ובחול"ם ולפי דעת רבי יהודה המדקדק הראשון שהוא מן שורש קבן א"כ לא יתכן להיותה צווי כי ימצא כן מהבנין הקל אולי תהיה שם הפועל על משקל ומשמרו את השבועה:


AND CURSE ME THEM. *Ve-kovno* (and curse them) is irregular.⁶⁵, for that is the rule when a *nun vav* is used to indicate the pronoun. According to the rules of grammar the imperative is the same as the imperfect.⁶⁶ The only difference between them is the prefix.⁶⁷ Compare, *yirdefehu* (he shall pursue him); *yirdefenu* (he shall pursue him); *yirdefuhu* (they shall pursue him); and *yirdefo* (shall pursue him⁶⁸ is represented by a *cholam* only when a *heh vav* or a *nun vav* is not used to indicate the pronoun.) in *The enemy shall pursue him* (Hos. 8:3).⁶⁹ However, *kovno* comes with a *nun* vocalized with a *cholam* joined to the root. According to Rabbi Judah, the first grammarian, the word *kovno* comes from the root *kof, bet, nun*.⁷⁰ is not a sign of the pronoun. The word *kovno* is similar to *yirdefo*; i.e., the pronoun is represented by a *cholam*. If this is the case, then *kovno* cannot be an imperative, for we do not find such a vocalization in the *kal*.⁷¹ signified by a *vav* (Filwarg). Perhaps *kovno* is an infinitive vocalized like the word *shomro* (keep) in *and because He would keep the oath* (Deut. 7:8).

⁶⁶ It is vocalized similarly.
⁶⁷ A prefix is placed before the verb in the imperfect.
⁶⁸ The pronoun him
⁶⁹ These are examples of verbs in the imperfect combined with the pronoun.
⁷⁰ Thus the nun
⁷¹ We do not find the imperative combined with the pronoun him

GIVE EAR UNTO ME. The word *adai* (unto me) is related to the word *ad* (unto). The word *adai* (unto Me) in *Yet have ye not returned unto Me* (Amos 4:6) is similar. It is similar to the *vav* of *le-mayeno* (a fountain) in *into a fountain of waters* (Ps. 114:8).⁷⁴ in this verse means a fountain of, not a fountain.

### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 23:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:21:1)


**לא הביט און.** לפי דעתי כי מזאת המלה למד בלק לשלוח נשי מואב במחנה ישראל והטעם כי אין השם כבן אדם שיתנחם כי לא ראה און בישראל והנה אם יהיה בהם און לא יקום דבר השם כי כל דבריו הם על תנאי רק במקום שבועה וכן הנביא אומר רגע אדבר וזה טעם בדבר בלעם:


NONE HATH BEHELD INIQUITY IN JACOB.⁷⁹ I believe that Balak learned from this utterance to send Moabite women into the camp of Israel.⁸⁰ Scripture’s meaning is that God is not like a man that he should repent (v. 19), for He did not see iniquity in Israel. However, if there be iniquity in Israel, then God’s word will not come to pass, for all of God’s words are conditional unless accompanied by an oath. Compare, *At one instant I may speak concerning a nation…to build and to plant…but if it do evil in My sight…then I repent of the good, wherewith I said I would benefit it*. (Jer. 18:7-10). This is the meaning of Balaam’s statement.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 23:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/23:22:2)


**כתועפת.** כמו קרני ראם ופירוש תועפות תוקף וכן ותועפות הרים לו גם יתכן היות פירושו וקרני הרים וכסף תועפות לך פירושו וכסף תועפות הרים ואמר לו כמו ותרועת מלך בו והטעם שזה האל שם תוקף לישראל וכל זה בעבור שהוא דבוק בשם ולא יבקש כי אם מאתו כי אין להם צורך למנחש וקוסם:


LIKE THE LOFTY HORNS OF THE WILD-OX. *Ke-to’afot re’em* (like the lofty horns of the wild-ox) is similar to *karne re’em* (the horns of the wild-ox) (Deut. 33:17).⁸⁶ refers to an animal. The meaning of *to’afot is*, the might of.⁸⁷ *To’afot* (the heights of) in *The heights of the mountain are His also* (Ps. 95:4) is similar.⁸⁸ It is also possible that the meaning⁸⁹ of *ve-to’afot harim lo* (the heights of the mountains are His) is, the horns of the mountains are also His.⁹⁰. The meaning of *ve-kehsef to’afot lakh* (and precious silver unto thee) (Job 22:25) is, and silver, as mighty as the mountains.⁹¹ is short for *to’afot harim* (might of the mountains). Scripture reads *lo* (to him). [It means to them.] Compare, *and the shouting for the King is among them* (v. 21). It means that this God made Israel strong. God did all this for them because Israel cleaves to God and does not seek anything from anyone but the Lord, for they have no need for an enchanter and a diviner.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 24:6:1

STRETCHED OUT. The *tet* of *nittayu* (stretched out) rceives a *dagesh* to compensate for the *nun* of *natah* (stretched),¹⁰ comes from the root *nun, tet, heh*. which is swallowed.¹¹ is a *nifal*. ### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 24:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:8:1)


**אל מוציאו.** והטעם כי האל המוציאו ממצרים שם כח לו כתועפות ראם ואל יטעון טוען בעבור מ"ם אל מוציאם ויחשוב כי מלת לו סימן לשם כי כן משפט הלשון כמו תכו לרגליך ישא מדברותיך עד אנה ינאצוני העם הזה ורבים כן:


GOD WHO BROUGHT HIM FORTH. The meaning of our verse is: the God who brought him [Israel] out of Egypt made him as powerful as the lofty horns of the wild-ox. Let not the one who would dispute this claim that the word him¹⁸ (him) in the clause *Is for him like the lofty horns of the wild-ox*. refers to God, because Scripture earlier used the plural form *motzi’am* (brought them forth) when it stated, *God who brought them forth* (Num. 23:22).¹⁹) like the lofty horns of the wild-ox. Our verse reads: God who brought him out of Egypt, for him (*lo*) like the lofty horns of the wild-ox. Now, just as the word *lo* (him) in the first verse applies to God, so must the word *lo* (him) in the second verse apply to God. For such is the style of Scripture.²⁰ in Num. 23:22 applies to Israel and similarly in our verse. Compare, *And they*²¹ *sit at Thy feet; he*²² *receives* (yissa) *Thy words* (Deut. 33:3); and *How long will this* (ha-zeh)²³ (this) is in the singular. *people despise Me* (yena’atzuni)²⁴ (will despise me). (Num. 14:11). There are many such instances.

²¹ Israel.
²² Israel; translated literally.
²³ Zeh
²⁴ Yena’atzuni

(shall lop) in *Shall lop the boughs with terror* (Is. 10:33) and *tefa’er*²⁸ (bough). (go over the boughs) in *thou shalt not go over the boughs* (Deut. 24 :20).²⁹

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 24:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:8:4)


**וחציו ימחץ.** כל חץ מחציו ימחץ וכן וצדיקים ככפיר יבטח בנות צעדה וכן מברכיך ברוך כל אחד ממברכיך יהיה ברוך וכן אורריך:


AND PIERCE THEM THROUGH WITH HIS ARROWS. Each one of his arrows shall pierce.³⁰ (arrows) is in the plural, and *yimchatz* (pierce), the verb which governs it, is in the singular. Hence I.E.’s comment. So too, *But the righteous are secure as a young lion* (Prov. 28:1);³¹ (the righteous) is in the plural while *yivtach* (is secure) is in the singular. *Its branches run over the wall* (Gen. 49:22); *Blessed be every one that blesseth thee* (v. 9).³² (blessed be) is in the singular; *me-varekhekha* (they that bless thee) is in the plural. Similarly, *korerekha* is in the plural, and *arur* is in the singular. The latter means, everyone that blesses you wil be blessed. So too, *and cursed be everyone that curseth thee* (*Ibid*.).

**וקם שבט.** מלכות והנכון בעיני כי מלת דרך שיראה בדרכו כטעם הכוכבים ממסילותם ורבים פירשוהו על המשיח והקדמונים אמרו סנחריב בלבל הגוים והנה מואב ועמלק ואשור ועוד למה השלים וענו עבר רק היה ראוי להיות דרך כוכב בסוף משלו וחסירי דעת יחשבו כי המפרש דרך כוכב על דוד הוא מכחש ביאת המשיח חלילה חלילה כי המשיח מבואר היטב בנבואת דניאל כאשר פירשתי שהזכיר עמידת מלכי יון וקום החשמונים ועמידת בית שני ושני המצור והגליות והישועה זה אחר זה ואין צורך לנביא בעולם עם דברי משה שהוא העיקר אם יהיה נדחך בקצה השמים ושב ה' אלהיך את שבותך:


AND A SCEPTRE³⁹ (a rod). Hence I.E.’s comment. SHALL ARISE. The reference is to a royal sceptre.I believe that *shall step* means that the star shall be seen making its way, as in *The stars in their courses* (Jud. 5:20). Many explained that the reference is to the messiah. The ancients said that Sanherib⁴⁰ mixed up the nations.⁴¹ 54a. However, note that Scripture speaks of Moab, Amalek, and Asshur.⁴² Furthermore, why does Balaam conclude with *and shall afflict Eber* (v. 24)?⁴³ On the contrary, Balaam should have ended his parable with *There shall step forth a star out of Jacob*.⁴⁴ Those who lack intelligence think that anyone who explains that *There shall step forth a star* refers to King David denies the coming of the messiah.⁴⁵ Far be it, far be it, for the messiah is clearly stated in the prophecy of Daniel. I have already explained that Daniel first mentions the coming into existence of the Greek kings⁴⁶ and the arising of the Hasmoneans. He mentions the existence of the second temple, the years of the siege, the exile, and the salvation. He notes these things in order. There is no conceivable need for another prophet,⁴⁷ since we have the words of Moses, who is the most important prophet: *If any of thine that are dispersed be in the uttermost parts of heaven… the Lord thy God will bring thee* (Deut. 30:4,5).⁴⁸

**בני שת.** כמו בני אדם כי הוא העיקר כי נח מבני בניו היה ויאמר היצחקי כי פירשו על בני עמון גם מואב והטעם כפול גם אמר שהוא מגזרת וחשפי שת רמז לבנות לוט והוא רחוק בעיני כי השת הוא האחור שהוא כמו היסוד כמו כי השתות יהרסון ורבים פירשו כל בני שת מגזרת כי השתות והטעם כי יהרום המדינות ואיננו רחוק:


THE SONS OF SETH. People. Seth was the most important son of Adam, for Noah was descended from him. Yitzchaki⁵¹ says that the reference is to the Amonites and the Moabites, and that Scripture repeats itself.⁵² He also says that the word Seth is derived from the word *shet* (buttocks) in *and with buttocks uncovered* (Is. 20:4) and that it alludes to the daughters⁵³ of Lot.⁵⁴ However, this appears to me to be farfetched, for *shet* refers to the backside,⁵⁵ which is the foundation of the body.⁵⁶ is foundation, not buttock. Compare, *ki ha-shatot yeharesun* (When the foundations are destroyed) (Ps. 11:3). Many others have explained that the word *shet* (Seth) in *all the sons of Seth*, is related to the word *ha-shatot* (foundations) in *When the foundations are destroyed*. It means that the cities will be destroyed.⁵⁷ (and break down all the sons of Seth) means: and will break down all foundations. This interpretation is not far-fetched.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:20:1)


**וירא את עמלק.** בדרך נבואה והמשל ראשית גוים ופירושו כי הוא הגוי הנלחם עם ישראל בראשונה ואחריתו עד שיהיה אובד וכן היה בימי שאול שהמית מאיש ועד אשה מעולל ועד יונק וזקן ורבים פירשו ראשית גוים כי הם יחשבו בראש הגוים ולא היה כן:


AND HE LOOKED ON AMALEK. Via prophecy.⁶⁵ *The first of the nations* is the parable. It means Amalek was the first nation to wage war against Israel, but his end shall be utter destruction. This⁶⁶ took place in the days of Saul, who slew *man and woman, infant and suckling* (I Sam. 15:3) and old men. Many explain that the meaning of *the first of the nations* is that Amalek was considered to be the head of the nations. However, this was not the case.⁶⁷

footnotes:
⁶⁵ He did not actually look at Amalek.
⁶⁶ The destruction of Amalek.
⁶⁷ Amalek was never the chief of the nations.



### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 24:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:21:1)


**וירא את הקיני.** משפחת יתרו וכתוב המה הקינים וחבר הקיני והמשל ושים בסלע קנך. והטעם כפול כי אילו היה מושבך גבוה כקן העוף לא יצילך:


AND HE LOOKED ON THE KENITE.⁶⁸ The family of Jethro. Scripture writes, *These are the Kenites* (I Chron. 2:55) and *Now Heber the Kenite* (Jud. 4:11).⁶⁹. This shows that the Kenites are descended from Moses’ father-in-law. *And though thy nest be set in the rock* is the parable.⁷⁰ The latter repeats the preceding clause.⁷¹ repeats *Though firm be thy dwelling place*. Its meaning is, though your dwelling place be as high as the nest of a bird, it will not save you.

### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 24:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:22:1)


**לבער קין.** כמו ושבה והיתה לבער וכן כאשר יבער הגלל ובערת הרע וקין הוא הקיני:


KAIN SHALL BE WASTED. *Le-va’er* (wasted) is similar to the word *le-va’er* (eaten up) in *it shall again be eaten up* (Is. 6:13); and *yeva’er* (sweepeth) in *as a man sweepeth away dung* (I Kings 14:10); and *u-vi’arta* (so shalt thou put away) in *So shalt thou put away the evil from thee* (Deut. 13:6).⁷² means to destroy. Kain and the Kenite are one and the same.

⁷² In other words, le-va’er

וטעם **עד מה אשור תשבך.** כאומר עד מתי תשבך אשור לא יעזבך כי אם היתה לבער ואשור לשון נקבה והטעם מחנה וכן ותפול שבא ותקחם ותערוך ישראל:


[HOW LONG? ASSHUR SHALL CARRY THEE AWAY CAPTIVE.] Balaam, as it were, said: How long shall Asshur carry thee⁷³ away captive? He will not let go of you until you are wasted. Asshur is feminine. Asshur is short for the camp of Asshur. Compare, *va-tipple sheva va-tikkachem* (and the Sabeans made a raid) (Job 1:15); *Va-ta’arokh yisra’el* (and Israel…put the battle in array) (I Sam. 17:21).

### Verse 23

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 24:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:23:1)


**וישא משלו ויאמר.** הוא וצים מיד כאשר הזכיר שאשור ישבה הקיני אמר גם יבא עת שיעונה אשור ועבר עמו והטעם העברים שישבה אשור כי הקינים היו דרים עם ישראל ופירוש המתרגם ארמית ידוע רק אין מנהג הכתוב להזכיר עבר בלא נהר. יש מפרשים וצים לשון רבים מגזרת וצי אדיר וי"א שפירושו כמו ופגשו ציים את איים כי דמם לציים שישום אדם מראותם:


AND HE TOOK UP HIS PARABLE, AND SAID. The reference is to *But ships shall come from the coast of Kittim* (v. 24). When Balaam mentioned that the Kenite would be carried away captive, he also said that a time would come when Asshur would be afflicted and Eber along with him. The latter refers to the Hebrews that Asshur carried away captive, for the Kenites lived with the Israelites. The interpretation of the Aramaic translation is well known.⁷⁴ (Eber) by *ever perat* (the other side of the Euphrates). However, it is not the practice of Scripture to mention the word *ever* without the word *nahar* (river) following it.⁷⁵ Some explain that *tzim* (ships) is a plural. It is related to the word *tzi* (ship) in gallant ship (Is. 33:21). Others say that the word *tzim* is related to the word *tziyim* (wild-cats) *in And the wild-cats shall meet with the jackals* (Is. 34:14). Balaam compared the Kittim to wild-cats because people will be gripped by fear when they appear.⁷⁶

footnotes:
⁷⁴ Onkelos renders ever
⁷⁵ When referring to the other side of the Euphrates.
⁷⁶ These commentators explain our verse as follows: wild-cats shall come from the land of Kittim.


###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 24:23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/24:23:2)


וטעם **אוי מי יחיה משמו אל.** הטעם על מלך אשור ששם נפשו כמו אל וכן כתיב בספר ישעיה או טעמו מי יחיה מהגזרות ששם אל בעולם על ידי אשור כי מלך אשור נצח את כל הגוים כי כן כתוב:


[ALAS, WHO SHALL LIVE AFTER GOD HATH APPOINTED HIM.] The reference is to the king of Asshur who made himself into a god. The latter is noted in the Book of Isaiah.⁷⁷ Or its meaning is: Who shall survive the decrees which God placed in the world via Asshur, for the king of Assyria conquered all the nations. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture.

footnotes:
⁷⁷ See Is. 10:7. Isaiah did not actually say this. He intimated that the king of Assyria, in destroying nations, acted like a god.

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 25:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/25:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/25:4:2)


**והוקע אותם.** כמו ויוקיעם בהר כדברי המתרגם ארמית והעד נגד השמש והטעם בפרהסיא כמו לעיני השמש הזאת:


AND HANG THEM. *Ve-hoka otam* (and hang them) is similar to *va-yaki’um* (and they hanged them) in *and they hanged them in the mountain* (II Sam. 21:9). It is to be understood in accordance with the words of the Aramaic translation.⁶: execute those who are guilty of a capital crime. However, I.E.’s reference might be to Targum Jonathan, who renders *ve-hiki’um, u-tzelovinun* as, and hang them (Krinsky). However, it should also be noted that *u-tzelovinun* can also be rendered, and crucify them. The proof text is, *In the face of the sun*.⁷ The meaning of *in the face of the sun* is, in public. Compare, *in the sight of this sun* (II Sam. 12:11).⁸. The next verse continues, *but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun*.

footnotes:
⁶ Onkelos renders u-ketol de-chayyav ketol
⁷ That the reference is to public execution. For they were hung in the mountain so that all in the vicinity could see them executed.
⁸ The entire clause reads, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun

**אתם.** כמו דברו לשלום:


WITH THEM. *Otam* (with them)⁸ means them. Scripture should have read *ittam* (with them). Hence I.E.’s comment. is similar to *dabbero* (speak…unto him) in *speak peaceably unto him* (Gen. 37:4).⁹ is irregular, for it is a compound of *dabber* (speak) and *oto* (him). *Dabbero* literally means speak him. We thus sees that Scripture employs the term “him” with the meaning of “with him.” The same applies to the term *otam* (them). Scripture occasionally employs it with the meaning of “with them.”

⁹ Dabbero

Samuel,¹⁸ his sons, and his grandsons who were singers¹⁹ and were called the Korahites²⁰ is proof of this.²¹ The Book of Psalms states, *For the leader; a Psalm of the sons of Korah* (Ps. 49:1). The Torah also records the family of the Korahites (v. 58). Scripture mentions the sons of Korah with the sons of Reuben because the adult and the minor sons of Dathan and Abiram died. **הימיני.** אל תבקש דקדוק בשמות וכן מן פוני ומן לשפופם השופמי לימנה משפחת הימנה ואיננו הימיני כמו מן בריעה בריעי וחגי ושוני חסר יו"ד היחס או זה יו"ד היחס ושל השם חסר והוא הנכון ואחר ראובן שמעון וגד החונים עליו רק מנשה קודם אפרים ובמדבר סיני הפוך והנכון שזה בעבור מספרם כי בני אפרים יוסיפו על בני מנשה במדבר סיני שמונת אלפים ושלשת מאות ובערבות מואב יוסיפו בני מנשה על בני אפרים עשרים אלף ומאתים וכן זכר למשפחות חמשה בנים לבנימין והם בכר וגרא ונעמן וראש וארד:


THE JAMINITES. Do not seek grammatical consistency in names. Compare, *puvvah*²³ and *puni* (Punites) (v. 23).²⁴ rather than *puni* to be used for a member of Puvvah’s family. From *shefufam*²⁵ Scripture derives *shufami* (v. 39).²⁶ to be used. Scripture also reads: *of yimnah* (Imnah), *the family of yimnah* (v. 44), not *ha-yemini*²⁷. as it does in the case of *bri’ah*²⁸ and *beri’iy* (Beriites)²⁹ (v. 44); *Chaggi*³⁰ and *shuni* were sons of Gad. Scripture refers to members of their family by the terms *chaggi* and *shuni* rather than *chaggi’iy* or *shuni’iy*. and *shuni* (v. 15) lacking the *yod* gentile.³¹ On the other hand, the *yod* of *chaggi* and *shuni* might be the *yod* gentile and the *yod* of the proper name³² of the names of *chaggi* and *shuni*. is missing. The latter is correct. After Reuben, Scripture lists Simeon and Gad, who pitched next to Reuben.³³ However, Manasseh is mentioned before Ephraim.³⁴ The order is reversed in the wilderness of Sinai.³⁵ It appears that this is due to their number, for the sons of Ephraim were more numerous than the sons of Manasseh in the wilderness of Sinai by eight thousand and three hundred,³⁶., 35). and in the plains of Moab the sons of Manasseh numbered more than the sons of Ephraim by twenty thousand and two hundred.³⁷ No mention is made of the family of the following five sons of Benjamin: Becher, Gera, Naaman, Rosh, and Ard.³⁸

**ויהיו פקודיהם.** פקודי הלוים במספר הזה נוספו שבע מאות והתימה כי לא נוסף בהם רק שבע מאות והנה ישראל שמתו מי שהיה מבן עשרים שנה ומעלה היה מספרם בפעם האחרונה קרוב מהמספר הראשון כי הלוים לא נכנסו עם פקודי ישראל והעד אלעזר הכהן:

The Israelites from among whom all those above the age of twenty died⁶⁶ numbered about the same as they did during their first numbering.⁶⁷ [The small increase in the number of Levites is strange] for the Levites were not included in the numbering of Israel.⁶⁸ Eleazar the Kohen proves the latter.⁶⁹

### Verse 1

וטעם הדבק פרשת הקרבנות שהשם צוה אז למשה שיצוה את בני ישראל הקרבנות שהם חייבים לעשות כי הוא לא יכנס לארץ עמהם והחל להזכיר עולת תמיד ואם הזכירה בתחלה יתכן שהנזכרת היא על הר סיני או שתהיה מערכת הקרבנות סדורה:


The reason the chapter dealing with the sacrifices follows²¹ is that God then²² ordered Moses to command the children of Israel regarding the sacrifices they are obligated to offer,²³ for Moses was not to enter the land with them. Scripture starts with the daily burnt offering even though it was mentioned earlier.²⁴ It is possible that the earlier burnt offering was the one offered at Mount Sinai.²⁵ On the other hand, it is possible that Scripture wants to insure that the arrangement of the sacrifices is in order.²⁶

footnotes:
²¹ The chapter dealing with the appointment of Joshua to succeed Moses.
²² Following the appointment of Joshua.
²³ In the Land of Israel.
²⁴ In Ex. 29:42. The point is, why repeat the law of the burnt offering.
²⁵ When Israel camped around Mount Sinai. In other words, it does not pertain to the daily burnt offering to be made when they entered the Land of Israel.
²⁶ Scripture repeats the law of the burnt offering here because it wants to list in order all of the burnt offerings which the congregation is obligated to bring, i.e., the daily burnt offering, the new moon burnt offering, the Passover offering, etc.

**בשבתו.** שב אל יום השבת אע"פ שנמצא כל שומר שבת מחללו והטעם כל שבת ושבת כמו יום ביומו:


OF EVERY SABBATH. The *vav* suffixed to the word *shabbat*¹³ in the word *shabbato* (every Sabbath). refers to the day of Sabbath.¹⁴ is feminine. Thus Scripture should have used the term *shabbatah* if the reference was to every Sabbath. Hence I.E.’s comment that the *vav* refers to the word *yom* in verse 9, which is masculine. Thus according to I.E. we should render *shabbato* (every Sabbath) as every Sabbath day. This is so even though we find the word *me-challelo*¹⁵. (from profaning it¹⁶ as masculine.) in *Every one that keepeth the sabbath from profaning it* (Is. 56:6). The meaning of *be-shabbato* (of every Sabbath) is, *every sabbath and sabbath*. Compare, *yom be-yomo* (daily) (Ex. 5:13).

### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 28:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/28:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/28:11:1)


**ובראשי חדשיכם.** אמר רבי משה הכהן הספרדי נ"ע שפירושו חדש ניסן כי כן כתוב ראשון הוא לכם ואחר כן אמר זאת עולת חדש בחדשו שיעשו כן בכל חדש על כן הוסיף לחדשי השנה ופירושו נכון הוא ואע"פ שיש לטעון על יו"ד ובראשי חדשיכם רק בעבור שמצאנו הנה חדש מחר ישר דבורו:


AND IN YOUR NEW MOONS. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen the Spaniard, who rests in paradise, says that *u-ve-roshe chodshekhem*¹⁸ (and in your new moons) refers to the new moon of Nisan, for Scripture clearly states, *it shall be the first month of the year to you* (Ex. 12:2).¹⁹ Scripture then goes on to say, *This is the burnt-offering of every new moon* (v. 14), that is, they shall offer this burnt offering²⁰ on every new moon. The Torah therefore adds, *throughout the months of the year* (*Ibid.*).²¹ Rabbi Moses’ interpretation is correct. He is right even though the *yod* in *u-ve-roshe chodshekhem* (and in your new moons) argues against his interpretation.²² is a plural. Hence *roshe chodshekhem* seems to mean the many first days of the month. If the reference was to the new moon of Nisan, then Scripture should have read *u-ve-rosh chodshekem* (and on the first day of your months). However, the fact that we find *hinneh chodesh machar*²³. (Behold, tomorrow is the new moon) (I Sam. 20:5) shows that what he says is correct.²⁴. This implies that an ordinary new moon is called *chodesh*, and the new moon of Nisan *rosh chodesh*. Otherwise Samuel would have referred to the new moon by the phrase *rosh chodesh*.

Scripture tells us that the children of Gad came to Moses and Eleazar and the princes of the congregation, and spoke their piece (Num. 32:2-6). Scripture then writes, *So Moses gave charge concerning them to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of the fathers’ houses* (Num. 32:28). Scripture therefore reads,⁷ *And Moses spoke unto the heads of the tribes*.⁸ *saying…*(v. 2). *When a man voweth a vow…he shall not break his word*. Scripture there⁹ writes, *he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth* (v. 3).

AND BINDETH HERSELF BY A BOND. Or bindeth herself by a bond.¹⁴ of *ve-aserah* means or, not and.[5.] HER BOND. *Essarah* (her bond) belongs to a different form.¹⁵. It is not the same as *issar* (bond).¹⁶ has a *dagesh* in the *samekh*. In other words, *esar* and *issar* come from the same root but belong to different forms.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/30:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/30:11:1)


**ואם בית אישה נדרה.** האלמנה בימים הקדמונים והניא אותה לא תקיים נדרה בימי אלמנותה וזה על דבר העתיד שנדרה ומת הבעל קודם הגעת הזמן. מלת סליחה מפורשת:


AND IF A WOMAN VOWED IN HER HUSBAND’S HOUSE. If the widow vowed in an earlier time and her husband disallowed it, then she does not have to keep the vow in her widowhood. This speaks about a vow which she vowed regarding the future, and the husband died before the vow was to take effect.¹⁷ The meaning of *selichah* (forgiveness) has been previously explained.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁷ Otherwise our verse would be repeating verse 9. For if a husband can annul his wife’s vow which was made when she was under her father’s charge, he can certainly annul avow made under his charge. Hence I.E. explains that our verse deals with a divorcee or widow who uttered a vow while married and had the vow nullified by her husband, who died before the vow became due. Our verse teaches that in such a case the nullification of the vow retains its efficacy.
¹⁸ See I.E. on Num. 14:19.

### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Numbers 31:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/31:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Numbers/r/31:20:1)


**וכל מעשה עזים.** כאשר פירשתי. והנה הבגד בעבור שנגע בחלל הוא טמא הטעם ועמכם כל בגד עד שתתחטאו או תהיה מלת תתחטאו יוצאה וכן והתאויתם לכם כי הגבול הוא הפעול:


AND ALL WORK OF GOATS’ HAIR.²¹. Literally, goats’ work. Hence I.E.’s comments. This is to be interpreted in accordance with my earlier explanation.²² (goats) is to be rendered as goats’ hair.” In other words, “goats’ work” means a garment made out of goats’ hair. Observe, the garment²³ is unclean because it touched a corpse. The meaning of our verse is, the garments shall be with you²⁴ (and as to every garment) is, and with you all garments. I.E. reads our verse as follows: And all garments taken in spoil…[shall be with you outside of the camp] until you are purified. I.E. interprets thus because *titchate’u* is in the *hitpa’el*. Words in the *hitpa’el* are reflexive. until you are purified.²⁵ (ye shall purify) as if written *ad she-titchatu’e* (until you are purified). On the other hand, *titchate’u* (ye shall purify) might be transitive.²⁶ means ye shall purify, i.e., the garments. *Ve-hitavvitem*²⁷. *lakhem* (and ye shall mark out) (Num. 34:10) is similar,²⁸. for *gevul* (line)²⁹ is the object.³⁰ (and ye shall mark out) is transitive.

²² See I.E. on Ex. 25:4 (Vol. 2, p. 534) “Izzim
²³ Mentioned in our verse.
²⁴ In other words, the meaning of ve-khol beged
²⁵ I.E. interprets titchate’u
²⁶ In other words, titchate’u
²⁷ It too is in the hitpa’el
²⁸ For it too is transitive even though it is in the hitpa’el
²⁹ Which follows “and ye shall mark out.”
³⁰ Hence ve-hitavvitem

**יתר הבז.** חוץ מאשר אכלו על כן אמר יתר והזכיר מספרם כי היה מספר רב ולא שמענו שלל כמוהו גם כן הזכיר המכס כי גם הוא רב ומלת מכם מפועלי הכפל על משקל וממר ליולדתו והוא מגזרת תכסו על השה והטעם חלק:


OVER AND ABOVE THE BOOTY.⁵¹ Aside from what they consumed. Scripture therefore reads *yeter* (above).⁵² The Torah mentions the amount of spoil because it consisted of a vast number. We never heard of a similar amount of spoil.⁵³ Scripture also mentions the tribute,⁵⁴ for it too was very great. The word *mekhes* (tribute) (v. 37) comes from a double root.⁵⁵. It is vocalized like the word *memer* (bitterness)⁵⁶. in *and bitterness to her that bore him* (Prov. 17:25). *Mekhes* is related to the word *takhossu* (ye shall make your count) in *ye shall make your count for the lamb* (Ex. 12:4). The meaning of *mekhes* (tribute) is a portion.
