### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 13:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:5:1)


**עמד בעיניו.** הטעם במראהו כי המראה הוא בעין וכל המפרשים אמרו שטעמו בעצמו והטעם כאשר היה:


STAY IN ITS APPEARANCE. *Amad be-enav*²⁵ means stay in its appearance. The term *enav*²⁶ is employed, for its appearance is seen by the eye. All the commentaries says that *beenav* (in its appearance) means in its make-up, that is, in the way it was.²⁷ (it remains as it was). Also see Rashi: “In its appearance in its original size.” According to this interpretation *amad be-enav* (stay in appearance) is to be rendered, remained as it was.

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 13:6:1

AGAIN. *Shenit* (again) means a second time.


###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 13:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:6:2)


**כהה הנגע.** רבים החכמים אמרו כמו חשך ועדותם ותכהין עיניו מראות ואמרו כי כהות לבנות פירושו כמו לבנה אדמדמת שיהיו בו שניהם ולפי דעתי שמלת כהה הפך פשה ומגזרת ותכהין עיניו והקרוב אליו ולא כהה בם וטעם לא פשה הנגע במקום אחר והנה הם שני סימנים שכהה המקום הנגוע ולא פשה בשלם:


THE PLAGUE BE DIM. Many of the wise men say that the word *kehah* (dim) means dark.²⁸ (the plague be dim) means the affliction is black. They offer proof from *vatikhhena* (were dim) in *and his eyes were dim* (Gen. 27:1).²⁹ They say that the phrase *kehot levanot* (dull white) (v. 39) is similar to *le-vanah adamdamet* (reddish-white) (v. 19)³⁰ (dull white) means black white. in that it contains both colors. However, I believe that the word *kehah* (dim) is the reverse of *pasah* (spread).³¹ It is related to the word *va-tikhhena* (were dim) in *and his eyes were dim* (Gen. 27:1). The word *khihah* (stopped) in *and he diminished*³² *them not*³³ (I Sam. 3:13) is close to it. The meaning of *kahah ha-nega* (the plague be dim) is that the plague did not spread to another place. Note, there are two signs, namely, the size of the affliction was diminished and it did not spread to the healthy part of the body.

³¹ It means diminished.
³² Translated according to I.E. See Krinsky.
³³ He did not “cut them down to size.”

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 13:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:19:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 13:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:19:2)


מלת **צרעת** מחלה וכן ושלחתי את הצרעה ואין מלת ושלחתי טענה כי הנה ישלח דברו אני שולח את כל מגפותי ישלח בם חרון אפו:


The word *tzara’at* (leprosy) (v. 20) means a disease. Similarly *ha-tzirah* (the disease)⁴² in *I will send the disease* (Ex. 23:28). The fact that the Torah reads, *and I will send* is no argument against this interpretation,⁴³ means a disease. There are some who argue that the term “sent” (*shalach*) applies only to living things. They translate *ha-tizirah* (the disease) in Ex. 23:28 as the hornet. They render Ex. 23:28 as *I will send the hornet*. for Scripture reads, *He sent His word* (Ps. 107:20); *For I…send all My plagues* (Ex. 9:14); and *He sent forth upon them the fierceness of His anger* (Ps. 78:49).

⁴² Translated according to I.E.
⁴³ That tzirah



### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 13:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:20:1)


**והנה מראה.** לא יתכן בדקדוק מראה בקמץ גדול תחת האל״ף והה״א במפיק כמו ידה רגלה כי לא נמצא כן בבעלי הה״א הנח הנעלם בסוף המלה ודגשות נו״ן:


AND, BEHOLD, IF THE APPEARANCE THEREOF. It is not grammatically correct to vocalize the *alef* of *mareha* (its appearance) with a long *kamatz* and a *mappik*⁴⁴ of *marah* is a pronominal suffix. We would therefore expect it to have a *mappik*. Hence I.E.’s comment. in the *heh* as in the case of *yadah* (her hand) and *raglah* (her foot),⁴⁵ (her hand) and *raglah* end in *kamatz, mappik heh*. If *marehah* followed their vocalization, the word would read *marah*. for we do not find words whose roots end in a silent *heh* to be so treated.⁴⁶.

footnotes:
⁴⁴ A dot which indicates a pronominal suffix (her or its). The heh
⁴⁵ Yadah
⁴⁶ The root of marehah is resh, alef, heh

E. on Ex 1:9 (Vol. 2, pp. 11-14).

### Verse 29

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 13:29:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:29:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/13:29:1)


וטעם להזכיר **ואיש או אשה.** בעבור הזקן ועוד כי הוא צריך לאמר על הקרח והגבח איש ולא אדם סלל להוציא האשה והנה פירוש (פי׳‎ מ״ח ואיש או אשה ר״ל אחר שלקח לשון איש שאינו כולל לאשה כמו מלת אדם. הוצרך לומר אשה בעבור הראש לא בעבור הזקן כי הזקן שב לאיש ולא לאשה ובקרח ובגבח אמר כמו שאמר ואיש כי ימרט ראשו ולא הזכיר בו אשה כי לא תמצא קרחת וגבחת באשה מפני הלחות שבה כמו שמפרש למטה. ומה שאמר ולא אדם. ר״ל ולא אמר אדם שהוא כלל לאיש ולאשה עד כאן) כי יהיה בו נגע בראש או בזקן לאיש:


[AND WHEN…] Scripture mentions a man or a woman⁵⁴ (man). It now employs *ish ve-ishah* (a man or a woman). Hence I.E.’s comment. because it deals with an affliction in the beard⁵⁵, then we would have thought that the law spoken of in our verse applies only to males. Hence Scripture speaks of a man and a woman. The law regarding the affliction in the head applies to both a man and a woman, while the law of the beard applies only to a man. [and the head]. Also, because the Torah has to use the word *ish* (man), and not the term *adam* (a human being) to exclude women from the law of the bald head and the bald forehead (v. 40).⁵⁶ with regard to the aforementioned. Scripture thus wanted to emphasize that the law regarding afflictions in the hairy head applies to both men and women. Note, our verse means, when a man or a woman has an affliction upon the head or a man upon the beard.⁵⁷

footnotes:
⁵⁴ Till now Scripture introduced the afflictions with the term adam
⁵⁵ Our verse deals with an affliction in the head and the beard. Had it read adam
⁵⁶ The law regarding an affliction in a bald head does not apply to a woman, for women are rarely bald. Hence Scripture could not use the term adam
⁵⁷ So Sarim and Krinsky.

MALIGNANT. The word *mameret* (malignant) is similar to the word *mammir* (pricking) in *a pricking brier* (sillon mamir) (Ezek. 28:24). Now, since the word *sillon* (brier) means a thorn, the word *mamir* means painful.⁸¹ (Ezek. 28:24) as a painful thorn. The second *mem* in *mameret* is a root letter and the word *mameret* is not related to the word *me’erah* (curse).⁸² has only one *mem* in it. It is possible that the reason Scripture does not mention silk and cotton⁸³ is that the Torah speaks of what is contemporarily present.⁸⁴ Compare, *If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee* (Ex. 23:5). The same law applies to a horse and a mule. On the other hand, it is possible that the affliction only strikes wool and flax.

## Chapter 14


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 14:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/14:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/14:1:1)


אמר **וידבר ה׳‎.** כי יחל תורת המטהר ואמר ר׳‎ יונה הספרדי המדקדק כי נרפא נגע הצרעת מן הצרוע הוא הפוך והיה ראוי להיותו נרפא הצרוע מנגע הצרעת ולמה נהפוך דברי אלהים חיים בעבור חוסר דעתנו והלא שם כתוב כי נרפא הנתק טהור הוא ועוד כי נרפא הנגע:


[AND THE LORD SPOKE.] Scripture states *and the Lord spoke*¹ in Lev. 13:1 would appear to apply to our chapter as well. Therefore the clause *And the Lord spoke unto Moses* in Lev. 14:1 seems unnecessary. Hence I.E. points out that our portion begins with *And the Lord spoke* because it contains a new commandment, *viz*., the laws of the cleansing of the leper. In other words, our chapter is not a mere continuation of what came before it. because it begins the laws of the one who is cleansed. Rabbi Jonah the Spaniard, the grammarian, says that *and, behold, if the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper* (v. 3) is inverted. It should have read “and, behold, if the leper be healed from the plague of leprosy.”²

footnotes:
¹ Our chapter continues the theme of the preceding chapter. Thus the statement And the Lord spoke unto Moses
² In other words, our verse should be interpreted as if written, if the leper be healed from the plague of leprosy, for according to Rabbi Jonah it is the person not the plague who is healed.

[HE SHALL BE BROUGHT.] *He shall be brought* is to be interpreted like its counterparts,⁴, by his consent or against his will.” for it is possible that after the plague of leprosy is removed the afflicted person will not want to bring what he is obligated to.⁵

AND THE PRIEST SHALL GO FORTH OUT OF THE CAMP. Even though the *kohen* declared him clean he shall not enter the camp or the city until he brings his cleanliness offerings and completes⁶ as in *Vat. Ebr.* 38. Most *Mikra’ot Gedolot* read, *ve-yeshalem* (and pays). all that he has been commanded to do.

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 14:14:1

**על תנוך.** טעמו ידוע ממקומו והנה המטהר מהצרעת שהוא בגוף כמו הכהן שימלא ידו כי העון כמו הצרעת בנפש והבהן מקום חבור והוא עקר כל המעשים והימנות בעבור כח הצד הימין והתנוך זכר לשמוע אשר צוה:


UPON THE TIP. The meaning of *tenuch* (tip) is understood from its context.⁴⁸ Now, the one who is cleansed from leprosy, which is an affliction in the body, is similar to the *kohen* who is installed,⁴⁹ for sin is like a leprosy in the soul.⁵⁰ who is installed is cleansed from leprosy of the soul, i.e., from sin. The thumb is the place of connection.⁵¹ It is the main component of all acts.⁵² The right thumb was selected because of the power of the right side. The tip of the ear is a reminder to listen to what God has commanded.⁵³

### Verse 37

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 14:37:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/14:37:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/14:37:1)


**שקערורות.** אין אחות למלה הזאת ולא נדע אם היא מרובעת כפולה האות האחרון או מחמשת אותיות ופירושיה לפי טעם המקום יש אומרים כדמות סימנין או חוטין ויש אומרים שהיא מלה מורכבת מטעם ותשקע האש. ורורות מגזרת רר בשרו וזה רחוק:


HOLLOW STREAKS. The word *sheka’arurot* (hollow streaks) has no sister.⁷⁸ is feminine. We do not know if it is a quadrilateral⁷⁹. with the last letter⁸⁰. doubled or if it is a pentaliteral.⁸¹. The meaning of *sheka’arurot* is to be ascertained from its context. Some say that it refers to marks or streaks. Others say that it is a compound word. It is akin to *va-tishka* (sank down)⁸² in *and the fire sank down* (Num. 11:2) and to *rorot*, which is related to the word *rar* (run)⁸³ in *run with his issue* (Lev. 15:3).⁸⁴ is made up of the words *shaka* (sank down) and *rorot* (run). According to this interpretation *sheka’arurot* means running cracks in the skin. However, this is far-fetched.

⁸² Translated literally.
⁸³ That is, flow.
⁸⁴ That is, sheka’arurot

**ואת הבית יקציע.** מגזרת מקצעות וכן מר ואהלות קציעות וטעמו פצולות ויש אומרים שיפצלו המקצוע ואין זה נכון כי כבר פשה נגע בבית רק יקציע כל הבית:

This interpretation connects the word *yaktzi’a* to the word *miktzo’a* (corner). See Ezek. 46:21. ## Chapter 15


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 15:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/15:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/15:1:1)


**וידבר יי אל משה ואל אהרן.** כי הכהנים יפרישו בין זבה לנדה כאשר אחז"ל בין דם לדם ועתה יחל לבאר הטמאים מדבר נסתר כי הצרעת נגע גלוי:


AND THE LORD SPOKE UNTO MOSES AND TO AARON. For the *kohanim* distinguish between a woman who has an issue (*zavah*) and one who menstruates (*niddah*).¹ Compare the Rabbinic interpretation on *between blood and blood*² then the *kohen* shall decide the aforementioned. The Rabbis interpret *between blood and blood* as meaning between “between menstrual blood and blood of an issue and blood of childbirth (*Sifre*, on Deut. 17:8).” (Deut. 17:8). Scripture now begins to deal with those who become unclean from a hidden source,³ for until now it dealt with leprosy which is a visible plague.

¹ Hence this commandment was also communicated to Aaron.
² Deuteronomy 17:8-9 states that if there be a dispute regarding blood and blood
³ Such as an issue.

### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 15:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/15:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/15:8:1)


**ירק.** ידוע מפעלי הכפל והעד דגשות קו״ף רוקי הנה גם רוקו יזיק כי הזוב מהחליים הנדבקים ואין מנהג האדם שירוק בפני חברו רק איננו בכוונה כי הזב זרק רוקו ונפל על הטהור:


SPIT. The meaning of *yarok* (spit) is known. It comes from a double root.¹¹. The fact that the *kof* of *rukki* (my spittle) (Job 7:19) has a *dagesh* is proof of this.¹² compensates for the missing root *kof*. Note, the spit of the one who suffers an issue is harmful,¹³ for the issue is one of the infectious diseases. It is not the practice of men to spit in the face of other people.¹⁴ (*ve-khi*) *he that hath an issue spit upon him that is clean* could conceivably be rendered, and when (*ve-khi*) he that hath an issue spit upon him that is clean. “And when” implies that this is the normal course of events. Hence I.E.’s comment. What happened occurred unintentionally. The one suffering from an issue expectorated his spittle and it fell on a clean person.¹⁵ is to be rendered as “and if” that is and if by accident.

footnotes:
¹¹ Its root is resh, kof, kof
¹² For the dagesh
¹³ Hence it is a source of uncleanliness.
¹⁴ And if
¹⁵ In other words, ve-khi

**וידיו לא שטף במים.** היה נראה לנו כי כל מאכל והדומה לו שיגע בו הזב והנגיעה היא בידים וידיו שטופות איננו טמא בעבור שלא נגע במקום הזוב רק כאשר ראינו כל אבותינו פירשו וידיו כגופו קבלנו דבריהם ועל דרך הפשט כי כל טהור שיגע בו הזב וידיו שטופות הוא יטמא ולא בגדיו ואם לא היו שטופות יטמאו בגדיו וזה כמו הנוגע בכל אשר יהיה תחתיו:


WITHOUT HAVING RINSED HIS HANDS IN WATER. It would have appeared to us²⁰ that any food or anything similar, that the one having an issue touched by hand,²¹ means touched by hand. and the hands were washed, is not unclean, for the afflicted did not touch the place of the issue.²² However, since we saw that our fathers²³ explained that the hands are like the body²⁴ means without immersing his body. See *Niddah* 66b; *Kiddushin* 25a. we accept their words. According to the plain meaning of our verse if the one experiencing an issue touches someone with hands that have been washed the one touched is unclean but his garments are not unclean. However, if the one suffering the issue did not wash his hands then the garments are unclean.²⁵ there is no difference whether the one having an issue touched a person with hands that have or have not been washed. This law is similar²⁶ to the one regarding he who touches anything which is under the saddle.²⁷

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 15:31:1

**והזרתם.** יש מפרשים בו והזרתם בחסרון הה״א וזה לא יתכן כי הה״א איננו מאותיות המשך כי לא יהיה נח נעלם כי אם בסוף המלה רק פירושו כמו ונזרו מקדשי בני ישראל כעין והרחקתם וממנו נזיר שהרחיק נפשו מתאות העולם ומשקלו והפלתם את הארץ כי הנו״ן מובלע בדגש:


THUS SHALL YE SEPARATE. Some say that *ve-hizzartem* (thus shall ye separate) is missing a *heh*⁵⁵ comes from the root *zayin, heh, resh*. and is to be interpreted *ve-hizzhartem* (and you shall warn). This cannot be so, for the *heh* is not vowel letter.⁵⁶ It is only silent at the end of a word.⁵⁷ On the contrary, *ve-hizzartem* is related to the word *ve-yinnazeru* (that they separate)⁵⁸. in *that they separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel* (Lev. 22:2). The meaning of that *ve-hizzartem* is, and you shall distance.⁵⁹. The word *nazir* (nazirite) is derived from the same root. A *nazir* is one who has distanced himself from the lusts of the world. *Ve-hizzartem* is vocalized like the word *ve-hippaltem* (and you shall divide)⁶⁰. in, *and you shall divide the land* (Ezek. 45:1), for the *nun*⁶¹ and *ve-hippaltem*. is swallowed in the *dagesh*.⁶² of *ve-hizzartem* and the *peh of ve-hippaltem*.

[WHEN THEY DREW NEAR.] The word *be-korvatam* (when they drew near) is an infinitive.⁴ Compare, *le-korvah* (to come unto) in *to come unto the work* (Ex. 36:2).⁵ is made up of the infinitive *korvah* plus the pronominal suffix. The *heh* in *le-korvah* has been turned into a *tav* in *be-korvatam* as is the practice with the feminine *heh*.⁶ is connected to a pronominal suffix, the *heh* changes into a *tav*. Rabbi Joshua,⁷ who says that *be-korvatam* is a noun following the paradigm of *chokhmatam* (their wisdom) (Jer. 49:7),⁸ is made up of the noun *korvah* plus a pronominal suffix. errs.

**כתנת בד קדש.** ולא הזכיר האפוד והחשן ומעיל האפוד כי כבר הזכיר ונשמע קולו בבואו אל הקדש ומזה הכתוב למדו אנשי בית שני ששמשו בלא אורים ותומים גם נביאים היו שם:


THE HOLY LINEN TUNIC. Scripture does not mention the ephod,¹⁸ the breastplate,¹⁹ and the robe of the ephod,²⁰ for it earlier mentioned, *and the sound thereof*²¹. *shall be heard when he*²². *goeth in unto the holy place* (Ex. 28:35).²³ must wear the robe when he enters the Holy of Holies. Now, the *ephod* and the breastplate were attached to the robe. Hence there was no need for Scripture to repeat once again that Aaron shall wear these garments when he enters the Holy of Holies. Rashbam on Ex. 28:35 explains similarly. It should be noted that this interpretation is contrary to the accepted *halakhic* opinion which rules that the *kohen gadol* does not enter the Holy of Holies wearing the *ephod*, its band, the breastplate, and the robe. See *Rosh Ha-Shanah* 26a. Also see Rashi, “This teaches us that he must not officiate in the interior (the Holy of Holies) robed in the eight garments which were the insignia of the High Priest…in which he performed the service outside…but in the four garments…like an ordinary priest” (Rosenbaum and Silbermann). The men of the second temple who served without the *Urim* and the *Thummim*²⁴ learned from this verse [that their practice was proper].²⁵ and the *Thummim* in our verse, it appears that the wearing of the *Urim* and the *Thummim* is not essential for the service to be valid. There were also prophets there.²⁶ may officiate without the *Urim* and the *Thumim* if the latter are not available.

**גרלות.** ידועים מדברי קבלת אבותינו. אמר הגאון כי עזאזל שם הר ונקרא כן בעבור שהוא תקיף כי טעם זכר השם כטעם הררי אל יקותיאל והגאון הלוי תפשו כי האל״ף במלת עזאזל הוא בין זי״ן לזי״ן ויש אומרים שהוא הר סמוך אל הר סיני והשם צוה להוליך השעיר ולהעלותו שם עד שישחט ואחר כן היו מוליכים אותו בבית המקדש להר אחר והעד שאמר ויעש אהרן וכן בחג שבועות לפי דעתי כאשר אפרש במקומו ויש אומרים כי עבודת בית שני לא היתה כראשון כי היה הכהן מחוסר בגדים ואין כפרת וזה המפרש אמר כי השעיר ישלח במדבר כי כן כתוב ושלח את השעיר במדבר וטעמו כטעם צפור המטהר מהצרעת שהוא על פני השדה מקום שאין שם ישוב והעד אל ארץ גזרה ואנחנו השיבונו כי השעיר ישלחו במדבר כאשר הוא כתוב וירדוף אחריו עד שיברח ויעל אל הצור על כן אמרו חז״ל ודוחפו ואמר רב שמואל אף על פי שכתוב בשעיר החטאת שהוא לשם גם השעיר המשתלח הוא לשם ואין צריך כי המשלח איננו קרבן כי לא ישחט ואם יכולת להבין הסוד שהוא אחר מלת עזאזל תדע סודו וסוד שמו כי יש לו חברים במקרא ואני אגלה לך קצת הסוד ברמז בהיותך בן שלשים ושלש תדענו:


LOTS. We know what they are from the words of our sages.³¹ 36a. The Gaon³² says that Azazel is the name of a mountain. It is so called because of its might.³³ 63a. Azazel is a combination of *az* (strong) and *el* (tall). Azazel thus means mighty and tall mountain (Krinsky). God’s name³⁴ is mentioned in Azazel as it is in *ke-harere el* (the mighty mountains) (Ps. 36:7) and in *yakti’el* (Joktheel) (II Kings 14:7). The Gaon, the Levite,³⁵ caught him in error. He pointed out that the *alef* of Azazel is placed between one *zayin* and the other *zayin*.³⁶ in it, for the word is spelled *ayin, zayin, alef, zayin lamed*. There are those who say that Azazel is the name of a mountain close to Mount Sinai. God commanded that the goat be led and brought up there until it slipped down the mountain. Later on in the time of the temple, they led it to a different mountain. “And Aaron did” (v. 34) is proof of this.³⁷. I.E.’s point is that Scripture goes out of the way to state that Aaron did as God commanded him in the wilderness, for later on when Israel entered Israel some parts of the Yom Kippur ritual were performed a bit differently. The sending of the goat to Mount Azazel is an example. The same, in my opinion, as I will explain in its place,³⁸ is true of the festival of Shavu’ot.³⁹ There are those who say that the service⁴⁰ during the second temple was unlike that of the first, for the *kohen*⁴¹ lacked the garments⁴²., the ephod, its band, the breastplate, and the robe. and there was no ark-cover. This commentator says that the goat was sent into the wilderness, for Scripture states, *and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness* (v. 22).⁴³ The latter is similar in meaning to the bird of the one who is cleansed from leprosy⁴⁴ which is sent into the open field, an uninhabited place. *A land which is cut off*⁴⁵ (v. 22) is proof of this.⁴⁶ We answered him that they sent the goat into the wilderness as it is written.⁴⁷ However, the goat was pursued⁴⁸ until it fled and climbed up a rock. The rabbis therefore said, “and he⁴⁹ pushes it down.”⁵⁰ 67a. The point is that since a person accompanied the goat it was possible for him to push the goat off the mountain. Rabbi Samuel⁵¹ says that even though it is written that the goat offered as a sin offering is to be offered to God, the goat that was sent was also offered to God. There is no need for this interpretation, for the goat sent into the wilderness did not serve as an offering since it was not slaughtered. If you are able to understand the secret that follows Azazel⁵² (for Azazel into the wilderness). According to I.E. the word *ha-midbarah* is the key to understanding the meaning of Azazel. then you will know its secret and the secret of its name, for it has comrades in Scripture.⁵³ (goat) and *azal* (to go). There are many such compound names in Scripture. Compare, Emmanuel (God is with us). According to I. E. the meaning of *la-azazel ha-midbarah* is, for a goat that goes into the wilderness. I will reveal a bit of its secret to you in a hint. When you are thirty-three, you will understand it.⁵⁴ (satyrs). According to I.E. the *se’irim* were demons that had the shape of goats. Now it is not clear what the purpose was of sending the goat to demons who were shaped like goats. According to Nahmanides the goat was a gift to Satan so that he would not interfere with Israel’s sacrifice. However, it is doubtful that I.E. had this in mind. Weiser suggests that the goat was sent to a place of demons so that the sins which it (literally or symbolically) bore would not contaminate people, for demons dwell in a place which is uninhabited.

APPOINTED. *Itti* (appointed) means prepared for his time.⁷⁹ Or *itti* refers to an individual whose custom it was to always lead the goat on the Day of Atonement. The *yod*⁸⁰. relates to the word *et* (time).⁸¹ *Itti* is similar to *penimi* (internal).⁸² is the *yod* of relation. The *yod* suffixed to a word is often a first person pronominal suffix, hence I.E.’s comment. The interpretation of those who explain *itti* to mean wise⁸³ (ittim) (Est. 1:13). According to this interpretation a “timely” man is a man who is aware of what is currently happening, i.e., a wise man. does not appear correct to me.⁸⁴ Our sages, of blessed memory, said that the “bearer”⁸⁵ was a *kohen*.⁸⁶ 66a. Their words are true.

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 16:29:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/16:29:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/16:29:2)


**בחדש השביעי בעשור לחדש תענו את נפשותיכם.** אחר שהכתוב אומר ותתענג בדשן נפשכם ידענו כי הענוי הפך התענוג והוא הצום ועוד ונפש נענה תשביע שטעמו כמו ותפק לרעב נפשך כי דרך דברי הנביאים להכפל ואחר שיש לנו קבלה אין צורך לחפש ואין עניתי בצום נפשי ראיה בעבור זכר צום והכלל כל עינוי שימצא במקרא דבק עם נפש הוא הצום:


IN THE SEVENTH MONTH, ON THE TENTH DAY OF THE MONTH, YE SHALL AFFLICT YOUR SOULS. Since Scripture writes, *And let your soul delight itself in fatness* (Is. 55:2), we know that affliction is the reverse of delight and that affliction of the soul refers to fasting.¹⁰⁵ Furthermore, Scripture states, *And satisfy the afflicted soul* (Is. 58:10), the meaning of which is like *And if thou draw out thy soul to the hungry* (*Ibid*.), for it is the style of the prophets to repeat themselves.¹⁰⁶ is another way of saying *the afflicted soul*. We thus see that affliction of the soul refers to a lack of food. Hence it refers to fasting. Now since we have tradition¹⁰⁷ there is no reason to go on searching.¹⁰⁸ *I afflicted my soul with fasting* (Ps. 35:13) is no proof¹⁰⁹ because the word fast is mentioned.¹¹⁰ The general rule is, whenever we find in Scripture the word affliction connected to soul, the reference is to a fast.¹¹¹

¹⁰⁸ For proof that our verse speaks of fasting.

¹¹¹ Whenever the Torah speaks of the affliction of the soul the reference is to fasting.

אילו היה כתוב במחנה מותר לשחטו מחוץ למחנה וזו המצוה תלויה גם בבית המקדש רק בכל מקום שהוא קרוב לירושלים והקרוב ידענו מדברי קבלה כי אם היה המקום רחוק יזבח ויאכל בשר כי כן כתוב ורבים אמרו כי הבשר אסור בגלות ויפרשו בשר ויין לא בא אל פי בשר דג ולא דברו נכונה ואיני רוצה להאריך להשיב עליהם:


If the Torah had read, *in the camp* (v. 3),². then it would have been permissible to slaughter it³ outside the camp.⁴. Also, this⁵ commandment⁶ is dependent upon the Holy Temple.⁷ However, this law applies only to any place that is close to Jerusalem.⁸ and Rashi. We know how close from the words of tradition,⁹ 57b. for if the place is far, one is permitted to slaughter flesh.¹⁰ The latter is so, for Scripture states it.¹¹ Many say that it is forbidden to eat flesh in the exile.¹² They explain *neither came flesh nor wine in my mouth* (Dan. 10:3)¹³ as referring to the flesh of fish.¹⁴ as referring to the flesh of fish, for they maintain that one cannot eat meat outside of the Land of Israel. They did not speak correctly. I do not want to dwell on this and answer them.

**אשר הם זונים.** כי כל מי שמבקש אותם ומאמין בהם הוא זונה מתחת אלהיו שיחשוב כי יש מי שייטיב או ירע חוץ מהשם הנכבד והנורא. ובזו הפרשה לא הזכיר הגר כי המצוה על ישראל בזבחים ובעולות והזכיר הגר שלא יעזבו ישראל שיזבח הגר לעבודת כוכבים בארץ ישראל וכן משפט כל דם שהוא אסור בעבור שהוא הנפש כי הבשר בדם והאמת כי הנפש שבה יחיה האדם הוא בדם הלב:


AFTER WHOM THEY GO ASTRAY. For whoever seeks after them and believes in them strays from under his God, for he thinks that there is someone aside from God the glorious and awe inspiring who does good or bad. This section¹⁷ does not mention the stranger, for the commandment regarding sacrifices and burnt offerings falls on Israel. Scripture mentions the stranger¹⁸ in order to teach that Israel shall not permit a stranger to sacrifice to idols in the Land of Israel. The law regarding *all manner of blood* (v. 10) is similar.¹⁹ The eating of blood is prohibited²⁰ because it is the very life, for the flesh lives by the blood.²¹ The truth of the matter is that the life by which a person lives is in the blood which is in the heart.

Since Scripture mentions the beast (*chayyah*) which is not offered as a sacrifice, and similarly the fowl,³⁶ it goes on to speak of *every soul that eateth that which dieth of itself* (v. 15), which is also not offered as a sacrifice. Scripture also mentions the latter because of its reference to an animal which is taken in hunting.³⁷ (dying of itself) or *terefah* (tom), for they are taken by bow and arrow or traps. If one does so deliberately³⁸. he violates a negative precept³⁹ and is flogged.⁴⁰ also is unclean. Hence I.E. points out that he is not only unclean but he violates the law which prohibits the eating of an animal that dies of itself or is torn. If he does so accidentally, he brings a sin offering. If one should argue,⁴¹ does not Scripture state, *thou mayest give it*⁴² *unto the stranger that is within thy gates, that he may eat it* (Deut. 14:21)? The answer is that this⁴³ speaks of a stranger who dwells in the Land of Israel. Scripture similarly reads, *or the stranger that sojourneth among you* (Lev. 16:29). We shall not allow him to eat anything that dies of itself. However, we may give it⁴⁴ to the stranger that comes into our gates⁴⁵ and he will eat it outside.⁴⁶

**ערות בת אביך.** יש אומרים שהיא האחות מאב ואם ואנחנו ידענו כי השוכב עמה עובר על שני לאוין ויש אומרים כי זה הפסוק לחזוק והצדוקים אמרו שאיננה בת אם ויפרשו מולדת אביך שגדלה אביך והטעם שלקח האב אשה והיתה לה בת קטנה וכן יפרשו על תמר וראייתם כי לא ימנעני ממך רק לא היתה מולדת דוד ואחר שהמעתיקים אמרו כי בת אשת אב מותרת אין צורך להשיב על הבודאים מלבם ויתכן להיות בת אשת אביך בת אנוסה:


THE NAKEDNESS OF THY FATHER’S WIFE’S DAUGHTER. There are those who say that this refers to a sister from a father and mother.³⁶ We know³⁷ that the one who sleeps with a sister from a father and mother violates two negative laws.³⁸ There are those who say that our verse was written for emphasis.³⁹ The Sadducees⁴⁰ say that *thy father’s wife’s daughter* does not refer to the daughter of one’s mother. They explain that *begotten of thy father* means whom your father raised. Our verse deals with an instance in which the father took a woman who had a small daughter. They say the same thing regarding Tamar.⁴¹ Their proof is, *for he will not withhold me from thee* (II Sam. 13:13).⁴² She thus was not begotten by David. Now since the transmitters of tradition said that the daughter of your father’s wife is permitted, we have no need to answer those who invent things in their hearts. It is possible that “the daughter of thy father’s wife” refers to a daughter⁴³ resulting from a rape.⁴⁴

**דודתך היא.** חשובה היא כדודתך וכן הנה חנמאל דודי והנה מה יעשו הסומכים במצות על התורה לבדה כי לא אסר הכתוב אשת אחי האם ולא אם האב ולא אם האם על כן אנחנו צריכים לקבלה ויתכן שלא הזכיר אשת אחי האם כי נלמוד מאשת אחי האב והזכירה בפרשת קדושים גם הנזכרות שלא הזכירם הכתוב דבר על ההוה:


SHE IS THINE AUNT. She is considered as your aunt.⁴⁷ Similarly “Behold Hanamel, my uncle.”⁴⁸. 38 reads: *in the presence of Hanamel mine uncle* (Jer. 32:6). Be that as it may, I.E.’s point is that Hanamel was not Jeremiah’s uncle. He was the son of Jeremiah’s uncle. Nevertheless, Scripture refers to him as his uncle. Now what will those who rely on the Torah alone for the commandments⁴⁹ do? For Scripture does not prohibit the wife of the brother of one’s mother, and not the mother of one’s father, or the mother of one’s mother.⁵⁰ We therefore need tradition. It is possible that the reason that Scripture did not mention that the wife of one’s mother’s brother is prohibited is that we learn this from the prohibition of the wife of the father’s brother. The prohibition of the wife of one’s brother is mentioned in the Torah (Lev. 19:3) portion *Ye shall be holy*. Also, the reason that those whom I mentioned⁵¹ are not listed in Scripture is that the Torah speaks of that which is prevalent.⁵²

**לצרור.** מגזרת וכעסתה צרתה והנה לא הזכיר בפרשת קדושים עונש השוכב עם שתי אחיות כאשר לא הזכיר עונש השוכב עם בת בנו ועם בת בתו וטעם המפרש כי רחל ולאה לא היו אחיות וראייתו כי את כל התועבות האל וזו איננה ראיה גמורה והשואל איך יעניש השם על דבר שלא הזהיר יש משיבים כי בני נח נצטוו על העריות האלה ואחרים אמרו אף על פי שהכתוב אמר כל התועבות האל בשם כלל אין הפירוש על כולם כי אם על רובם ודעתי תדענה בפרשת וילך משה:


TO BE A RIVAL. *Li-tzeror* (to be a rival) is related to the word *tzaratah* (her rival) in *And her rival vexed her* (I Sam. 1:6). Note, Scripture does not mention in the Torah portion *Ye shall be holy* (Lev. 19:2)⁵⁴ lists those with whom one is not permitted to have sexual intercourse and the punishment for violating these prohibitions. the punishment for sleeping with two sisters, and it does not mention the punishment for sleeping with the daughter of one’s son and with the daughter of one’s daughter.⁵⁵ The one who says that Rachel and Leah⁵⁶ were not sisters⁵⁷ errs. His proof is, *for all these abominations…* (Lev. 18:27).⁵⁸ However, this is not a rigorous proof. There are those who answer the one who asks, how could God punish for something He did not warn against,⁵⁹ by saying the sons of Noah were warned about these sexual offenses. Others say⁶⁰ that even though Scripture makes a general statement, *for all these abominations…*, the reference is not to all these abominations but to most of them.⁶¹ You will learn my opinion⁶² in the Torah portion *And Moses went* (Deut. 31:1).⁶³

**ואל אשת עמיתך.** להוציא השבויה ויש אומרים כי כבר היתה אסורה ואשר גברה תאות יצרם על דעת לבם תעו בפירוש לזרע וידענו כי המשגל נחלק לג׳‎ חלקים האחד לפריה ורביה בלא תאוה והשני להקל מלאות הגוף והשלישי לתאוה הנמשלת לתאות הבהמה ואחר שאמר הכתוב לזרע שטעמו אפילו לזרע הנה היא אסורה אסור חמור ומזרעך לא תתן הבא אחריו לעד. והוסיף לטמאה בה כי לא ינקה כל הנוגע בה והוא טמא לעולם ובפרשה הזה לא אסר הנכרית כלל ואין טענה מהשבויה כי היא מתייהדת:


WITH THY NEIGHBOR’S WIFE. This excludes the captive woman.⁶⁵ There are those who say that she⁶⁶ was previously prohibited. Those whose sexual craving⁶⁷ overcame the intelligence of their heart erred in explaining the meaning of *le-zara*⁶⁸ (carnally).⁶⁹ We know that sexual intercourse is divided into three groups. One, to be fruitful and multiply⁷⁰ and not to satisfy lust. Two, to relieve the fullness of the body.⁷¹ 3:2, “He will…not engage in sexual intercourse whenever he lusts, but only when he knows that he has to ejaculate for reasons of health.” Three, for the purpose of lust, which is similar to the lust of an animal.⁷² Now since Scripture says *le-zara* (carnally), the meaning of which is even for seed,⁷³ a married woman is prohibited by a very severe prohibition.⁷⁴ *And thou shalt not give any of thy seed to set them apart to Molech* (v. 21) is proof.⁷⁵ (for seed) means for the purpose of children, for the word seed in verse 21 definitely applies to children. Scripture adds to *defile thyself with her* to let us know that the one who touches her will not be cleansed; he will be defiled forever. This verse⁷⁶ does not at all prohibit a non-Jewish woman.⁷⁷. 38 reads: This verse (verse 21) prohibits all non-Jewish women. There is no argument from the captive woman,⁷⁸ for she converts to Judaism.

TO MOLECH. Molech is the name of an image. The rabbis interpreted Molech as a general term for all⁷⁹ whom a person accepts as a king over him.⁸⁰ (king). It is possible that Molech is the abomination of the Ammonites.⁸¹

ומלת **להעביר.** כמו לשרוף כי זאת היתה עבודתו ויש אומרים כי יעביר הבן על האש ויש מי שיחיה ויש מי שימות ואחרים פירשו בעבור שאין בפסוק זכר אש להעביר מתורת השם לדת המולך וחללת השם שהוא נקרא עליך שהוא אלהיך בתתך מזרע קודש למולך. והגאון אמר כי הנאוף על שמנה מעלות והקשה שבכלם הבהמה שהיא ממין אחר ואחריה הזכר שכל המין אסור ואחריה ערות אשת אב וחביריה שהן אסורו בכל עת ולא אאריך כי לא יועילו אלו הדברים כי הכתוב אמר על כלם ונכרתו הנפשות העושות:


The word *le-ha’avir* (to set apart) is to burn, for that was the way Molech was worshipped. Some say that they used to pass⁸² (to set apart) literally means to pass over. their sons over the fire. Some lived and some died. In view of the fact that the verse does not mention fire, some explained *le-ha’avir lamolekh* (to set apart to Molech) as meaning to cause to pass over from the Torah of God to another religion.⁸³ You will defile the Lord who is known as your God⁸⁴ when you give from the holy seed to Molech. The Gaon says that fornication has eight levels.⁸⁵ The most severe is intercourse with a beast of another species; afterwards comes the male, the entire gender of which is prohibited; afterwards comes the nakedness of the father’s wife and her companions,⁸⁶ which are prohibited at all times. I will not dwell on this, for what purpose is there to these words since Scripture says, concerning all of them, *even the souls that do them shall be cut off* (v. 29).

**ואת זכר.** אחר שמצאנו הן שכבתי אמש את אבי הנה אזהרה לשוכב ולנשכב ויאמר רב חננאל ז״ל כי יש מי שיחדש בגופו כצורת בשר אשה וזה לא יתכן בתולדה ויש אומרים אנדרוגינוס וכל הצער הזה בעבור היות משכבי אשה לשון רבים ודברי יחיד שני משכבים והנכון בעיני כי המצוה כפשוטה גם אנשי התושיה חייבו מיתה עליה והכתוב אחז דרך כבוד לאמר כמו לא תקרב ואחר שהזכר נברא לעשות והנקבה להעשות הזהיר הכתוב שלא תהפוך דברי השם ויש משכב להוציא הזרע על כן מלת משכבי לשון רבים. ואין ראוי להאריך:


WITH MANKIND. Since we find, *Behold, I lay yester-night with my father* (Gen. 19:34), we see that the prohibition⁸⁷. applies to the one who lay and the one who is lain with.⁸⁸. Rabbi Hannanel, of blessed memory, says that there are those in whose body a female genitalia is newly formed.⁸⁹ However, this is impossible according to the laws of nature.⁹⁰ There are those who say that the reference is to an androgynous person. All this pain was caused by the fact that Scripture employs the plural *mishkeve ishah* (as with womankind).⁹¹ is “intercourses of a woman.” Intercourses is plural. It implies more than one type of intercourse, i.e., anal and vaginal intercourse. There is an individual opinion⁹². 55a. that *mishkeve ishah* refers to two types of intercourse.⁹³ I believe that the precept is to be taken literally.⁹⁴ The men of sound wisdom⁹⁵ also applied the death penalty to those who performed this act.⁹⁶ 83b. Scripture employed respectable language in saying [thou shalt not lie].⁹⁷ is a euphemism for intercourse. Compare, *thou shalt not approach* (v. 14).⁹⁸ is a euphemism for intercourse. Now, since the male was created to make⁹⁹ and the female to be made,¹⁰⁰ Scripture notes that one should not reverse the words of God. There is a type of laying whose aim is to emit semen.¹⁰¹ literally means layings of. I.E.’s point is that *mishkeve* here refers to laying down for the purpose of pouring seed; i.e., it is a euphemism for intercourse. Hence Scripture employs the term *mishkeve* which is a plural.¹⁰² (Krinsky). It is unfit to dwell at length on this.

**תבל הוא.** אנשי הדקדוק אמרו שזאת המלה מהכפל כמו תמס יהלוך והתי״ו נוסף ואמרו כי טעמה כמו השחתה ויש אומרים כי גם מבול ממנו וקרוב מגזרת בלל ה׳‎ שפת כל הארץ וזה הכלל אסר הכתוב כל מין שיוכל האדם להתייחד עמם אשת איש ונכריה ואשר לא יוליד כי מין לא יוליד כי אם ממינו וכמינו:


IT IS PERVERSION. The grammarians say that the word *tevel* (perversion) comes from a double root.¹¹⁰. Compare, *temes* (melteth)¹¹¹. in *which melteth and passeth away* (Ps. 58:9). The *tav* of *tevel* is superfluous.¹¹² They say that *tevel* means destruction.¹¹³ There are those who say that the word *mabbul* (flood) is related to it.¹¹⁴ means destruction. However, the word *mabbul* is most likely related to the word *balal* (confound) in *the Lord did there confound the language of all the earth* (Gen. 11:9). This is the general rule: Scripture prohibits all kinds of women with which it is possible for a person to be alone;¹¹⁵ a married woman, a non-Jewish woman,¹¹⁶. 38 quoted in note 77. and those with whom intercourse cannot result in children,¹¹⁷ for a kind cannot reproduce except with its own kind and with those like its kind.

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 18:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/18:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/18:28:1)


**כאשר קאה.** פועל עבר מגזרת שתו ושכרו וקיו כי אותיות אהו״י מתחלפים ויש ארץ לשון זכר נעתם ארץ ולא נשא אותם הארץ או חסר מלת היא כאילו הוא כאשר היא קאה כמו באה עם הצאן:


AS IT VOMITED OUT. *Ka’ah* (vomited out) is a verb in the perfect. It is related to the word *keyo* (spew)¹³⁰. in *Drink ye, and be drunken, and spew* (Jer. 25:27), for the letters *alef, heh, vav, yod* interchange.¹³¹ of *ka’ah* is in place of a *yod*. The word *eretz* is found in the masculine.¹³² is masculine. Hence the noun *eretz*, which it governs, has to be masculine. Compare, *netam aretz* (the land burnt up)¹³³ is masculine. Hence the noun *aretz*, which it governs, is masculine. (Is. 9:18), and *ve-lo nasa otam ha-aretz* (and the land was not able to bear them)¹³⁴ is masculine. Hence the noun *eretz*, which it governs, is masculine. (Gen. 13:6).¹³⁵ is usually feminine. Hence I.E.’s comment. On the other hand, the word *hiy* (it)¹³⁶ might be missing.¹³⁷ is a feminine participle from the root *kof, alef, heh*, and *eretz* is feminine. Our verse should be interpreted as if it read, *ka’asher hiy ka’ah* (as it vomited out). In this case, *ka’ah* is similar to *ba’ah* (cometh) in *cometh with the sheep* (Gen. 29:6).¹³⁸ is a feminine participle from the root *bet, alef, heh*.

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:2:1)


טעם **אל כל עדת בני ישראל.** להכניס את הגרים בעבור שהם נזהרים על העריות כישראלים:


[UNTO ALL THE CONGREGATION OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.] The reason that Scripture states *unto all the congregation of the children of Israel* is to exclude strangers¹ 38. *Mikra’ot Gedolot* reads, *The reason why Scripture states unto all the congregation of the children of Israel is to include the strangers*. The reading in *Vat. Ebr.* 38 appears correct, for *unto all the congregation of the children of Israel* seems to imply that what follows only applies to the children of Israel. Furthermore, in his comments on Lev. 20:1, I.E. explicitly says that our chapter applies only to the children of Israel. By strangers I.E. means non-Jews living in Israel. See I.E. on Ex. 20:9 (Vol. 2, p. 427). since they, like the Israelites, are commanded to abstain from prohibited sexual relations.

¹ So Vat. Ebr.


###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:2:2)


וטעם להזכיר זאת הפרשה אחרי העריות שלא יחשבו כי בעבור שמירת העריות לבדם יעמדו בארץ אמר להם שגם יש מצות אחרות אם לא תשמרום תגורשו מן הארץ והם עשרת הדברים הנזכרים כי הנה הזהיר על עבודת כוכבים אחר שאמר כי קדוש אני ה׳‎ כי הוא כנגד הדבור הראשון על דעת רבים ולא תשבעו בשמי הוא דבור לא תשא ואת שבתתי תשמרו זכור את יום השבת גם איש אמו ואביו תיראו הוא דבור כבד את אביך ואת אמך גם לא תעמוד על דם רעך דבור לא תרצח. ודבר השפחה הנחרפת אזהרת לא תנאף עם שהיא חפשית. גם לא תגנובו ולא תכחשו ולא תשקרו ולא תעשוק את רעך כנגד השלשה הנשארים:


The reason this chapter follows the one dealing with prohibited sexual relations is that the Israelites should not imagine that they would remain in the land by observing only the laws dealing with the prohibited sexual relations. God informs them that there are other commandments. If they do not observe them, they will be exiled from the land. The aforementioned are the ten statements.² God warns against idol worship after stating, *I the Lord…am holy* which, according to many commentators, is parallel to the first statement of the Decalogue.³ (Ex. 20:7). *And ye shall not swear by my name falsely* (v. 12) is parallel to *Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain* (Ex. 20:7).

### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:3:1)


וכבר אמרתי לך בפרשת ואלה המשפטים שכל מצוה ומצוה עומדת בפני עצמה לכן יש כדמות סמך להדביק הפסוקים. והנה פרשת קדושים תחלתו איש אמו ואביו תיראו והנה אמר כי יאריכון ימי המכבד אם כן יקצרון ימי המקלה על כן אמר תיראו וטעם להזכיר האם קודם האב כי הקטן איננו מכיר בתחלה כי אם אמו ואחר כן אביו ואחר כן שבת כי מצוה על הקטן לשמור את השבת ואין ככה שאר המועדים ואחר כן יכיר אלהיו ששבת ביום השביעי ואחריו אל תפנו אל האלילים ומורא האבות ידוע מהקבלה. ואמר איש פעם אחת דרך קצרה. ואמר תיראו לשון רבים כי חייבים הרואים ללמדו ולהכריחו וכן בשמירת שבת:


AND YE SHALL KEEP MY SABBATHS. This parallels *Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy* (Ex. 20:8). *Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father* is similar to *Honor thy father and thy mother* (Ex. 20:12). *Neither shalt thou stand idly by the blood of thy neighbor* (v. 16) is likewise the same as the statement *Thou shalt not murder* (Ex. 20:13). The law regarding the bondmaid designated for a man (v. 20) is parallel to *Thou shalt not commit adultery* (Ex. 20:13 with a free woman. Similarly, *Ye shall not steal; neither shall ye deal falsely, nor lie one to another* (v. 11); *Thou shalt not oppress thy neighbor* (v. 13) are parallel to the three remaining statements.⁴ is parallel to *Thou shalt not steal* (Ex. 20:13). *Neither shall ye deal falsely, nor lie one to another* is parallel to *Thou shalt not bear false witness* (*Ibid*.). *Thou shalt not oppress thy neighbor* is parallel to *Thou shalt not covet* (Ex. 20:14). I have previously told you in my comments on the Torah portion *Ve-Elleh Ha-Mishpatim* (now these are the ordinances) (Ex. 21:1) that each and every precept stands by itself.⁵ However,⁶ (literally, therefore). However, I.E. occasionally uses the term *lakhen* in the sense of however (Filwarg). It is also possible that we should read *akeh* rather than *lakhen*. there is some support for connecting the verses.⁷ Note, the section that opens with the words *Ye shall be holy* (v. 2) begins with *Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father* (v. 3). Now Scripture tells us that the years of the one who honors his parents will be long (Ex. 20:12). This implies that the days of one who disrespects his parents will be shortened. Scripture therefore says, *Ye shall fear*.⁸. The implication is that one who disrespects his parents will suffer premature death. According to I.E. the meaning of *Ye shall fear every man his mother, and father* is, be afraid of disrespecting your parents, for if you dishonor them you will suffer dire consequences. Our verse is thus parallel to Ex. 20:12. The reason Scripture mentions the mother before the father is that a child first recognizes only its mother.⁹ Then it recognizes its father. The Torah next mentions the Sabbath because, unlike all the other festivals, a child is commanded to keep the Sabbath.¹⁰ The child shall then recognize his God who rested on the seventh day.¹¹. I.E. speaks of a progression. The child learns to recognize its mother, then its father, and then God. Scripture next mentions, *Turn ye not unto the idols* (v. 4). We know from tradition what Scripture means by fearing parents.¹² fearing one’s father refers to sitting in his place, speaking in his turn, and contradicting him. See *Sifra* on this verse. Our verse employs the word *ish* (every man) once¹³. See Lev. 17:3,10,13; Lev. 15:2. because it wants to be brief. Scripture employs the plural *tira’u* (ye shall fear)¹⁴ is in the singular. Thus the verb governing it should be in the singular. Hence I.E.’s comment. because those who observe the child have to teach him and force him to fear his parents. It is the same case regarding Sabbath observance.¹⁵

**האלילים.** הם הפסילים ונקראו כן כי הם דבר שקר כמו רופאי אליל כלכם ויתכן להיות מגזרת אל והטעם שאיננו יש:


UNTO THE IDOLS.¹⁷. The reference is to statues. They are called *elilim* because they are false objects. Compare the word *elil* (no value) in *Ye are physicians of no value* (Job 13:4). It is possibly related to the word *al* (not). *Elilim* means things that do not exist.

NOR…MOLTEN GODS. Made to receive power from those who are on high, for there is no need for another god along with Me.¹⁸ Scripture therefore states,¹⁹ *I am the Lord your God*. ### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:8:1

**ואכליו.** כל אחד מאוכליו וכן וצדיקים ככפיר יבטח:


BUT EVERY ONE THAT EATETH IT. The meaning of *okhelav* is every one that eats of it.²³ is a plural. It literally means they that eat of it. Our verse thus literally reads, they that eat of it shall bear his iniquity. Hence I.E.’s interpretation. Similarly *But the righteous are secure as a young lion*²⁴ (Prov. 28:1).²⁵

**כי את קדש ה׳‎ חלל.** אחר שהקריב האימורים לגבוה הנה כל הבשר קדש. וחלל מגזרת חול שאין לו טעם כדמות חלל. ובפרשה הזאת באר עונש העון ונכרתה הנפש ההוא:


BECAUSE HE HATH PROFANED THE HOLY THING OF THE LORD. After he offered the parts designated to God by Scripture, all the flesh²⁶ is holy. *Chillel* (profaned) is related to the word *chol* (profane). It is something that has no significance.²⁷ It is like an empty space (*challel*). In this section²⁸ Scripture explains the punishment,²⁹ namely, *and that soul shall be cut off*.

וטעם **ובקצרכם.** אחר זבח שלמים כאשר נתת לשם האימורים כן תתנו מקציר ארצכם לכבוד השם לעני ולגר. ודקדוק בקצרכם זר והוא שם הפעל מן הקל:


[AND WHEN YE REAP THE HARVEST.] This follows the law dealing with the peace offering, for as you gave to God the parts designated in Scripture, so shall you, out of respect for God, give what Scripture designates from the harvest of your land³⁰ for the poor and the stranger. The word *u-ve-kutzrekhem* (and when ye reap the harvest) is grammatically irregular.³¹ rather than with a *kubbutz*. In other words, *u-ve-kutzrekhem* should have read *u-ve-kotzrekhem*. It is an infinitive³² in the *kal*.

### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:10:1)


**תעולל.** תכרית העוללות הם הקטנים כמו עולל גם יקראו יונקות וזאת המלה כמו ושרשך מארץ חיים שטעמו יכרית השרש וכן מסעף פארה יכרות הסעיף:


GLEAN. *Te’olel* (glean) means to cut off the *olelot*, that is the young grapes. Compare, *olel* (young child). Very young children are also called *yonekot* (sucklings).³⁴ (young children and the sucklings). This word³⁵ means a young child or a young plant. *Te’olel* thus appears to mean to plant a young shoot. However, it has the opposite meaning. It means to harvest a young plant. Thus a word coming from a root meaning a young plant can, in the *pi’el*, have the opposite meaning, i.e., to destroy a young plant. is similar to *shereshkha* (root thee out)³⁶ comes from the stem meaning root. Thus the word might be taken to mean to root. However, it has the opposite meaning in the *pi’el*. in *And root thee out of the land of the living* (Ps. 52:7), the meaning of which is, to cut the root. Similarly the meaning *of mesa’ef*³⁷ comes from the same root as *se’if* (a branch). However, in the *p’iel* it means to cut the branches. *purah* (Is. 10:33) is to lop the boughs.

footnotes:
³⁴ See Lam. 2:11, olel ve-yonek
³⁵ Olel
³⁶ Shereshkha
³⁷ Mesa’ef

**ופרט.** ידוע בדברי קבלה מגזרת הפורטים על פי הנבל:


THE FALLEN FRUIT. The meaning of *peret* (fallen fruit) is known in the words of tradition.³⁸ is often used in Rabbinic tradition and there has the meaning of that which is singled out. See *Sotah* 37b; *Chagigah* 6a. Thus *peret* means the single grapes that fall off the vine. See *Pe’ah* 6:5, *Two grapes are peret; three are not peret*. It is related to the word *poretim* (thrum)³⁹ means those that pluck on each one of the strings of the psaltery. in *That thrum on the psaltery* (Amos 6:5).

³⁸ The word perat
³⁹ According to I.E. ha-poretim…al ha-navel

FOR THE POOR. Of Israel.

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:13:3)


**פעלת.** כמו שכירות וכן ופעולתו לפניו ויתכן היותו דרך קצרה והטעם שכר פעולתו ורבים פירשוהו על שכיר יום שיאמרו לו גם תעשה בבקר ובבקר אתן לך שכר שני ימים והמעתיקים אמרו כי הוא שכיר יום כי שכיר לילה לא תבוא עליו השמש.


THE WAGES. *Pe’ulat* means the wages of.⁴⁸ literally means labor of. Hence I.E.’s comment. Compare, *Behold, His reward* (u-fe’ulato) *is with Him* (Is. 40:10). It is possible that Scripture is elliptical and that *pe’ulat* is short for *sekhar pe’ulato* (the wages of his labor). Many say that Scripture speaks of a person hired for the day.⁴⁹ One is not permitted to tell him to work the next morning and in the morning say I will pay you for two days’ work. The transmitters of tradition⁵⁰ 61a. say that our verse⁵¹ refers to someone hired for a day,⁵² for the sun is not permitted to set on a worker⁵³ who is hired for the night.⁵⁴

footnotes:
⁴⁸ The word pe’ulat
⁴⁹ According to this opinion a person hired for the day must be paid as soon as the day is over.
⁵⁰ See Bava Metzi’a
⁵¹ Which states that a worker must be paid before the morning.
⁵² According to the rabbis a person hired for the day must be paid before the arrival of the next morning.
⁵³ An unpaid worker.
⁵⁴ That is, the verse in Deut. 19:24 which states that a worker’s wages are to be paid before the sun sets speaks of a worker hired for the night; that is, the employer has the entire following day to pay him.

**רכיל.** כמו רכולתך מכל אבקת רוכל והטעם המלשין כי הרוכל מעתיק יקנה מזה וימכור לזה והרכיל יגלה לזה מה ששמע מזה:


A TALEBEARER. The word *rakhil* (talebearer) is similar to *rekhulltekh* (thy merchandise) (Ezek. 26:12) and *rokhel* (merchant) in *With all powders of the merchant* (Cant. 3:6). *Rakhil* means a slanderer, for the merchant moves goods. (thy neighbor) is superfluous.⁶⁷ literally, then our verse reads, but thou shalt love to thy neighbor as thyself. This does not appears to make sense. Hence this interpretation means that we should ignore the *lamed* prefixed to *re’akha* and interpret our verse as reading, but thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself. I believe that *le-re’akha* is to be taken literally.⁶⁹ of *le-re’akha* (thy neighbor) is not superfluous. ### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:19:1)


וטעם להזכיר אחר אלה המצות **בהמתך לא תרביע כלאים.** להזהיר אחר היותך קדוש שלא תעשה חמס לבן אדם כמוך גם לא תעשה לבהמה לשנות מעשה השם על כן כתוב את חקתי תשמרו לשמור כל מין שלא יתערב מין עם מין:


[THOU SHALT NOT LET THY CATTLE GENDER WITH A DIVERSE KIND.] The reason Scripture states *Thou shalt not let thy cattle gender with a diverse kind* is to warn us. Since you are holy, in that you do not act violently towards your fellow human being, you must also not do anything to an animal which entails changing God’s work. Scripture therefore reads, *Ye shall keep My statutes*; that is, each species is to be preserved. A kind is not to interbreed with another kind.


###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:19:2)


**כלאים.** שני מינים ועוד אפרש מלת כלאים. וטעם השדה והבגד להיות לזכרון כי יש מצות רבות לזכר כחג המצות וסוכות וציצית ושופר ומזוזה ותפילין. ופה ארמוז לך סוד דע כי השלם שלם מאד על כן כתוב באברהם וישמור משמרתי מצותי חקותי ותורותי:


WITH A DIVERSE KIND. *Kilayim* (a diverse kind) means two kinds. I will yet explain the meaning of *kilayim*.⁷¹ The reason for the law regarding a field and a garment is that they serve as reminders,⁷² for many commandments serve as reminders. Examples of the latter are: the festival of unleavened bread,⁷³ Sukkot,⁷⁴ serve as a reminder of booths in which the Israelites dwelled during their sojourn in the desert (Lev. 23:43). *tzitzit*,⁷⁵ serve as a reminder of God’s commandments (Num. 15:39). *shofar*,⁷⁶ is to serve as a reminder, among them, God’s revelation, to repent. *mezuzah*,⁷⁷ and *tefilin*.⁷⁸ serves a reminder of the Exodus (Ex. 13:9) and of our obligation to study and to teach Torah to our children (Deut: 6:4-9; 13-21). See *Yesod Mora*, Chapter 5. I will hint to you here at a secret. Know that “the complete is very complete.”⁷⁹ Scripture therefore says with regard to Abraham,⁸⁰ *and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws* (Gen. 26:5).⁸¹

### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:20:1)


**והוא שפחה.** אמרו המכחישים כי איננה יהודית והנכון על דרך הפשט שהיא הנזכרת בפרשת וכי ימכור איש את בתו לאמה והיא ישראלית והטעם שהוא יעדה שיקחנה אדוניה או בנו ואיננה מאורסה וזה טעם כי לא חפשה איננה חפשית עד שתהיה מאורסה כמשפט הבנות:


A BONDMAID, DESIGNATED FOR A MAN. The deniers⁸⁶ say that the bondmaid is not a Jewess. However, the correct interpretation according to the plain meaning of the text is that the bondmaid is the one mentioned in *And if a man sell his daughter to be a maid-servant* (Ex. 21:7) and that she is an Israelite. Our verse deals with an instance in which the bondmaid was designated for marriage to her master or his son.⁸⁷ However, she had not undergone the first stage of marriage.⁸⁸. During the period of *erusin*, which lasted for a year, the bride remained with her family. In the second stage, called *nesu’im*, the bride went to live with her husband. The meaning of *nor was freedom given her* is that she is not free until she undergoes the first stage of marriage as is the practice of young ladies.

FREEDOM. The *shuruk*⁸⁹. in *chufshah* (freedom) is in place of a furtive *kamatz*, for the individual form of the word is *chofesh*.⁹⁰ are vocalized with a *kamatz katan* when declined. Compare, *kotel, kotlah*; *chodesh, chodshah*. Thus *chufshah* should have read *chofshah*, for the word *chufshah* (freedom) is the word *chofesh* plus the pronominal suffix. Scripture states, *nor was freedom given her*, because it was traditional to write a writ of manumission⁹¹ if her father sold her for a set time. The transmitters of tradition said that our verse speaks of a woman who was half free and half servant.⁹² 2:5. “What manner of bondwoman [does Scripture speak of in Lev. 19:20]? She that is half bondwoman and half freedwoman.” What they said is true.

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:20:5

**בקרת תהיה.** יש אומרים שפירושו כמו פילגש ואמרו כי כן בנות מלכים ביקרותיך ולא פרשו נכון כי ביקרותיך טעמו השפחות היקרות ונעלם היו״ד בעבור האות המשרת בחיר״ק והיה בחיר״ק בעבור התחברות שני שואי״ן נעים האחד תחת האות המשרת והשני תחת האות הראשון של השרש בלשון נקבות ואין כח בלשון להזכיר ככה וכן משפט כל הלשון ואין מלה זרה חוץ ממלת ורבים מישני אדמת עפר יקיצו על קריאת בן נפתלי. ויש אומרים בקורת מגזרת לא יבקר הכהן והטעם שיחפש הדבר והמעתיקים אמרו כי יש עליו מלקות ברצועה של בקר וזה אמת מדברי קבלה והמלה כדמות אסמכתא. וטעם להזכיר זאת הפרשה כי הוא עושק אדני השפחה על כן יביא איל אשם ועוד על דרך דרש שזאת השכיבה כמו כלאים חפשי עם שפחה:


THERE SHALL BE AN INQUISITION. Some say that *bikkoret* (inquisition) means a concubine.⁹³ (there shall be an inquisition) as she shall be a concubine; that is, she shall not be considered a fully married woman. They say that the same applies to the word *biykkrotekha* (among thy favorites) in *Kings’ daughters are among thy favorites* (Ps. 45:10).⁹⁴ However, they did not explain it correctly, for the meaning of *biykkrotekha* is, among the precious handmaidens.⁹⁵ is the word *yikkrotekha* (your precious ones), i.e., your precious maidens plus the *bet* prefix. There is no connection between *bikkoret* and *biykkrotekha*, for the former comes from the root *bet, kof, resh* and the latter from the root *yod, kof, resh*. The *yod*⁹⁶. is missing⁹⁷ because the *bet*, which serves as a preposition, is vocalized with a *chirik*.⁹⁸ of *yikkrotekha* is swallowed up by the *chirik*. It is vocalized with a *chirik* because of the confluence of two mobile *shevas*,⁹⁹ is a combination of the prefix *be* plus the word *yekkrotekha*. In such cases the prefix is vocalized with a *chirik* and the *yod* is not sounded. the first beneath the prefix¹⁰⁰. and the second beneath the first root letter of the word *yikkrotekha*, which is in the feminine.¹⁰¹. The tongue does not have the power to enunciate two mobile *shevas* in succession.¹⁰² back to back. The same is true for the entire language.¹⁰³. It applies to all cases where we have two furtive *shevas* in succession. There is no exception to this except for the word *mi-yeshene* (that sleep) in *And many of them that sleep in the dust* (Dan. 12:2),¹⁰⁴ should have read *miyyshene*. according to the reading of Ben Naphtali.¹⁰⁵ There are those who say that *bikkoret* is related to the word *yevakker* (seek) in *shall not seek* (Lev. 13:36). The meaning of *bikkoret*¹⁰⁶ is that the matter shall be searched out. The transmitters of tradition say he¹⁰⁷ 11a it is the bondwoman who is lashed. Hence some emend *alav* to *aleha*. incurs the penalty of being lashed with a strap made from the skin of cattle (*bakar*).¹⁰⁸ 3:12. This interpretation renders *bikkoret* as cattled, i.e., lashed with a strap made of cattle hide. In our texts of Rabbinic literature there is no such interpretation. Radak quotes this interpretation in the name of Rabbi Saadiah Gaon. See Weiser. This is true by way of tradition.¹⁰⁹ The word *bikkoret* is used as a support for the tradition.¹¹⁰ is not “lashed by cattle skin.” This section is placed here because the one who sleeps with the bondwoman oppresses the master of the bondwoman.¹¹¹ He therefore brings a ram as a guilt offering.¹¹² Furthermore, this type of intercourse can be interpreted midrashically as mixing diverse kinds, namely, a free man and a bondwoman.¹¹³

### Verse 26

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:26:1)


**לא תאכלו על הדם.** דבוק עם הכתוב למעלה כי הזהיר על עץ נטוע שלא יאכלו מפריו עד השנה החמישית גם כן כל בשר טהור לא יאכל עד שיזרוק דמו על מזבח השם אם היה קרוב אל מקום הקדש והעד הנאמן דברי שאול כי הארון היה עמו כי כן כתוב הנה אוכלים על הדם כאילו אוכלים זבחים לשעירים כאשר פירשתי שהיה כן מנהגם במצרים לזבוח בשם השדים כי אחר שלא נזרק הדם על המזבח לשם השם הנה הדבר ברור על כן דבק עמו לא תנחשו כי במצרים היו אוכלים על הדם וזונים אחרי השדים ובארץ כנען מנחשים ומעוננים כי כן כתוב גם זה כמעשה ארץ מצרים וכמעשה ארץ כנען. ומלת מנחש מנסה כמו נחשתי ויברכני ה׳‎ כי נחוש בצורות ובמקלות ובמעשים ובתנועות ובימים ושעות:


YE SHALL NOT EAT WITH THE BLOOD. This is connected¹²⁹ to what is written above it.¹³⁰ Scripture warned against eating from the fruit of any planted tree until the fifth year. It similarly also prohibited one, if he is in the proximity of the sanctuary, to eat from any permitted flesh unless its blood first be sprinkled on the altar of God. The account of King Saul is a faithful witness to this interpretation, for the ark of the Lord was with Saul, and Scripture explicitly states, “Behold, the people are eating with the blood.”¹³¹. As I explained,¹³² it was as if the people were sacrificing to the demons, for this was their custom in Egypt. There they were accustomed to sacrifice in the name of the demons. Now this is clear,¹³³ is clear (Krinsky). since the blood was not poured on the altar in the worship of God. *Neither shall ye practice divination* is connected to *ye shall not eat with the blood* because they used to eat with the blood and go astray after the demons in Egypt, and they used to practice divination and soothsaying in Canaan. The aforementioned is clearly stated in Scripture.¹³⁴ This too was like the *doings of the land of Egypt;*…and…*the doings of the land of Canaan* (Lev. 18:3). The word *menachesh* means divines. Compare, *I have observed the signs* (nichashti), *And the Lord hath blessed me* (Gen. 30:27). Divinations take many forms. There are types of divination that employs images,¹³⁵ sticks,¹³⁶ actions,¹³⁷ movements,¹³⁸ days,¹³⁹ and hours.¹⁴⁰

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:26:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:26:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:26:2)


**תעוננו.** יש אומרים מלשון ענה שיחשוב בלבו דבר ויטה אזניו לשמוע מה יענה המדבר ולא אבה הדקדוק ויש אומרים מעונן לשון ועונתה לא יגרע והנכון בעיני מגזרת ענן כי ידוע כי יש מי שיעונן שיסתכל בעננים ובדמותם ובתנועתם ויתכן להיות תעוננו מפעלי הכפל כמו תסובבו כי מצאנו ועוננים כפלשתים כי יתכן היותו מבנין הכפול והעד ומעונן ומנחש:


SOOTHSAYING. Some say that the word *te’onennu* (soothsaying) is related to the word *anah* (answer). The soothsayer imagines something in his heart and inclines his ear to hear what the speaker will answer.¹⁴¹ means “and do not practice answering.” However, the rule of grammar rejects this interpretation.¹⁴² (answer) comes from the root *ayin, nun, heh*. Verbs from this root do not double their middle stem. There are those who say that *te’onennu* comes from the word *onah* (time). It is similar to the word *onatah* (her conjugal rights)¹⁴³ in *and her conjugal rights, shall he not diminish* (Ex. 21:10).¹⁴⁴ is, and do not set times; that is, do not divine by setting aside lucky days. However, it appears to me that *te’onennu* is related to the word *anan* (cloud), for it is known that the one who practices divination looks at the clouds and observes their forms and their movements. *Te’onennu* probably comes from a verb with a doubled root.¹⁴⁵. It is like the word *tesovevu* (you will go round about),¹⁴⁶. for we find, *And with soothsayers* (onenim) *like the Philistines* (Is. 2:6).¹⁴⁷ is a *kal*. There is no question that *onenim* comes from the root *ayin, nun, nun*. [I note this] for it is possible that *te’onennu* is a doubled form.¹⁴⁸. A verb which has a *vav* as it middle letter has its last stem letter doubled in the *pi’el*. In other words, the root of *te’onennu* is *ayin, vav, nun*. The last stem letter is doubled in the *pi’el*. Compare, *te-komem* from *kof, vav, mem*. *Me’onen* (one that uses divination) *u-menachesh* (Deut. 18:9) is proof.

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 19:28:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:28:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/19:28:2)


ומלת **לנפש.** הגוף המת וכן מתורגם והוא האמת ולא נדגש הנו״ן להקל על הלשון:


The word *le-nefesh* means for a dead body. It is also so rendered in the Aramaic translation.¹⁵⁰. This is its true meaning. The *nun*¹⁵¹. does not receive a *dagesh*¹⁵², or *kamatz*. If it is vocalized with *a pattach*, the letter which follows it receives a *dagesh*. I.E. explains that Scripture chose to vocalize *la-nefesh* with a *kamatz* to simplify enunciation (Weiser). However, it should be noted that if the *lamed* of *la-nefesh* was vocalized with a *sheva*, then the *nun* would also not receive a *dagesh*. Thus I.E.’s interpretation does not explain why the *lamed* of *la-nefesh* was not vocalized with a *sheva*. It is possible that in I.E.’s version of the Torah *la-nefesh* was vocalized with a *pattach* and that I.E. is explaining why, contrary to the laws of grammar, there is no *dagesh* in the *nun* of *la-nefesh*. in order to simplify enunciation.

¹⁵⁰ Onkelos renders la-nefesh, al mit
¹⁵¹ Of la-nefesh
¹⁵² A preposition prefixed to a stressed syllable of a noun can be vocalized with a sheva, pattach

### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 20:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/20:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/20:1:1)


וטעם **וידבר ה׳‎ אל משה לאמר.** בעבור כי אלה המצות חיוב על כל ישראל ואין גר עמם על כן כתוב בתחלה אל כל עדת ישראל ועתה יחל להזכיר עונש הזנות על כל מי שהוא דר בא״י אזרח או גר תושב והחל מהקשה שבכלם והוא אשר יתן מזרעו למולך והטעם לשכב עם עובדת עבודת כוכבים:


[AND THE LORD SPOKE UNTO MOSES, SAYING.] Scripture earlier¹ stated, *unto all the congregation…of Israel*, because the commandments, which followed, are obligatory upon all of Israel.² Strangers have no part in them.³ Scripture now begins to mention the punishment for harlotry, which will befall anyone who lives in the Land of Israel, be he native born⁴ or resident alien.⁵ It begins with the most severe of them all, namely, with the individual who gives of his seed to Molech, that is, the one who has intercourse with a woman who worships idols.⁶ 4:9: “If a man says *And thou shalt not give any of thy seed to set them apart to Molech* (Lev. 18:21) means, and thou shalt not give of thy seed to make it pass to heathendom, they put him to silence with a rebuke.”

¹ Lev. 19:2.
² That is, only upon Israel.
³ Non-Jews do not share these laws with Israel.
⁴ An Israelite.
⁵ A non-Jew living in Israel. Hence our chapter explicitly notes that what follows applies to both an Israelite and a non-Israelite.
⁶ This interpretation is rejected by the Mishnah. See Megillah

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 20:3:4

והיה נראה לנו כי טעם באבן שם המין כמו ויהי לי שור וחמור ודברי הקבלה נכונים והם אמת. ויאמר רבי יונה המדקדק הספרדי נ״ע כי פירוש ובמשפחתו הדומה אליו ומי הביאנו בצרה הזאת רק פירוש כמשמעו כי עם הארץ יעלימו עיניהם בעבור שהם ממשפחתו:


It would have appeared to us that *ba-even* (with stones)¹² (v. 2) is a collective noun.¹³ is to be rendered with stones. Compare, *And I have oxen* (shor),¹⁴ *and asses* (chamor)¹⁵ (Gen. 32:6).¹⁶ However, the words of tradition are correct.¹⁷ literally. According to the Midrash the culprit was first stoned by one stone. See *Sanhedrin* 6:4, “The place of stoning was twice the height of a man. One of the witnesses knocked him down…If he died that sufficed; but if not, the second witness took a stone and dropped it on his heart. If he died that sufficed; but if not, he was stoned by all Israel.” They are true. Rabbi Jonah the Spanish grammarian who rests in paradise says that *and against his family* (v. 5) means all those like him.¹⁸ Who brought us into this trouble?¹⁹ Our verse is to be taken literally. The people of the land²⁰ will hide their eyes because they are of his family.²¹

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 20:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/20:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/20:6:1)


**והנפש אשר תפנה אל האבת.** טעמו כאשר אכרית הנותן מזרעו למולך בסתר או בגלוי אם לא ימיתוהו עם הארץ כן אכרית הזונה מאחרי לפנות אל האובות ומצאנו נפשים גם כל נפש ארבעה עשר וכן והכרתי אותו:


AND THE SOUL THAT TURNETH UNTO THE GHOSTS. This means as I will cut off the one who gives from his seed to Molech in secret or in public if the people of the land do not kill him, so will I cut off the one who strays from me and turns to ghosts. We find the term *nefashim* (souls) (Ezek. 20:13) in Scripture.²² (souls) is masculine. *Nefesh* (soul) is usually feminine. However, our verse reads, *ve-hikhratti oto* (and will cut him [the soul] off). It thus treats *nefesh* as masculine. I.E. therefore points out that *nefesh* is sometimes treated as a masculine in Scripture. We also find *all the souls* (nefesh) *were fourteen* (arba’ah asar)²³ (fourteen) is masculine. Thus Gen. 46:22 treats *nefesh* as masculine. (Gen. 46:22). We similarly read,²⁴ *and will cut him*²⁵ (oto) *off*.

footnotes:
²² Nefashim
²³ Arba’ah asar
²⁴ In our verse.
²⁵ The soul.

**והתקדשתם כי אני ה׳‎ אלהיכם.** קדש ונתתי לכם חקת לשמרם כדי לקדשכם וכבר הזכיר זה הכתוב והטעם להכניס את הגרים התושבים עם ישראל שהם חייבים להיותם קדושים בעבור שידורו בארץ קדושה:


SANCTIFY YOURSELVES THEREFORE, AND BE YE HOLY; FOR I AM THE LORD YOUR GOD. *Ki ani Adonai Elohekhem* (for I am the Lord your God) means for I the Lord your God am holy. I have given you statutes to observe in order to sanctify you.²⁶ Scripture has already mentioned this.²⁷ It repeats this command so as to include the strangers residing among Israel, for they too are obligated to be holy so that they may continue to be allowed to dwell in a holy land.

והחל להזכיר עונש הכתובים בתחלת הפרשה מהאב כאשר החל איש אמו ואביו תיראו. וטעם להזכיר האב קודם האם בעבור כבודו ואיננו כמו איש אמו ואביו תיראו כי לא יומת אם לא היה בר מצוה:


Scripture begins the list of punishments at the beginning of the section²⁸. with the person who curses his father in the same manner that Scripture earlier starts with *Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father* (Lev. 19:3).²⁹ (Lev. 19:2). Our verse mentions the father before the mother out of respect for the father. It is unlike *Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father*,³⁰ for he is not put to death if he has not reached the age of *mitzvah* observance.³¹

footnotes:

FOR WHATSOEVER MAN THERE BE THAT CURSETH HIS FATHER OR HIS MOTHER SHALL SURELY BE PUT TO DEATH.³² The phrase *asher yekallel* (that curseth) is to be read as if written twice. Our verse is to be read as if written, “and whoever curses his mother.”³³ *He hath cursed his father or his mother* is another way of saying he has committed a great abomination.

**עונו ישא.** לבדו. וטעם להזכיר אלה הדברים באחות בעבור שגדלו יחד והם נערים משחקים וכל עת יתייחד עמה ולא הזכיר הכתוב עונש בת הבן או בת הבת כי סמך על תורה שבעל פה גם יתכן שלא הזכירם בעבור חוסר תאות האב כי הוא בא בימים הזמן שתהיה לו בת בוגרת ועל כן לא הזכיר הכתוב אם האב ואם האם כי הן זקנות:


HE SHALL BEAR HIS INIQUITY. He alone shall bear his iniquity. The reason scripture mentions these things⁵⁵ regarding the sister is that they grew up in one house and are young people who play. The brother is always alone with his sister. Scripture does not mention the punishment for intercourse with the daughter of one’s son or the daughter of one’s daughter, for it relied on the oral Torah.⁵⁶ 51a. It is possible that they are not mentioned because of the father’s lack of desire,⁵⁷ for he is advanced in years when he has a mature daughter. It is for this reason that Scripture does not mention the mother of one’s father and the mother of one’s mother, for they are aged.⁵⁸

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 20:19:1

Its meaning is, I have previously⁶⁰ warned you not to uncover the nakedness of thy mother’s sister.⁶¹ However, our verse reads, *And…the nakedness of thy mother’s sister…* Why the anomaly? Hence I.E.’s comment. Now the one who uncovers the nakedness⁶² has made naked his near kin.⁶³ is another way of saying he has committed a heinous act. See I.E. on verse 9.

### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 20:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/20:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/20:21:1)


ואמר על אשת אח **נדה** והטעם ראוי שירחק ממנה וכן אמרו אחיכ׳‎ שונאיכם מנדיכם והנה אין בעריות זכר נדה כי אם באשת אח והנדה אסורה גם תבוא עת להיות מותרת גם כן יתכן באשת האח כאשר אפרש בפרשת כי ישבו אחים יחדו ואשר אמרו כאשר היא אחות האב אסורה כן אסור לאשה שתנשא לדודה לא זה הדרך כי העריות הזכרים הם המכריחים ואין מי יכריחם ואם בדרך שקול דעתם החסרה יראה לנו למה לא נקבל עדות שתים נשים ואם על הערכים תהיינה ארבעת נשים כמו שני עדים על כן אנחנו צריכים לקבלה:


[IT IS IMPURITY.] Scripture employs the term *niddah* (impurity) with regard to a brother’s wife. The meaning of *niddah hiy* (it is impurity)⁷³, she is distanced. The term *niddah* usually refers to a menstruating women. is, it is fitting for him to distance himself from her.⁷⁴ comes from the root *nun, dalet, dalet*, which means to wander. Similarly, *Your brethren that hate you, that cast you out* (menaddekhem)…*have said* (Is. 66:5).⁷⁵, which is related to the word *niddah*, has the meaning of to distance. Note, there is no mention of *niddah* in all of the prohibited sexual partners⁷⁶. except with regard to a brother’s wife. A *niddah*⁷⁷ is prohibited.⁷⁸ However, a time comes when she is permitted.⁷⁹, and they immerse themselves seven days after the cessation of their menstrual flow, with 12 days being the minimum. This possibility,⁸⁰ as I will explain in the section *If brethren dwell together* (Deut. 25:5), also arises in the case of a brother’s wife. My reply to those who say,⁸¹ as it is prohibited to marry the sister of the father (v. 19) so it is prohibited for a woman to marry her uncle⁸² is: this is not the way of Scripture.⁸³ It is the males who are dominant⁸⁴ (your husband) *shall rule over thee*. with regard to the prohibited sexual practices.⁸⁵ No one dominates the male.⁸⁶ Let those who accept the faulty logic of those who offer the above interpretation⁸⁷ show us why we should not accept the testimony of two women.⁸⁸ If they⁸⁹ argue from the laws of evaluation⁹⁰ then four women should be equal to two male witnesses. We therefore need tradition.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/20:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/20:27:1)


וטעם **ואיש או אשה.** בעבור שאמר על האובות לטמאה בהם אמר היו קדושים והמיתו אשר יטמא נפשו באוב ובידעוני כי עד כה לא הזכיר עונש פונה אל אוב בפרהסיא. וטעם להזכיר האשה כי זאת האומנות ביד הנשים יותר וכן מכשפה לא תחיה:


[A MAN ALSO OR A WOMAN.] The reason Scripture states *A man also or a woman that divineth by a ghost or a familiar spirit, shall surely be put to death* is that the Torah earlier had said concerning ghosts and familiar spirits, *seek them not out to be defiled by them* (Lev. 19:31). Scripture now says, be holy and put to death the one who defiles himself with a ghost or a familiar spirit. Previously it did not mention the punishment for publicly turning to a ghost. Scripture mentions *woman*, for this art is mostly practiced by women. Similarly, *Thou shalt not suffer a sorceress to live* (Ex. 22:17).¹⁰²

footnotes:
¹⁰² Scripture mention a sorceress because women practice sorcery more than men. See I.E. on Ex. 22:17 (Vol. 2, p. 487).

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 21:2:1

**כי אם לשארו הקרוב אליו.** היה נראה לנו כי פירושו כמו איש איש אל כל שאר בשרו שם כלל ואחר כן פרט לאמו ולאביו:


EXCEPT FOR HIS KIN. It had appeared to us that the meaning of *she’ero* (His kin) is similar to *she’er* (near of kin) in *None of you…to any that is near of kin to him* (Lev. 18:6). In other words, *she’ero* is a general term,¹⁰ with the details *for his mother, and for his father* following.

###### Ibn Ezra on Leviticus 21:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/21:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Leviticus/r/21:2:2)


וטעם **בעל בעמיו.** שלא יטמא הבעל באשתו וכאשר ראינו שהעתיקו רבותינו כי יטמא לאשתו ושמו לשארו כדרך אסמכתא כאשר פירשתי במלת לעם נכרי ואמרו כי פירוש בעל גדול שהעם ברשותו כמו בעליו אין עמו בטל הפירוש הראשון. וטעם להזכיר אמו קודם האב כי הזכר חי יותר מהנקבה ברוב:


The meaning of *ba’al be-amav* (a chief man among his people) (v. 4) is that a husband¹¹. shall not defile himself for his wife. However, since we saw that our teachers transmitted to us the law that a *kohen* is permitted to defile himself for his wife,¹² 22b. the first interpretation falls away. They employed the word *she’er* as a support,¹³ (his kin) literally means his flesh. According to the rabbis the reference is to a wife. The sages render *ki im le-she’ero* (except for his kin), except for his wife. According to I.E. the plain meaning of *she’ero* is not his wife. He believes that the rabbis used this verse as a support for a law which they knew by tradition. as I explained in my comments on the phrase *unto a foreign people* (Ex. 21:8).¹⁴ means to any stranger. According to I.E. this is not the literal meaning of this phrase. The rabbis merely used this verse as a support. See I.E. on Ex. 21:8 (Vol. 2, pp. 458,459). The rabbis said that the meaning of *ba’al* is, a chief who rules over the people, as in *the owner thereof* (be-alav) *not being with it* (Ex. 22:13).¹⁵ (He shall not defile himself, being a chief man among his people) is: “Seeing that he is fit to become the highest and most honored one among his people [i.e., a high priest], it (Scripture) warns him not to profane his distinction with the impurity of the dead” (Nachmanides, Chavel translation). The reason Scripture mentions the mother of the *kohen* before the father is that in most cases the male lives longer than the female.¹⁶ will mourn for his mother before he does so for his father. Hence she is mentioned first.
